items.body: Jonáš Gruska‘s Juggler / ジャグラ does more than what it says on the tin. Originally assembled from covert recordings made inside an Akihabara pachinko parlour, the album documented a moment of revelation: Gruska discovering that beneath the assaultive barrage of gambling machines lay an accidental drone, a strange and unexpectedly serene harmony emerging from repetition, excess and addiction. Following copyright challenges from the manufacturer of the machines, the album was substantially reworked and reissued in 2026. Rather than diminishing the project, the transformation has deepened it. The revised version feels less literal, less claustrophobic and more dreamlike than the original. The opening “Juggler / ジャグラー (Resonant Remix)” drifts into ethereal ambient territory, extracting resonances from the source material. The album also sees the contribution of a number of different artists, each taking the original material into unexpected directions. Lénok, for instance, delivers an incantatory lullaby with “Tokyo dr4ft”, while MSHR subjects the recordings to a kind of sonic spin cycle, reducing them to hiss, gurgles and crumpled textures that hover at the edge of recognisability on “Juggler with Fourteen Balls.” The most direct connection to Akihabara arrives from Takako Minekawa, who situates the material within the district’s layered history of electronics, retro-futurism and hidden urban spaces with “ガラス管の向こう側は秋葉原の路地裏” (“Beyond the Glass Tube is a Back Alley in Akihabara”). It is perhaps the album’s clearest glimpse of the pachinko parlour culture. By contrast, bod [包家巷] “gambling” introduces unexpected elegiac notes onto cascading electronics with “gambling”. The closing track “sculpture 01: 2024/10/28 pachinko parlor UNO, Akihabara, Tokyo” from mw encapsulates the album’s central tension. After extended passages of glitches, loops and abstraction, the untreated pachinko recordings gradually emerge from beneath the processing, as if reality were slowly resurfacing through layers of interpretation. It is a remarkably effective gesture that reframes the entire album. What makes Juggler so fascinating is that the copyright dispute became part of the artwork rather than an obstacle to it. The reissue shifts the focus away from the machines themselves and towards the perception of them: not gambling technology, but accidental composition; not documentation, but listening. In doing so, Juggler raises intriguing questions about field recording, authorship and ownership while remaining, above all, a deeply immersive and surprisingly beautiful record. Helping us to make sense of the album Jonáš Gruska answered a few questions for us. Photo by Ester Mládenková Juggler began as a covert act of field recording inside a pachinko parlor in Akihabara, a space where recording is effectively forbidden. Did the “illegality” of the act itself become part of the conceptual framework of the album? Yes, the sensation of constantly being monitored by the employees of the parlor was a part of the experience. Basically, it felt like the only allowed action was to spend money. Sitting, observing, and listening on its own is suspicious and quickly grabs unwanted attention. the guests of the establishment, of course, didn’t care, the machines are extremely loud and captivating, so one does completely immerse oneself. One of the most striking aspects of the record is your description of hearing dozens of identical machines unexpectedly merge into a kind of drone composition. What was it about that experience that transformed what could be perceived as noise, advertising, and gambling stimuli into something almost meditative or transcendent? I believe ever since I started working with drone and ambient music, I became sensitive to „accidental“ drones in our environment. Hums, purrs, and buzzes of machines in the city can be very calming and harmonizing. I often found myself just appreciating electrical transformers and their calm 50/60 Hz buzz. This was a similar sensation, hearing beyond the individual effects of the machines and appreciating the deeper harmony of the emitted sounds. This was only possible when the parlor arranged the same machines in multiple rows and I actually had to look for this specific situation for a while. In June 2026, Juggler was reissued in a substantially altered form following copyright and rights-related concerns around the source material. Can you explain what happened, and how you navigated the tension between field recording, authorship, intellectual property, and the reality that these sounds were already part of a heavily controlled commercial environment? I was approached by the company that creates these machines and after some explanations on both sides I decided to recreate the original work to comply with their request. I originally argued about the ambient field recording practice, but in the end decided to see the request as a creative challenge and an inspiring piece of the story. The new edition is described as treating those legal and copyright constraints as part of the artwork itself, both sonically and visually. How did the reissue differ from the original version, and did being forced to rework the material ultimately change your understanding of the project or reveal possibilities you had not considered before? I was not forced to rework it. But the only other option was pulling the release completely. I felt like that perhaps the point of the recording was not the sound effects themselves, but the overall harmony that is present in that situation. So I extracted the most dominant frequencies and used algorithmic composition practice to rework the recording into “resonant edit”. This is slightly inspired by Alvin Lucier’s classic piece I am sitting in a room, but without the room—using just the track itself as the source of resonances. The title *Juggler* evokes both the famous pachinko machine series and the act of keeping multiple elements in motion at once. Looking back now, the album seems to juggle memory, addiction, childhood impressions, urban soundscape, field recording practice, legal restrictions, and artistic transformation. Do you see the reissued version as the definitive statement of the work, or as another stage in an ongoing process of reinterpretation? I would add one more layer to your interpretation — the remixing parties involved are also my fellow “jugglers” handling the recording in their own art-practice-hands. Some of them even feel like a circus experience. The new rework offers a bit of dynamic in a classically “fixed” medium, which I never did before but surprisingly enjoy. It makes me rethink the idea of static releases that will forever remain the same. You have devoted a significant part of your artistic practice to field recording, often approaching it as a way of documenting and listening to the world as it is. Juggler seems to complicate that idea: the recordings are made covertly, the source material is highly mediated and commercial, and the project itself was later reshaped by copyright concerns. Did this experience change your understanding of what a field recording can be? Has it altered the way you think about authorship, documentation, or the relationship between capturing reality and transforming it into art? To be honest, I never expected such an obscure project to grab so much attention. My field recording albums were never as popular as my music, so this caught me slightly off guard. But I received a huge amount of positive feedback from random people online, people that don’t even normally listen to field recordings. So there is something about this type of work that can transcend my usual audience and that is very inspiring. (Gianmarco Del Re)

items._cn_summary: 斯洛伐克声音艺术家Jonáš Gruska的《Juggler / ジャグラ》源自东京秋叶原弹珠机店的秘密录音，在遭遇版权诉讼后被深度重制再版。专辑将赌博机器的噪声转化为偶然生成的drone与和声，多位艺术家参与remix，将原始素材推向不同方向：有的走向空灵氛围，有的拆解为嘶嘶声与褶皱纹理，有的将声音置于秋叶原电子文化的历史脉络中。结尾曲中未经处理的弹珠机录音从层层电子处理中浮现，仿佛现实透过阐释的表层重新显形。版权争议本身成为作品的一部分，专辑从对机器的记录转向对聆听本身的追问，涉及田野录音、作者权与所有权的深层议题，是一张沉浸且出人意料地美丽的专辑。

items.body:
Alex Zhang Hungtai pivots yet again on 'Orion/Mother', playing (mostly) trumpet alongside some of the New York City underground scene's most intriguing improvisers, including Kwami Winfield, Laura Cocks, Lester St. Louis, TAK Ensemble's Madison Greenstone, 75 Dollar Bill's Che Chen and Leo Chang.

 'Orion/Mother' has its roots in a set of home recordings Zhang made with some of his talented local friends; "playing with you all deeply informed my current understanding in improvisation," he explains in his thank you note, "without you this album would not have existed." So over a two week period, in a rehearsal space in New York, he invited a handful of his friends to start "an ad-hoc group", playing trumpet over chopped up home recordings and wrenching them into the future. And while the finished article - split into two distinct sections - is long, it's fully worthy of your attention. As always, Zhang brings a unique ear into the room, resisting any usual improv tropes to concentrate on sounds that most artists would avoid - unruly resonances, glitches, off-piste rhythms and unsubtle interferences.

At it's best, the record sounds like jazz specters vanishing thru faded noise remnants and the wreckage of lost experiments. On 'Shadow Integration', Zhang's brassy wails echo out over a slippery, semi-rhythmic drum machine pattern, and on 'Tanhäuser Gate', the trumpet is even more isolated, weeping over a muted soundscape that's credited simply as "Ableton" on the accompanying notes. He maintains the same energy when he's working side-by-side with his collaborators, too, finding space for Winfield's circuit bent belches on 'Nataraja' and Chen and Chang's percussion on the jaw-droppingly spannered opener 'Sidewinder'. And even when the tone shifts on 'Mother', heading into a lighter (comparatively at least) zone on the woodwind-heavy 'Kali', Zhang has a knack for tying everything together with his lyrical performance. Just peep the title track, almost seven minutes of uncanny clanks and Tōru Takemitsu-strength murmurs that Zhang butters with pure improvised emotion.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于张颂泰在纽约与多位地下即兴乐手的合奏，以小号为核心，叠加被切割重组的家庭录音与电子声响。他有意回避常见的即兴套路，转而聚焦于不羁的共振、失灵的节奏与粗暴的干扰——铜管的哀鸣漂浮在滑动的鼓机纹理之上，或在标注为'Ableton'的静默音景中孤鸣。两周内拼凑而成的即兴团体在粗粝的开篇曲中碰撞出惊人的火花，木管主导的段落则提供了相对轻盈的对照。终曲近七分钟的不协和金属碰撞与低语，被他即兴演奏的情感洪流所包裹，呈现出幽灵般的爵士残影穿过实验废墟的听感。

items.body:
Playing the kacapi, a Sundanese box zither, XKatedral alumnus Svennson leads a trio with violinist Maya Bennardo and bass clarinet player Erik Blennow Caläv on 'For a Lemon Tree', meditating on pitch and negative space.

Made up of two long pieces, the album highlights not just Svennson's writing, but the trio's interplay. The initial, title track is a fully notated piece that emerged from their improvisations; it's reined in, in many ways, condensed but still featuring the tonal experimentation that defines their experimentation. Working in 11-limit Just Intonation tuning, the trio work in tiny gestures - Svennson's kacapi plucks are most evident at the beginning, but the sounds that croak from Caläv's clarinet and Bennardo's violin are just as beguiling.

And as impressive as that short-form track is, the lengthy 'Improvisation on Prakāśa' takes it to another level. As the title suggests, this one's fully improvised and illustrates the relationship the players have with each other. It's chilling stuff that doesn't reveal itself straight away; Svennson's kacapi sounds almost medieval at times, while Bennardo creates toneless, whooshing textures that transport us to another dimension entirely.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由卡卡比琴演奏者斯文森、小提琴手贝纳多与低音单簧管演奏者卡莱夫三位音乐家合作完成，围绕音高与负空间展开沉思。前半部分为完整记谱的标题曲，从即兴中提炼而出，以十一限纯律音准体系工作，演奏者以极简的声响手势彼此呼应——卡卡比的拨弦、低音单簧管的嘶哑声线与小提琴的无调性质感共同构建出凝练而克制的声响画面。后半部分的长篇即兴《Improvisation on Prakāśa》将三人的默契推向极致，斯文森的卡卡比呈现出近似中世纪鲁特琴的质感，贝纳多制造出无调性的气流纹理，将听者带入另一个维度的听觉空间。整张专辑将巽他传统乐器置于当代即兴与微分音作曲语境中，跨越文化与流派的边界，在微小声响中探索深层聆听的可能性。

items.body:
Ghost Dubs & The Bug duppy the latter’s cult, isolationist ambient excursion of 2022 with apposite measures of lead-boot trod and atmospheric levity for the hardest-to-please industrial dub freaks.

Selected cuts from ’Sub Zero’ - Kevin Richard Martin’s concerted return to interests in ambient-dub-noise fundamentals - are robustly togged out with bass insulation and Goretextured to the elements for a supremely crushing session that benefits from the biggest speakers you can lay yr mitts on. It catches KRM arguably in his imperial phase, sustaining a tear of substantial gear penned under his own name since ‘Sirens’ (Room 40, 2019) deep into the belly of his sound, to now clasp these chiral aspects of his steez - the supine, sunken, and strongback, stepping - in a deathly bind.

KMR’s key spar and Pressure MVP, Ghost Dubs goes super dank and wide on his half, opening subterranean caverns of space below ‘When I’m Gone’, punctuated only by abandoned ice-breaker clank and timber-shiver chorales, before pushing leagues below into knackered Porter Ricks or Rhythm & Sound terrain on rework of ‘Sorrow’. Martin keeps up his end of the bargain with a sonorous diffusion of ‘Screwed’, all icy plangency and keeling bass recalling aspects of Mika Vainio’s ‘Kilo’, then plumbing guttural crevasses of the spirit on remix of ‘Too Human’.
items._genre: ambient dub / industrial / dark ambient / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Kevin Richard Martin 2022年氛围-低音-噪音作品的混音再制版本，由The Bug和Ghost Dubs分别操刀。Ghost Dubs以极度低沉宽阔的手法重新塑造空间感，在冰层断裂的金属敲击与木制合唱的废墟声响中开凿地下洞穴，将原作推向Porter Ricks与Rhythm & Sound式的深邃领域。The Bug部分则以冰冽的金属质感和沉重的低音扩散进行声学重塑，呼应Mika Vainio式的冰冷张力，并向更幽暗的精神裂隙深入。两位混音者各自延续了原专辑的孤立主义氛围基调，但以更工业化的力度和更宽广的低频处理增强了压迫感与沉浸度。整体呈现出克制而凶猛的声响美学，适合在大功率音响系统中完整感受其物理层面的冲击力。

items.body:
Xiu Xiu reprise their Lynch reverence with a suitably bleak, beguiling take on the ‘Eraserhead’ score, nearly a decade after their ‘Twin Peaks’ homage became a surprise hit. The inimitable ‘70s flick’s industrial imagery and concrète score, arranged by Lynch with Alan Splet, prompts Jamie Stewart and co. to some truly discomfiting yet enigmatic work that arguably lives up to the legendary director’s vision.

"In 2016, with the blessing of David Lynch and Angelo Badalamenti, Xiu Xiu released and toured the surprisingly successful album and concert, Plays the Music of Twin Peaks. Out of respect and deference to the beloved series, the band decided to put the concert to rest in 2018. 

After the recent and untimely passing of David Lynch, Xiu Xiu began to receive several high-profile requests to revive their interpretation of this iconic music. However, in wanting to always try to follow, honor, and continue to be inspired by the incredibly high bar of artistic challenge set by Lynch, Xiu Xiu is instead going deeper. 

The album itself is a masterpiece in sound collage and experimentation, with tracks like “Tetra” and “Sleep Synth” shifting from minimal auditory sensations to a clobbering, grotesque cacophony. The album’s closing track, “In Heaven,” is a beautiful rendition of Peter Ivers’ original composition, with Stewart’s delicate and soft vocals showcasing the elegance and wonder found in Lynch’s directorial debut, Eraserhead. 

Eraserhead’s original sound design and score by Alan Splet and Lynch guide Xiu Xiu’s expanded interpretation, reflecting their influence as fans and musicians. The original film gives birth to Xiu Xiu’s visual lens, through which audiences are baffled and pummeled by the band’s imaginary unused auxiliary footage. 

Is it a short-term art installation, an exploded tribute to a cinematic triumph, an epitaph to an idol via an entirely new work? Yes. Is it intense, odd, curious, and shrouded in the gloomiest of nights? Of course. 

After all, it is Eraserhead."
items._genre: experimental / industrial / sound collage / dark ambient / avant-garde
items._cn_summary: Xiu Xiu 以2016年Twin Peaks致敬专辑的成功为前奏，在David Lynch辞世后选择深入其处女作《Eraserhead》的声音世界，向Alan Splet与Lynch共同构建的工业声响与具体音乐致敬。专辑以声音拼贴与实验为核心手法，曲目从极简听觉感知突变为沉重而怪异的噪音洪流，Jamie Stewart在终曲中以轻柔人声重绎Peter Ivers原作，呼应影片中优雅与不安交织的气质。乐评将其视为艺术装置、电影致敬与挽歌的多重叠加，认为它在Lynch设定的极高艺术标准下做出了延续与突破。整张作品既是粉丝视角的延伸，也是独立于原作的全新创作，笼罩在Eraserhead式的晦暗夜色之中。

items.body:
Michael J. Blood executes a stunning volte-face from rugged house and soul to more intuitive, introspective, world-building ambient jazz and electroacoustic dub realms under a new moniker SEES, signifying a newfound psychoactive frisson to his work that lands him somewhere in the spiritual vicinity of Vangelis, Moodymann, Ron Trent, Pendant, Terre Thaemlitz.

‘Ampersand Curve’ initiates a brilliant new phase of work by North Manchester’s most elusive artist, best known as Michael J. Blood. His string of ruffkut club bangers as well as jams with Rat Heart & Samizdat over the past seven years, have made his records a true cult property, and now find him signed to one of the UK’s most foundational techno imprints - more of which later this year.

But under the SEES aegis, he swims in very different waters, following his instincts to use the studio-as-instrument to produce his most impressive, deep-minded work, made from - and for - the heart. Where MJB was all about off-the-cuff club jams cooked for immediacy, his new stylistic switch reveals myriad worlds of influence swirling under the hood, where interrelated spheres of spiritual jazz, dub, ambient and concrète more clearly light up his rich inner world.

As the story goes, MJB was burgled a few years back, and lost most of his studio just as the project was hitting its stride. It prompted a personal review of his practice, re-learning new kit, allowing him to bend the rules. Adopting a sort of first thought, best thought approach to composition, the new methodology fuelled a renewed imagination in flux, or what he identifies as SEES: a personalised way of conveying complex emotions.

That un-doing of musical and mental conditioning opens the walls of his music to vast new horizons. Opener ‘Ithaca’ fathoms sonorous midnight jazz with 10 mins of a plangent, searching sax solo in HD widescreen, like some alternate version to the Blade Runner Love Theme, while a resonant vocoder soliloquy ‘Unseem’ reaches into space harmonised between Alvin Lucier and Ron Trent, and ‘Sheer’ chases the devil out of labyrinthine dub dimensions. The floating dream architecture of ‘Caprices’ caps the LP’s underlying narrative and painterly qualities with a romantic conclusion of blushing pads and shivered, metallic echoes of the subtropical that suggest a coming-to-terms with worries, refreshed and good to go again.

A huge, heartfelt tip for a 2026 stunner.
items._genre: ambient jazz / electroacoustic dub / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 北曼彻斯特音乐人Michael J. Blood启用新身份SEES，完成了从粗粝浩室灵魂乐向内省氛围爵士与电子声学dub领域的彻底转向。一次入室盗窃让他失去大部分设备，迫使他重新审视创作方式，以「第一念即为最佳」的即兴方法重构录音流程。新作中的萨克斯独白在深夜般的音色空间中展开长篇探索，vocoder独白在Alvin Lucier与Ron Trent的谐振区间里延展，dub轨道则向迷宫般的纵深处推进。他将录音棚本身视为乐器，融合灵性爵士、氛围、具体音乐与声学实验等多重脉络。专辑由英国某老牌techno厂牌发行，标志着他从俱乐部制作人转型为以内心世界为素材的作曲者。

items.body:
Hamburg’s post-punk goth wraiths play the hits for John Peel, slinging cuts sifted from their four sessions recorded 1982-1985, including tearing renditions of ‘Incubus Succubus’ and ‘Qual’, a thunderous ‘Sehnsucht’, the very Cocteaus-esque ‘Polarlicht’, and tortured romance of ‘Autumn’

"You only need listen to the soul-devouring nocturnal visitation of Incubus Succubus, or the obliterating fury of Qual (“Meine Wiege ist deine Grab” – “my cradle is your grave”) to see that underestimating Xmal Deutschland was never a good idea. When the Hamburg band first walked into the BBC’s Maida Vale Studio in November 1982 to record their debut session for John Peel, it was natural they should feel a flash of awe as they were ushered through the labyrinthine building, on the brink of joining a radio lineage that included The Fall, David Bowie, Siouxsie And The Banshees and The Cure. Yet the band – at that point singer Anja Huwe, keyboardist Fiona Sangster, guitarist Manuela Rickers, drummer Manuela Zwingmann and bassist Wolfgang Ellerbrock – also quickly picked up on the old-school energy and hierarchies of the place, the entrenched divisions between tea ladies and the producers and sound engineers, the tensions between the old-school male rock’n’roll way of doing things and their band’s place in the modern world.

John Peel rarely came to the studio to meet the bands he had selected for the honour of a Peel Session, having no interest in pressing the showbiz flesh (For Lulu or otherwise). Instead, as Sangster recalls, Xmal Deutschland immediately found themselves up against producers and engineers who, regardless of the blessing inherent in Peel’s invitation, weren’t terribly impressed with the sight of this female-majority German band. “They communicated quite clearly that they didn’t think you were very good, that they didn’t like the music, and would you please hurry up,” says Sangster, bristling at the memory 43 years later.

Yet Xmal Deutschland had – in the jaded language of the old-fashioned male-dominated music industry – very much paid their dues by the time they arrived at Maida Vale. They formed in Hamburg in 1980 – “a tough city,” says singer Anja Huwe, a significantly grittier place than the artier musical enclaves of Cologne or Dusseldorf. They had endured – and thrived – in their canal-side rehearsal studio, against all the health-and-safety odds. The punks next-door had soundproofed their space with egg boxes; when somebody dropped a cigarette, the solvent went up in flames. “All dirty carpets and grotty sofas,” recalls Sangster. “It was filthy, it was damp, it was cold.” Zwingmann, meanwhile, recalls the dangerous swerving of their VW van as they raced for late-night ferries, burdened with equipment.

They had shown their own grit, too, by making the decision early on that they were not going to be channelled into the Neue Deutsche Welle, then a buzzword for young German bands. “If we’d stayed in Hamburg and gone down that path, our career would have been over in a year,” explains Huwe. “Because it was a very short-lived movement.” After releasing their first two singles on Hamburg imprint ZickZack, in 1983 they found the label that could match their questing, independent energy. “We recorded a tape in the rehearsal room and we took it to 4AD,” recalls Sangster. “We didn’t go anywhere else.” Fetish, their debut album for the label, followed. Like formidable, backcombed Groucho Marxes, they never wanted to belong to any club that would want them as a member. “We just didn’t want to give them the obvious sort of thing, and we always kept our distance from everyone,” says Huwe. “We were like a group on our own. We never went to a place like the Batcave – and they always invited us. Everyone wanted us to join, but we never went there because we were not interested. We went to exhibitions, we wrote books, saw films – you know, enjoyed our own company.”

This record, a fabulous chronological document of the four Peel sessions they recorded between November 1982 (five months before the release of their 1983 debut album Fetisch) and May 1985, is the sound of a band who knew the power of that company and who ultimately refused to be intimidated by the gruffly condescending gatekeepers of Maida Vale. They found a strength in defying their old-school attitudes. “We benefited from that because we sort of got into ‘fuck you’ mode”, says Sangster, much to Huwe and Zwingmann’s delight. “That might be part of the energy that you’re hearing.”

It’s an energy that transmits with a piercing clarity in these sixteen tracks, the constraints of time and space giving what Sangster calls “a certain urgency” to these sessions. “Listening back, you can tell it’s sort of like a hybrid between a live performance and a studio performance,” she says. “These are different versions, which is what makes them interesting.”

As Huwe and Sangster stress, a Peel session wasn’t the time for Xmal Deutschland to experiment – “you would choose one of the bangers!” they laugh. That’s clear from the opening full-pelt Incubus Succubus, its supernatural vortex immediately transporting the listener right into the room, to the dreamy expanses of closing track Autumn (from May 1985), their first song in English. In between arcs the remarkable career of a band in constant motion: “It’s a really interesting snapshot, as it were, of our evolution, these four Peel Sessions all together,” says Sangster. “You can see how we grew as a band.” It’s there in untethered experimentalism and proto-Mandinka howls of Reigen, from their second album Tocsin, or the new expansiveness that comes with Nachtschatten’s twinkling synths (not a million miles away from The Cure’s pop experiments) or the gorgeous melody of Der Wind. Here are the fierce hexes of their early work – the angel-devil showdown of Geheimnis, Qual’s scything B-side Sehnsucht, the tribal skitter of In Motion – mutating into a different kind of spellbinding. The studio atmosphere might have been oppressive, but this collection of Peel Sessions shows a band making the space their own. “It was so different compared to how we lived, because it was British, very conservative,” says Huwe. “But we jumped in there.” With this compilation, you can hear the ripples Xmal Deutschland made then still powerfully resonating down the years."
items._cn_summary: 本文评介Xmal Deutschland在1982至1985年间为BBC著名主持人John Peel录制的四次电台session合集。来自汉堡的这支以女性为主导阵容的后朋克哥特乐队，以阴冷而暴烈的声响闻名，曲目包括撕裂般的《Incubus Succubus》《Qual》以及哥特氛围浓厚的《Sehnsucht》《Polarlicht》等。文章不仅梳理了乐队在Maida Vale录音室面对偏见与男性主导的旧式行业秩序时的经历，还回溯了他们在汉堡运河边排练室中艰辛成型的过程，以及主动拒绝被归入新德意志浪潮的清醒定位。乐评文字扎实，兼具历史语境与音乐描写，揭示了这支乐队在德国后朋克版图中长期被低估的艺术价值。

items.body:
The jittery pulses and waking dream-like atmospheres of Dx2ov land on London’s Blank Mind for an album strafing between cut-up sound poetry and whisked garage-house.

“Dx2ov arrives on Blank Mind with Tonegues, his second vinyl LP following on from Interzona on Gost Zvuk in 2024. The LP title is a wordplay on the idea of speaking in tongues and sonic tonalities, echoing the process and dialogue that went into creating the record. Taken from a vast archive of material from 2019-2025, these ideas were arranged with the collaboration of label owner Sam Purcell and then completed with the long-distance assistance of Toupaz.

Tonegues is best seen through the lens of a beat-tape, with the playful flow and variety that the format provides, bursting with oddball ideas and punctuated with intangible vocal samples. Much like the LP’s beguiling, hand-drawn artwork by Wolfgang Matuschek, it is a glimpse into an inner world, a portal to somewhere uncanny and strange borne through imagination.

Light dub flourishes mix with footwork/IDM hybrids and understated, melancholic synthesis on ‘2018’, whilst the loose, rhythmic march of ‘Fon32’ evokes the dusty beatdown styles of early 2000s Detroit downtempo records. Whilst on one of the LP highlights ‘Trout’ he lays down a gleefully strange bed for the surrealist storytelling of Jacob Dwyer about interactions with dogs, dripping old houses and a perennial wish for the phone to ring with a heavy dub poetry slant. Dx2ov swiftly moves through more footwork adjacent, almost bedroom hyper-pop territories with a penchant for gabber kicks on ‘No Strings (feat DJ Paprika)’ and the maximalism of album closer 'Demetch' which continues in the tradition of wonky, mid-2010s UK bass music flips. The outcome is a confounding, unorthodox piece of work, zigzagging between forms, textures and moods.”
items._genre: experimental electronic / IDM / footwork / dub / bass music
items._cn_summary: Tonegues（Dx2ov）的第二张黑胶专辑在伦敦地下厂牌Blank Mind发行，素材取自2019至2025年间积累的庞大档案，由厂牌主理人Sam Purcell协助编排、远在异地的Toupaz参与远程协作完成。整张专辑以beat-tape的形式展开，节奏松散而充满即兴感，碎片化的声音诗歌与车库舞曲节拍交错推进。曲目横跨轻盈的dub点缀、footwork与IDM的混合体、2000年代初底特律downtempo的颗粒质感，以及卧室hyper-pop和2010年代中期wobbly英伦bass的回响。专辑亮点'Trout'邀请Jacob Dwyer进行怪诞叙事朗读，主题围绕与狗的互动、破旧房屋和对电话响起的执念，呈现出浓郁的dub poetry质感。封套由Wolfgang Matuschek手绘完成，与音乐共同构筑出一个陌生而内向的想象世界。整体而言，这是一张在形式、质感与情绪间不断跳跃的非正统之作。

items.body:
Absolutely filthy/screwed club gunk  and no-wave machine music from Murray Collier (Grim Lusk, Dip Friso) & Conal Blake (Feedback Moves, Domestic Exile), working together as Inweys and highly tipped FFO Actress, MMM, Wino, V/Vm's 'Machine Component' series...

“Inweys debut release arrives as four pieces of broken body music. Lurking, barely human fragments brought into the present. Using a short drum-machine improvisation as core material, the pieces are formed from a processes of mining and re-mining for small details, with each fragment zoomed in on and turned into new pieces. There’s a transformation taking place, but one that doesn’t obscure the materiality of the recording tapes as sticky, corrosive matter. On skewed and stretched fabric they enact their palimpsestic play, sketching and altering the grid with itchy technologies. What their edits and improvisations don’t say they let space say the rest, with vacuum aerated frames for bass to diffuse and beats to wriggle. More King Tubby than Cage, more Mantronix than Reich: minimalism with molten tips.

Both Conal and Murray’s past work has embraced malleable and iterative technologies; music whose feeliness figures itself out in space in a messy precomposed/improvised dialectic. This is the sort of thing most “new music” experimentalists (or anyone who spends most of their time obsessively manipulating tapes in expensive studios) often can’t achieve; a liveness, birthed from learning in situated play. Like the lore of Phuture’s Acid Trax, a poverty of material is at the heart of this, rendering the work with an abortive conviction: a corpse waking to consciousness becomes amphibious. Instead of the composer we have a relation, two people navigating the awkward spooling between the two reels of tape. Inweys is scots for “inwards”, and in their working process this is what they do. But the result is circular motion. Until the tape runs out, all in ways move out”. "

Fielding Hope.
items._genre: experimental electronic / broken beat / no-wave / tape music
items._cn_summary: Inweys的首张专辑由Murray Collier与Conal Blake合作完成，以短小鼓机即兴为核心素材，通过反复挖掘、放大局部细节来重构片段，呈现出破碎、肮脏、近乎非人化的俱乐部声响与磁带物质性。整张作品强调制作过程中的“在场感”与即兴张力，将磁带编辑与现场操作并置，声音在不同轨道间持续扭曲、拉伸、叠加，留白与低频扩散构成空间骨架。乐评将其与King Tubby的混音美学、Cage的简约立场、Mantronix的电子质感并列，指出其核心在于以极简材料达成高密度的转化与矛盾感。两位艺术家过往的独立项目均聚焦于可变与迭代式的技术运用，此次合作以苏格兰方言“Inweys”（向内）为名，将创作过程指向内向挖掘，但结果呈现为循环运动式的声响螺旋。

items.body:
London-based Malaysian-Australian composer and professor Silvia Lim prioritises close listening on 'Flare', writing quiet, minimal patterns that draw attention to unusual textures and bewitching dissonances.

Having bounced between Malaysia, Australia and the UK growing up, Lim is fascinated by the idea of instability and how that might be represented sonically. She explores a certain kind of fragility on 'Flare', working with the flimsiness of timbre by zooming in to capture the most incidental sounds - the scraping of a slowly pulled bow on the strings or the softness of air blown through a bass clarinet's reed. On the two-part composition 'Grafting', Lim folds in unexpectedly beautiful melodies, letting them grind to a halt completely, or disappear into faint traces beneath resonant ghost notes and stifled wails. There's a trace of folk music in there, buried in the undergrowth. 

And on the four-part 'Field of Play', Lim prepares her instruments with a single tool each time: a hair clip, a bobby pin and piece of cork, presenting the pieces as proof of what sonic shifts these seemingly light preparations might cause. On 'contact', the bobby pin disintegrates the instrumentation, turning the strings into lightly boiling, echoing resonances and on 'hidden place', it's even more disorienting, sounding as if the cello is being lowered slowly into a vast metallic chamber.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以极简手法探索声音的脆弱性与不稳定性。作曲家通过放大弓弦摩擦、气流通过簧片等细微声响，将日常演奏中被忽视的质地与音色凸显出来。两段式作品《Grafting》中，旋律在意外出现后又骤然停滞，消融于残响与幽灵般的泛音之下，隐约可辨的民歌元素隐匿于层次深处。四段式《Field of Play》每首仅用单一物件改造乐器——发夹、弹簧夹、软木塞——却引发出截然不同的声学变化：从沸腾般的弦乐共振到仿佛大提琴被缓缓沉入金属腔体的迷幻空间。整体呈现出对器乐声学边界的细致探索，是当代作曲中注重听觉实验与声音物质性的代表作品。

items.body:
5 Gate Temple’s high priest John T. Gast turns in 13 mystic trodders and pulse meditations on his first album, proper, dedicated to this style since 2019. Proper fantasy free party x soundsystem tekkerz, for transcendent club pressure.

As torch carrier of a mutant ’90s rave spirit since the early 2010’s, John T. Gast has opened up the cruddiest wormhole between formative Cornish raves and community centre dances. On ‘Infant’ he goes head down, feet first in a particularly briny, rinsed-out style of steppers livicating the enduring geists of early AFX and turbo-charged Jah Shaka with X-amount of moist noise and mystery in the air - the sort of stuff that feels like coming up at the blue hour in a smoke-choked warehouse or damp UK field, mud up to your shins, and loving it.

While it’s his first album since ‘SINEAD MEMORY TAPE’ in ’23, ‘Infant’ is his most substantial salvo in this signature steppers style since at least ‘5GTOUR’ (2019), or even ‘INNA BABALON’ (2016). Satisfyingly crusted with distortion around the edges and fully marshy underfoot, it best portrays the JTG essence in long form, conjuring an hour of heavily hypnotic atmospheres and fritzed production styles practically incomparable to anyone beyond his immediate family of 5GT label oddballs: Tribe of Colin, Xterea, YL Hooi, et al.

Hewing tighter than ever to his thing, JTG generates one of the baddest tools in his bag between the cloven-hoofed whirligig ‘7thfloor (Myrda Mix)’ and the air-stepping gait of ‘Population’, taking in his stride a sort of Kongo Tekno hunch on ‘Going In’ and byzantine ambience of ‘Mrzy 2 (Stone Mix)’,  making room for strains of zoned-out dankness before reeling back to the blunted ends of Caustic Window and the ribboning melodica and jabbing subs of ‘Rising’, before the astro junkyard pound of the title tune and the body-levitating mastery of ‘Goin In (Mer Mix)’.

It all leaves a peculiar tang.

Big tip!
items._genre: dub techno / steppers / experimental electronic / UK bass
items._cn_summary: John T. Gast 在专辑《Infant》中呈现了十三首深沉、迷幻的steppers舞曲，将90年代锐舞文化的粗砺质感与Cornish锐舞场景的潮湿氛围融为一体。制作上充满失真边缘和泥泞低频，融合早期AFX的电子怪异、Jah Shaka的声音系统重击以及潮湿的噪音纹理，营造出烟熏仓库和英国户外锐舞的催眠氛围。从碎裂的故障制作到Byzantine式氛围段落，再到回响深远的次低音和melodica旋律线，专辑以长篇幅形式完整展现了作者标志性的声音美学，在当代地下电子场景中几乎无人能复制这种独特风格。

items.body:
DJ Plead and rRoxymore with a sick debut collab of rhythmelodically restless productions, infusing limber, freewheeling styles with subtly psychedelic balearic melodics - a big one for followers of CCL, Batu, Nick León, Olof Dreijer, Joe, Nídia & Valentina Magaletti.

After meeting for the first time in 2019, Hermione Frank and Jarred Beeler got together at Frank's Berlin studio, slowly sculpting fractal geometries before finally adding the finishing spit and polish at Beeler's parents’ house in Sydney. Marking some of the first original material from either in a minute, the EP knits the duo’s rhythmic fascinations in three ways. 

‘Celestial’ splices a rolling 4/4 with quicksilver polyrhythms and zippy melodic motifs swept into hand-clap trills, imagining something like Olof Dreijer re-shaping Joe’s angular syncopations. ‘Read Wrong’ follows to foreground a thumb piano on a more pendulous, sub-weighted flex, inflected with DJ Plead’s signature palette of drum sounds and canny orchestral flashes at the right moments, dipping like D1’s more melodic works or that forthcoming Nídia & Valentina Magaletti pearl. 

The duo save their most hard-hitting for last, sliding speedy, dembow-inspired geometries through green-tinted clouds of electronics on a UKF-compatible offbeat threaded with swooping subs and flighty flutes. The momentum never lets up, but the two producers manage to evoke a mood that's as suited to a late-nite solo thing as it is to peak time wreckage. In other words; deceptively effortless gear that hits harder the louder it gets.
items._genre: experimental electronic / club / polyrhythmic fusion / balearic
items._cn_summary: 这是DJ Plead与rRoxymore首度合作的EP，两人分别来自悉尼和柏林，经历了跨城市的创作过程。整张作品围绕节奏实验展开，将4/4底鼓与快速变换的复合节奏交织，融入零散而流动的旋律动机，呈现出不拘一律的自由感。开篇曲在滚动四四拍上叠加水银般的复节奏与拍手花音，中段引入拇指琴与深沉低音，结尾曲则将dembow启发的高速律动穿入电子云层与UKF兼容的离线节奏。两位制作人在鼓组音色选择上展现出对管弦乐质感的敏锐直觉，整体听感既适合深夜独处也适配舞池高峰，音量越大冲击力越强，体现了表面轻松实则层次繁复的制作理念。

items.body:
Mannequin tap an arsenal of secret German electro weapons, as played by Helena Hauff and I-F, hailing a pivotal era when body music set the scene for electroclash, stuffed with zingers FFO Le Syndicat Electronique, I-F, Dopplereffekt, Drexciya, Legowelt, Adult., The Hacker, DMX Krew, Gesloten Cirkel, and early Bunker Records electro 

“Active around the turn of the millennium, both projects share the involvement of producer Ive Müller while developing distinct collaborations and approaches to electronic music. H.E.I.M. Elektronik was founded in 1996 by Holger Erlenwein and Ive Müller (after the two artists split in 1999, Müller continued using the name), while MAS 2008 is the project of Ive Müller together with René Kirchner. Though separate entities, the two projects explored a similar sonic territory: stripped-down electro, minimal electronics and machine-driven body music shaped by analog hardware and a raw DIY production ethos.

The roots of Müller’s work go back to the final years of the DDR. As a teenager he worked as a licensed DJ — officially known as a “Schallplattenunterhalter” — operating a travelling disco across Saxony. With limited access to official Western releases, music circulated through cassette recordings taped from West German radio stations such as RIAS Berlin, NDR2 and Bayern3. Together with friends he travelled between youth clubs and discos around Leipzig with a “rolling discotheque”: a Russian Wolga pulling a trailer loaded with Electro-Voice sound systems sourced through the black market.

At the turn of the 2000s this background in underground electronic culture resurfaced in a series of recordings rooted in electro, EBM and minimal machine music. The tracks collected on Electronic Corporation 2000–2002 capture this moment: cold sequences, driving rhythms and stark synthetic textures produced with a direct and uncompromising approach.

Compiled and remastered by Rude 66 from the original sources, Electronic Corporation 2000–2002 documents a small but fascinating chapter of German underground electronics from the early digital era.”
items._genre: electro / EBM / minimal electronics / body music
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Ive Müller参与的两个项目H.E.I.M. Elektronik与MAS 2008在2000至2002年间的作品。两位制作人在冷战末期东德的地下电子场景中成长，青年时代以自制流动音响设备在各青年俱乐部之间辗转演出，早期音乐来源完全依赖从西德广播电台录制磁带。这段独特的文化背景直接塑造了后来作品中冷峻的合成器序列、硬朗的机械节奏与极简的硬件质感。整张专辑以模拟设备直录的粗糙美学为核心，旋律线条被压缩至最低限度，强调节奏与音色的原始冲击力。由Rude 66从原始素材重新编选并完成母带处理，呈现了德国电子地下场景中一个短小但极具文献价值的片段。

items.album: Cobalt Blue & Live at the Aquarium (2026 Remaster)

items.body:
Inspired by Ennio Morricone, J.J. Cale and Hindustani classical music, Michael Brook's 1992 4AD debut is a 2nd wave ambient/new age classic, finally remastered and bundled with the genius follow-up EP 'Live at the Aquarium'. Unmissable FFO Jon Hassell, Harold Budd, Daniel Lanois, Brian Eno and David Sylvian.

Brook is best known for his soundtrack work at this point - his influential scores for films like 'An Inconvenient Truth' and 'The Fighter' - but rewind back to the early 1990s and he was living in London, jobbing as a producer and working with Brian Eno. He'd released a few records by that point, collaborating with Eno and Daniel Lanois on his Editions EG debut 'Hybrid' and collaborating with Dutch artist Pieter Nooten on the excellent 'Sleeps with the Fishes' in 1987. But his most important contribution had arguably been his Infinite Guitar, a modified electric guitar that allowed him to play long sitar-like drones. He used that technique on Jon Hassell's beloved 1986 album 'Power Spot' and famously built an instrument for the Edge, who played it on 'With or Without You'. And while he was working with other musicians, he was sketching out ideas for this next record, working slowly in his bedsit in-between commercial work and attempting to adapt the music he loved, particularly bluegrass and the work of Indian flute player Pannalal Ghosh.

Unsurprisingly, it's Brook's guitar sounds that take the lead from the beginning, muddled with woozy synths and assistance from a team of his close associates: Brian Eno, Daniel Lanois, Roger Eno, Dead Can Dance's James Pinker, violinist Hahn Rowe, Hassell collaborator Richard Henderson and viola player Nell Catchpole. The music is very much of its era, a core text for 4AD or Les Disques Du Crepusule heads, and illustrates just how quickly "ambient" and "new age" music were evolving. Brook hadn't been classically trained, so was urged by Hassell to do some lessons with La Monte Young, an experience that had led him to the Infinite Guitar in the first place. But long sustain wasn't the beginning and end of his interest in Hindustani classical music or in 20th century minimalism. You can hear just how the genres were being re-codified here, how traditional rhythms were being re-interpreted on drum machines and how Steve Reich's and Philip Glass's innovations were being absorbed by wide-eyed onlooker long before they became rave's after-hours staples.

If the album sounds a little frilly 35 years after its original release, that's mostly because Brook's sound was jumped on by Hollywood remarkably quickly. Just three years after 'Cobalt Blue' was released, the track 'Ultramarine' was conspicuously placed in Michael Mann's 'Heat' alongside selections from Terje Rydpal, Lisa Gerrard and Brian Eno. And he quickly became a staple, contributing to Hans Zimmer soundtracks like 'Mission: Impossible 2' and 'Black Hawk Down' and working on prestige projects like 'Into the Wild' and 'Brooklyn'. So if you're interested in hearing a more stripped down version of the album, then 4AD handily bundled it with 'Live at the Aquarium ' when they reissued the album for the first time in 1999. The show was recorded at the press party for the release of 'Cobalt Blue' and features Brook on his own, playing even more passionately and demonstrating the nuance of his signature technique.
items._genre: ambient / new age / experimental / world fusion / minimalism
items._cn_summary: 这张1992年发行的专辑是Michael Brook为4AD厂牌录制的首张个人作品，灵感源自Morricone、J.J. Cale与印度斯坦尼古典音乐。Brook发明的Infinite Guitar——一种可演奏西塔琴式长持续音的改装电吉他——是整张专辑的音色核心，长泛音与朦胧合成器交织，辅以Brian Eno、Daniel Lanois等合作者的演奏。专辑将蓝草音乐、印度笛演奏家Pannalal Ghosh的东方元素、Steve Reich与Philip Glass式的极简主义以及新兴的鼓机节奏融为一体，记录了ambient与new age音乐在1990年代初快速演变的轨迹。同捆发行的'Live at the Aquarium' EP作为后续现场作品合为一辑重新制作，为这张被好莱坞电影配乐频繁借鉴的经典提供了完整的再版。

items.body:
Softly softly does it for the gorgeous debut duo of soundtrack composer Elori Saxl & saxophonist Henry Solomon with their lushly ephemeral grasp of 4th world ambient jazz, tipped for the anyone on the line between Lynch/Badalamenti, TLF Trio, Laurel Halo, Arve Henriksen or Alex Zhang-Hungtai's Love Theme side-wind.

Captured over a few days in LA, ‘Seeing Is Believing’ frames the sax player’s searching feel for tone across soundscapes sparingly coloured in subtle harmonic gradients by Elori Saxl’s fluttering Juno 106 keys. The nine parts are testament to the duo’s near-telepathic level of intuition and mutual vision of a palpably tissue-soft atmospheric music; one where spectres of ’70s minimalism and ’80s new age bleed forward into structures equally informed by soundsystem culture and contemporary pop production, achieving a sort of slow shifting, ecological pressure system that is a pleasure to sink into.

Within her richly visual, implicitly storytelling style, Elori Saxl draws on a wellspring of experience in composing for new music ensembles, and soundtracking and directing films for New Yorker and Slate, to set spacious dimensions for Solomon’s ruminative baritone sax and bass clarinet to wander freely. A quiet sense of restraint defines proceedings as their forms gently grow and sway from the dusky licks of ‘Reverence’ thru the gauzy lustre of the title piece, conjuring a geosmin waft in ‘Raindrops’ and LA hills panorama on ‘Reno Silver’, or balmiest breeze of Glass-like phrasing on ‘A Thousand Steps’, into the gorgeous, pitch bent and sensual sorcery summoned in standout ‘Heart.’

Stunner.
items._genre: ambient jazz / fourth world / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是配乐作曲家Elori Saxl与萨克斯演奏家Henry Solomon的二重奏首作，在洛杉矶于数日内完成录制。Saxl以Juno 106合成器铺设细腻的和声渐变色彩，Solomon则在上方展开探索性的次中音萨克斯与低音单簧管独奏。九首曲目呈现一种近乎心灵感应的默契协作，结构受七十年代极简主义与八十年代新世纪音乐影响，同时融入声音系统文化与当代流行制作手法。音乐在柔缓的动态中缓慢推移，从昏暗的爵士乐句延展到薄雾般的光泽织体，部分段落呼应菲利普·格拉斯式的清晰句法。整体克制而留白充裕，让乐器的即兴漫游拥有充足空间，作品具有强烈的画面感与叙事潜质。

items.body:
The inimitable DeForrest Brown, Jr. caps off his Speaker Music project with a final set of expressionistic technoid evolutions, editing live improvisations into studio-corrupted projections of his musical mind map that runs through jazz, trap, shoegaze, dub and drone. Essential listening whether you're into Miles, Drexciya or Autechre.

Primarily used to mean a "summary" of sorts, the word synoptic is often found in connection with Biblical scholarship, grouping the New Testament gospels of Matthew, Mark and Luke together because of their similarities. And on 'Speaker Music', Brown attempts to isolate comparable harmonies between various Black musical strands, examining the marching band music he grew up playing, Sun Ra and experimental jazz, and realising how all this factors into the development of electronic music, steering its course even now. Brown calls the project "theory first", an analysis of rhythm in Black music as it pertains to his landmark text 'Assembling a Black Counter Culture'. And it's run its course at this stage; if you've heard 2023's excellent 'Techxodus' or its predecessors, you'll already know the general theme - a sonic space where free jazz, footwork, gospel and noise exists at once in spiritual harmony.

Brown's final act as Speaker Music is to take recordings from his residencies at Troy's EMPAC and Vancouver's Libby Leshgold Gallery and sculpt them into dense "studio-as-instrument" snapshots of his theory. He starts with Don Lewis, the musician and engineer (and nuclear weapons specialist) who developed a pre-MIDI sound controller for analog synthesizers that he called the LEO, or Live Electronic Orchestra. Brown uses this methodology to guide his own setup (on iPad, MacBook and mixer), using software modules, effects units and drum machines to simulate Lewis's arsenal of vintage boxes, then transports the results to the studio for "post production editing, overdubbing and spacial manipulation." He ends up with a sound that's constantly changing, on the one hand driven by the skittering techno-to-trap drum sequences that powered his other records and on the other zeroing in on the sonic density and physicality of set texts like A Guy Called Gerald's 'Black Secret Technology' and Miles Davis's ornery and prophetic masterpiece 'On The Corner'.

On opener 'Techno-Vernacular Expressionism', Brown makes the direction clear by ducking the whirring hi-hats and syncopated kicks deep beneath elasticated and saturated dub-echoed chords. Even when the rhythms are moved closer to the spotlight on 'Saecularhythmia...' they're muddled with remnants of those same chords, spliced alongside Brown's own decelerated half-human monologs. These experiments open the floodgates for a sequence of punk-ier experiments that consider the impact of sound on the body itself, taking into account not just rhythm but tone, timbre and distortion. On 'Chaosmosis', Brown's obsessively edited beat sequences are set, 'Amber'-like, against a single growling synth note and on the title track, he uses rhythmelodic hits and coarse feedback to herald a psych-jazz pivot into oscillatory mayhem in the third act. It's a record that constantly collapses and rebuilds itself, turning Drexciyan electro sequences into chiming church bells on the brilliant 'GLO//A' and day zero techno into euphoric nu-gaze on  the crushing finale, 'Dhalgren (Nihilism is Not Enough)'. We're gonna miss Speaker Music, but we've got a feeling this isn't the last we'll hear from Brown.
items._genre: experimental electronic / techno / free jazz fusion / IDM
items._cn_summary: DeForrest Brown, Jr. 以 Speaker Music 身份发布的最终专辑，将驻场即兴录音经工作室后期编辑、叠录与空间处理，转化为理论驱动的声响拼贴。专辑追溯 Don Lewis 的 LEO 控制器理念，在 iPad、MacBook 与调音台上模拟模块合成器、效果器与鼓机的组合，编织出 Techno-Vernacular Expressionism 所定义的路径——碎拍 techno 与 trap 鼓组深陷于饱和回响和弦之下，减速的人声独白与自由爵士和声交织。作品审视黑人音乐脉络中行进乐队、Sun Ra 实验爵士与电子乐的内在关联，将节奏、音色与失真视为作用于身体的物质力量，在密集编辑的节序中重现 Autechre 与 Miles Davis 那种不可预测的物质密度。

items.body:
Returning to Shelter Press, INA GRM director François J. Bonnet collages harsh, feedback-dense textures, resonant chimes and disorienting synths, inking a serpentine narrative that's part Fennesz, part Valerio Tricoli, part Jake Muir.

There's a storyteller's flair to 'Sub Re', and that's not just because the title directly references Victor Hugo's 'Toilers of the Sea'. The veteran French sound artist fashions two sides of bumpy collaged plot points, drawing us in at first with dense electroacoustic guitar noise that wouldn't sound out of place on a loveliescrushing record. Referencing shoegaze merely in its full-on power, he cuts to Sonic Youth-style squealing feedback before submerging the cacophony completely, ducking it beneath smudged low-end rumbles and 'Mulholland Drive'-like hums. It sets the scene neatly for the next movement, where Bonnet introduces an ensemble of bells that slowly, surely gather momentum; imprinted with the rhythm of post-rock, believe it or not, it's a stretch that echoes Constellation's vital early releases, stirring tape noise and chimes with simple, pensive riffs that travel confidently from quiet to loud. 

But Bonnet never makes it that easy. Before long, these elements too have disappeared, replaced by subtly beating extended tones and xenharmonic wails that are skillfully merged with thick Sunn O)))-style drones, bringing us right back to where we started. And on the flip, Bonnet is just as ambitious, beginning with an industrial organ-scape that dissolves into an evocative hum of brassy notes and inclement field recordings. Even this feels like purposeful narrative red-herring because within moments, Bonnet brings the breathy pipe organ sounds bet, forming a light, major key crescendo that he uses to foreshadow the album's most drastic mood shift. The sun cracks through the rainclouds at last and we're lowered into a dry, verdant locale that's seemingly teeming with life. It's only in the last few minutes of the side when Bonnet seems to refer back to his last record, the impressionistic 'Shifted in Dreams', with a short blast of hypnagogic moodiness before the album flickers to a close.
items._genre: electroacoustic / drone / noise collage / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 法国声音艺术家François J. Bonnet（INA-GRM总监）以新专辑《Sub Re》延续其拼贴式声音实验传统。专辑标题援引雨果《海上劳工》，整张作品以叙事情节铺陈：开篇以密集电声吉他噪音切入，融合Sonic Youth式啸叫反馈，随后沉入低频嗡鸣；中段引入钟声群组与磁带噪音，呈现后摇滚式的渐强弧线；后续段落转入Sunn O)))式厚重无人机与非谐律哀鸣。专辑B面从工业管风琴音色出发，逐步揭开至明朗的大调音阶高潮，暗示雨过天晴的转调叙事，尾段则回溯其前作《Shifted in Dreams》的半梦半醒氛围。两面拼接形成有起承转合的声音旅程，将电声作曲、噪音、无人机与具体音乐技法熔于一炉，结构野心与技术控制力兼备。

items.body:
Gulp Joachim Nordwall’s queasiest, most curdled synth tones on this supremely detuned co-op with Athens’ Stellage crew = 45 minutes of pure nasal-drip tang and gungy pulses tipped FFO Connor Camburn, Wolf Eyes, Conrad Schnitzler, Ilpo Väisänen’s Liima alltimers.

Joachim Nordwall’s 1st solo jaunt since capping the ‘Healing Music’ series in ’23 finds the DIY linchpin and serial collaborator coaxing potently psychoactive tones from an undisclosed set up. It appears to be one of his most intently focussed jags in recent memory, concentrated on juicing a paucity of ingredients for optimal flavour. Nothing that new then? Well, aye, but when he really gets into it, with an effect that really probes parts of the psyche untouched by anything we’ve heard from him before, he produces synaesthetic sounds that frankly makes our ears salivate. 

A starting exercise in plucky pulse-work recalling Robert Aiki Aubrey Lowe initiates a real descent into the nether regions of Nordwall’s imagination, pulling into sepulchral drone on ‘Trance Recording’ and Droog wet dream material on ‘Abandoned Test Site’, while allowing for some levity in the lacquer-crackling pulse poem ‘Expand Your Mind’. However, he soon pitches back into resonant, metallic sonorities with durational conviction on a ‘Some Skies Overlap’ bringing to mind Connor Camburn works, but with an icier edge, and his title track spews molten drums in a rumbling, spark-spitting torrent. 

Proper filth. Snorkel it!
items._cn_summary: Joachim Nordwall 完成《Healing Music》系列后的首张个人专辑，与雅典 Stellage 团队合作，以不公开的设备系统产出四十五分钟的极度失调合成器音景。整体听感粘稠、恶臭、带有鼻腔刺激感，介于酸涩脉冲与厚重嗡鸣之间，被拿来与 Connor Camburn、Wolf Eyes、Conrad Schnitzler、Ilpo Väisänen 等人并置。作品从弹拨式脉冲出发，逐步滑入墓穴般的低频持续音和湿漉漉的鼓机节奏，中间穿插表面略带轻盈的音色裂纹诗。合成器金属质感与电钻般的高频颤动贯穿始终，鼓组在末段以熔岩状倾泻而出。整张专辑聚焦于极简元素的最大化榨取，用有限的音色堆叠出心理深层探索的声响空间。

items.body:
Four ensemble works by the English composer James M. Creed.

Another Timbre extend a quietly enchanting introduction to young composer James M. Creed with his 2nd album, a slowly unfurling, minimalist investigation of consonance/dissonance written for, performed, and recorded by three young ensembles - Standard Issue, To Your Ear Collective and Outline Ensemble - including his guitar as part of three works. Referencing the expansive stillness and microtonal work of Éliane Radigue, the bloodletting of Julius Eastman, and Wandelweiser staple Antoine Berger
items._cn_summary: 英国年轻作曲家 James M. Creed 的第二张专辑，收录四首为室内乐团创作的合奏作品。Another Timbre 厂牌发行，由三支年轻乐团——Standard Issue、To Your Ear Collective 与 Outline Ensemble——演奏并录音，其中三首作品加入了吉他。整体风格呈现出缓慢展开的极简主义倾向，深入探讨协和与不协和之间的张力。创作参照包括 Éliane Radigue 的广阔静默与微分音实践、Julius Eastman 的激烈表达，以及 Wandelweiser 群落的代表人物 Antoine Berger。专辑将极简结构与实验性室内乐手法结合，是当代古典与现代作曲领域的值得关注的新声音。

items.body:
Memotone’s sublime, world-building ambient-jazz-fusion project yields a total gem for Accidental Meetings, perfused with the presence of Ugné Uma, Typesun & Jabu on a new highlight of his personalised microcosm, tipped for anyone on the line from Savath & Savalas to Moritz Von Oswald Trio, The Necks to Laurel Halo.

Active since 2011, it’s been a real pleasure to hear Will Yates cultivate his memotone sound into something more complex, yet not necessarily more complicated, on a slew of LPs for the likes of TTT, Sähkö, and World of Echo, plus that ace cut on Carrier’s debut LP. Club music is now long in the rearview, while ambient and jazz musics have taken precedence as the multi-instrumentalist continues to diversify his creative binds across more free-formed, expressive soundscapes, breezing with elements of spiritual jazz as much as psych folk, post rock,contemporary classical and strands of electronic music. 

‘Warm Shadows’ features some of his most seductive and expansive work, shaped with an underlying grasp of abstract, instrumental narratives that have become his calling card during this last decade. Intimacy and slowness are key to his exquisitely hushed appeal; unfolding the softest brushstrokes with patient electroacoustic nuance and attention to detail on two standouts with emergent Lithuanian vocalist Ugné Uma, who channels a mix of smouldering spiritual jazz and Eastern European melancholy on ‘Laimèti Pavyksta’, and even Sade-esque soul on the dusky closer ‘You Are Different.’ 

Elsewhere, the Bristolian connection makes for another highlight with Jabu’s Jasmine Butt’s subtle contribution to ‘Round The Bend,’ comparable to something from BoC’s ‘Campfire Headphase’, but left to his own devices memotone proves a consummate, atmospheric storyteller. Opener ‘For The Feral’ feels like a miniature of The Necks, and his feel for dreamy electro-acoustic texture best comes into play on ‘One Winged Bird’ and the tongue-tip moisture in the air of ‘The Freedom,’ all pointing to an artist arguably in their imperial phase. 

Tip!
items._cn_summary: Memotone（Will Yates）的《Warm Shadows》是一张氛围爵士与电子原声融合作品，延续了他在TTT、Sähkö等独立厂牌积累的个人化微观宇宙路线。专辑以亲密与缓慢为核心手法，通过细腻的电声质感展开抽象的器乐叙事。立陶宛歌手Ugné Uma在两首曲目中贡献了灵性爵士与东欧忧郁交织的人声，Jabu的Jasmine Butt则带来类似BoC《Campfire Headphase》氛围的合作段落。作品横跨灵性爵士、迷幻民谣、后摇滚、当代古典与电子音乐等多个领域，开篇曲式展现了对The Necks即兴结构的理解，多曲中则以梦幻电声纹理营造呼吸感。整体呈现出一位多乐器演奏者在创作生涯高峰期的沉稳表达。

items.body:
A digestibly pared-down version of Félicia Atkinson's 90-minute score to Georges Franju's controversial French horror film 'Les yeux sans visage' ('Eyes Without A Face'), 'SANS VISAGE' is her most sinister material to date, made on piano and keyboards and improvised to the film. 

Atkinson was just a teenager when she first saw Franju's 1960 film and it moved her enough that when she was approached by Belgian cultural institute VIERNULVIER to work on a new score, she knew exactly how to approach it. She remembered how impactful the film's themes had been and how resonant they were even decades later, where violence against women is still nauseatingly commonplace. In the film, an adaptation of an even more disturbing novel by Jean Redon, a plastic surgeon stalks and kills women who look like his disfigured daughter, removing their faces in an attempt to create a new one for her. Atkinson dedicates her slow-motion, menacing soundtrack to Gisèle Pelicot, remarking how patriarchal violence cycles again and again through history, creating cages within cages for women. But there's hope; Atkinson doesn't languish in darkness and terror, she knows that in there somewhere, liberation might be on the horizon. 

Underneath the grim, gloomy electric piano notes and agonising pauses, Atkinson seems to relish in a sense that escape might be possible. And if you've seen the film then you'll realise that she's acknowledging the fact that Dr. Génessier, the antagonistic surgeon, meets a fittingly grisly end. While he's let off the hook by police, his daughter Christiane is horrified by his crimes, freeing the dogs he was experimenting on and letting them take their revenge. It's a horror film, after all. But Aktinson swerves all the usual tropes; she improvises an impressionistic dream of wailing tones and aborted phrases that centre the resolution, not the torture itself. Re-scores are often a creative dead end, but thankfully this one adds texture, color and new context to the source material - it makes us want to watch the film all over again.
items._genre: avant-garde / experimental / dark ambient / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: Félicia Atkinson 为乔治·弗朗朱1960年法国恐怖片《无脸之眼》重新配乐，将原90分钟长度的影像配乐精简为更易消化的版本。整张作品以钢琴与键盘即兴完成，笼罩在阴郁电钢琴音符与窒息式留白之下。她从少女时代起便对这部关于整形外科医生杀害女性并剥取其面部皮肤的影片印象深刻，并将此作献给Gisèle Pelicot，揭示父权暴力在历史中反复循环的残酷现实。Atkinson 并未沉溺于黑暗，而是以哀嚎的音调与破碎的乐句构建印象派梦境，将重心放在解救与释放而非折磨本身。这一再创作超越了原素材的边界，为黑白影像增添了新的层次与色彩，驱使观众重新审视这部经典。

items.body:
Edgar puts his kinky, Latinate stamp on myriad styles of Hi-NRG, gothic synth-pop, and cumbia, including a cover of Amanda Lear’s ‘Follow Me’ among its bevy of sleazy darkroom snax...

"Edgar debuts on Dark Entries with Pavor, an 11 track LP of sleazy disco, warped synthpop, and gothic cumbia. Veteran musician Luis Gutierrez has spent the past two decades touring in bands, running Lalalandia Studio, and building his practice in Oakland and Guadalajara. But now, for his first solo outing, he has become Edgar, a pop star who knows no limits! “Edgar feels mightier than anyone but is always reduced to his vices” says Gutierrez, and Pavor delivers vices in spades.

From the opening salvos of “Otra Agua,” it’s clear we’re in for a wild ride: seasick synths slide along slamming disco beats, menacingly chanted vocals sit amid a flurry of careening horror movie samples. The mischief does not abate as we’re guided through a demented funhouse of genre detournements. Edgar puts his indelible fingerprints over every inch of this vinyl, from uptempo numbers like the spooky chip-tune frenzy of “Nunca Mas” to the twisted cumbia of “Panteon.” We’re even treated to a fairly faithful (and majestic) Spanish-language cover of Amanda Lear’s “Follow Me,” here titled “Sigueme.” EBM, space disco, and horror movie soundtracks all find their way into the mix on Pavor, but the diverse palette comes together perfectly, like a Yello album for the 21st century.

On Pavor, Edgar brings us a healthy dose of pure excess, reminding us that dread can be a hell of a lot of fun. "
items._genre: darkwave / synth-pop / Hi-NRG / gothic cumbia / EBM
items._cn_summary: Edgar的首张专辑《Pavor》在Dark Entries厂牌发行，是一张跨越多种风格的地下舞曲作品，融合了Hi-NRG高能迪斯科、哥特合成器流行、黑暗cumbia、EBM及恐怖电影配乐元素。主创Luis Gutierrez拥有二十余年乐队经历与录音棚运营背景，专辑呈现出一种放纵而怪诞的审美，将扭曲的合成器旋律、沉重的迪斯科节奏与咏唱式人声并置，还收录了Amanda Lear名曲《Follow Me》的西班牙语翻唱版。整体编排如同一部失控的恐怖嘉年华，将类型之间的界限彻底模糊，制造出既阴暗又充满趣味的听觉体验。

items.body:
Al Wootton wears his polyrhythmic club cap on four percussive trips, with a big standout 'Tone Circle' channeling Shackleton's 'Blood On My Hands' alltimer.

As with recent years’ turns toward more offbeat rhythm and meter, Wootton maintains a wonky ballast for supple dancers across ‘River Song’. They follow a certain declension of energies and rhythmic democracy from tune to tune, starting up rolling and acid-psychedelic like early ‘90s PWOG with ‘Xana’, and stretching out on West African-styled swing punctuated with Mbalax-esque talking drum detonations haunted with creepy sound design. ‘River Song’ continues that sort of dubbed Mbalax on a Mark Ernestus Ndagga Rhythm Force tip with sloshing bass and phantasmic synths, and ‘Hechicera’ simmers it all down to a palpitating goo leavened with rhythmelodic woodblocks.
items._genre: percussive electronic / polyrhythmic club / dub / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Al Wootton延续其近年对复节奏与非常规节拍的探索，专辑《River Songs》收录四首打击乐导向的俱乐部作品，整体维持着一种适合舞池的摇摆律动底座。开篇曲《Xana》回溯九十年代初PWOG式的滚动质感与迷幻酸音，随后在西非风格律动中融入Mbalax式手鼓爆发，配合阴森的声效设计。《River Song》延续同条路线，借鉴Mark Ernestus Ndagga Rhythm Force的dub处理手法，混响贝斯与幽冥合成器层叠。《Hechicera》则将上述元素收束为可塑的节拍粘液，木鱼敲击贯穿其中。最值得关注的'Tone Circle'呼应了Shackleton经典'Blood On My Hands'的气质，在低饱和度氛围中铺设复杂的复合节拍。整张作品在打击乐逻辑与电子声响设计的交叉地带持续深耕，对节奏感与空间感有要求的听众会从中获得满足。

items.body:
KILLER second LP from Lucid Dreams paying dues to Bristol’s rich trip hop history, landing at the intersection of theeee moodiest OG 90’s blueprints x fwd club pressure, slowed to cinematic, doom-jazzy vapours - huge tip FFO Raime, Massive Attack, Photek, Jabu, Palmskin Productions...

The Lucid Dreams handle finds Jason Luxton aka Overlook switch from inch-tight contemporary D&B into roughly-related downbeat interzones surely evoking a nocturnal Bristol for anyone raised on Tricky, Portishead or Massive Attack classics. Seemingly crafted by candlelight and bathed in opiated atmosphere, the album unfurls a midnight soundscape in considerable depth across 15 parts in 64 minutes - plenty time to roll one (or two) and luxuriate in the LP’s carefully plotted course of dub-swept, smudged bass ’n drums and smoky pall.

Like Raime before him, Lucid Dreams ideally inhabits a certain dark slipstream of intrigue that riddles post-punk thru to trip hop and its downbeat descendents, but also factored with a feel for D&B’s psychoacoustic spatial engineering that is key to his music’s appeal. Exquisite attention is paid to the dusty jazz drums and low register spectres shapeshifting its cloistered structures from the Bohren-pced doom shuffle of ‘Smoke & Mirrors’ up to what feels like dark echoes of proto-Goa or sci-fi scores in ‘Reincarnation’.

His noirish ‘Reverie’ plays out like a Tricky witching hour special, and ‘Clairvoyance’ feels like Photek or SD on 33-not-45, next to dankest Wild Bunch/early Massive Attack nod ‘Slow-Wave’, and ‘Sleepwalking’ balances Flying Saucer Attack and ‘Mezzanine’ vibes, whilst ‘Transcendence’ holds a fine line of weightless ‘90s noir tension into the high plains drift of a ‘Realisation’ recalling aspects of Memotone’s ‘Warm Shadows’.

A real sleeper gem.
items._genre: trip hop / dark ambient / downtempo / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Lucid Dreams的第二张全长作品，由Jason Luxton（艺名Overlook）操刀，他此前以紧致的当代D&B制作闻名，此作则转向更为绵长的慢速低频地带。整张唱片横跨15个段落、共计64分钟，以烛光般的昏暗氛围铺陈午夜声景，融合Bristol九〇年代trip hop的忧郁底色与当代地下俱乐部的空间声学处理。制作上突出灰尘感十足的爵士鼓机、低频贝斯幽灵般的形变以及烟雾弥漫的混响空间，曲目从带有Bohren der Club of Gore气息的doom shuffle逐步推进到接近proto-Goa与科幻配乐质感的暗色回响。整张唱片展现出对九〇年代Massive Attack、Tricky、Portishead式黑暗质感的深度继承，同时以D&B制作中的心理声学空间感作为结构支点，是一张在氛围营造与节奏暗流之间取得微妙平衡的地下佳作。

items.body:
Apartment House ably execute the first recording of an hour-long piece defined by a certain sense of cathartic bloodletting that prompted pianist Philip Thomas to describe it as “obscenely gorgeous; wonderfully moving without ever overstepping the line into sentimentality." 

"Composed between 2023 and 2025 after Jurg Frey withdrew from clarinet performance, this 54-minute chamber work places Heather Roche's clarinet within the string quartet of Mira Benjamin, Chihiro Ono, Bridget Carey and Anton Lukoszevieze, as Apartment House reveal a quietly extraordinary balance of stillness and motion, warm tonal color, intimate dialogue and a slow, organic passage toward unexpected transformation."
items._genre: contemporary classical / chamber music / experimental / minimalist
items._cn_summary: 这是Jürg Frey的单簧管五重奏首录，由Apartment House乐团演奏。作品创作于2023至2025年间，Frey在退出单簧管演奏生涯后完成，时长54分钟，以单簧管为核心与弦乐四重奏展开对话。乐评将其描述为一种宣泄式的创作过程，钢琴家Philip Thomas称之为'惊人地优美，在不越界陷入感伤的前提下依然动人'。音乐在静止与运动之间取得精妙平衡，音色温暖而细腻，通过缓慢的有机展开实现意想不到的转化。整体呈现出安静而非凡的特质，适合关注当代古典与实验音乐交叉领域的听众。

items._cn_summary: 理查德·D·詹姆斯1992年的经典专辑历经多次再版，依然保持着诞生之初的鲜活生命力，被视为其个人厂牌AFX旗下最具怀旧与振奋特质的作品之一。这张专辑是深入探索詹姆斯众多微观音乐世界的入口之作，以环境音乐与智能舞曲的融合手法，奠定了Aphex Twin作为电子音乐先锋的地位。文本将之描述为通往其宏大音乐宇宙的门户毒品，暗示其影响力深远且容易令人沉迷。专辑以编程化的音色与氛围纹理构建独特的听觉空间，是90年代电子音乐场景中无法绕开的里程碑式录音。

items.body:
One of those releases that makes you feel like no other music exists for a hot minute, Dean Blunt returns with a second Black Metal album for Rough Trade, delving deeper into his unfathomable yet completely approachable and direct take on visceral x melancholic folk-pop. Spoiler: It’s really fucking good.

Aided on most of the songs here by Joanne Robertson’s vocal counterpoint and Giles Kwakeulati King-Ashong’s skittering drums, these songs once again connect to AR Kane’s distinct approach to the avant grade thru imperfection. In effect, it feels like Blunt manages to squeeze all the sterile sheen out of overly tasteful music, leaving a throbbing mass of flesh, blood vessels, nerve endings - exposed and beautiful. It’s what AR Kane called ‘Kaning’ (see Dhanveer Singh Brar’s excellent 'Beefy's Tune’ book for more on this) - and effectively provides a vital riposte to a world in which so much “art" is presented and consumed as a form of numbing.

And that riposte requires no explanation - a personal narative woven with little concession to anything - there’s not even a tracklisting or credits on the physical formats, instead Blunt’s ideas are wrapped up in a succession of first grade earworms, string sections here and there, billowing subs - all melancholy, blunt smoke and bliss. 

"Flaws are discontinuities that act as tiny fissures, allowing the dim and distant, diffused gem light of pre-creation to slip thru - it is this that music existed for - a signpost, a reminder, a note.” Rudy Tambala / A.R. Kane

Black Metal 2 is as real as it gets.
items._genre: experimental folk-pop / avant-garde / lo-fi / art pop
items._cn_summary: Dean Blunt 延续 Black Metal 系列，带来第二张专辑深入其独特的实验民谣流行美学。与 Joanne Robertson 的声部交织和 Giles Kwakeulati King-Ashong 的碎拍鼓机共同构建出一种粗粝却有机的声响质地，承接 AR Kane 所提出的'Kaning'美学——以不完美抵抗精致化的主流制作。专辑拒绝提供曲目列表和制作人员名单，将所有意图封装在旋律钩子、弦乐段落和低频轰鸣之中，不加解释地直抵听者。评论引述 AR Kane 成员 Rudy Tambala 的话语，将瑕疵比作创世前的微光裂隙，暗示音乐作为路标与提醒的本质。整体气质忧郁而坦诚，在极简呈现中蕴含复杂的情绪层次。

items.body:
If you thought Dave Huismans’ (aka 2562, aka A Made Up Sound) recent return as ex_libris was good, his new, long-form minimalist dub special for Fergus Jones’ FELT label under the "In Transit" alias is another leap up, giving wings to nearly 40 mins of the finest shine-eyed downbeat pressure this side of NWAQ/154, Studio Pankow, Civilistjävel! or Rod Modell - proper top tier business.

In Transit sees Huismans go one step deeper down the rabbit hole he entered as ex_libris a few months ago. Like that project, it finally sees light of day after many years marinading in folders he would return to irregularly as a sort of meditative practice, dusting down loops and seeing how they connected after some dozen years hidden away in the archive.

When he finally got to unravelling them, they revealed a vibe that’s a far cry from his earliest work, and although sharing a slower, hazier aesthetic with ex_libris, he would logically push that sound deep into a sort of subconscious hypnagogia guided by sixth senses and shorn of any urgent, rhythmic impulses. The result is hugely absorbing  - deep without losing momentum, winding down different paths that feel engaging rather than forgettable.

At a rested heart rate the tracks swim on the imagination from distant, sonorous clanks and whispered chords in ‘A.33’, thru the tongue-tip thizz and searching tendrils of ‘A.2829’, to the subaquatic jazz sway of ‘A.18’, gently surfacing for air in the blissed iridescence of an ‘A.25’ shades away from NWAQ’s ‘Dead Bears’ vibes shared with the crystalline synth motifs of ‘A.19’, and vaporised to exquisite effect in ‘A.3132.’  

Special one.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dave Huismans（2562、A Made Up Sound）以In Transit为名在FELT厂牌下发行的长篇极简dub作品。素材源于他十余年间不定期翻看、从存档中重新连接循环段落的冥想式创作实践，呈现出远离早期作品的潜意识催眠氛围，节奏脉冲被剥离，取而代之的是缓慢、朦胧的下行声景。专辑近四十分钟篇幅横跨多首编号曲目，从远处的金属共鸣与低语和弦，到舌颤质感与游丝般的搜寻旋律，再到水下爵士摇摆感与晶体合成器动机，最终在蒸汽化的余韵中消散。整体走向深沉却不失行进感，各路径引人入胜而非流于遗忘，将dub的回声美学推入近催眠的听觉纵深。

items.body:
Adrian Rew's properly hypnotic cult classic 'Slot Machine Music' has finally been reissued and it sounds even more terrifying and prescient than it did back in 2013 at the height of the basement noise era. One of the best environmental recording records bar none - don't sleep.

Back in 2009, PAN released its fourth album, 'Kenrimono', a set of recordings made by Greek sound artist Ilios at Japanese pachinko halls. The sheer density of it was as shocking and as intense as anything the noise genre had to offer, packed out with whirring, crunching and chiming resonances that took you to the smokey epicenter of the Japanese gambling world. And when 'Slot Machine Music' arrived a few short years later we assumed the sound would be similar; we were wrong. Initially dropped via Rew's own Ergot Records on CDr before the great Aaron Dilloway stepped in to handle the vinyl edition on his own Hanson imprint, the album seemingly grew from the Midwestern noise petri dish - but it wasn't an exercise in aesthetic posturing, using the racket of the modern American casino to mimic the intensity of a Wolf Eyes set. Instead, Rew was drawn to the experience itself, that's been meticulously designed by malign forces to guide behavior: those trapped inside the casino's four walls are seduced into spending more, losing more and returning to do it all over again.

Rew didn't know much about the environment when he visited Cleveland's Horseshoe Casino for the first time in 2013 armed with an Olympus LS-11 recorder and a camera. And over four months, he developed a peculiar relationship with the culture, surreptitiously taping the soundscapes at various Midwestern locations - in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio and Illinois - while attempting not to lose too much cash in the process. And it's a warts-n-all set, with dialog snippets and outdoor ambiance giving us more than simply the dense mass of chimes and stings and themes that you'd hear on the casino floor itself. What Rew is able to do is create a snapshot of a time and place, capturing the sheer desolation of the casino experience and using it to drive a narrative that Robert Altman would be proud of. The first thing you notice is that each machine's sounds are in tune with the next; "game designers," explains Rew, "tune their machines to the key of C in order to optimize harmonic cohesion." So although Rew's recordings are full-bodied, they're never too chaotic or discordant. 

Indeed, if you check in for the entire record - 2013's iconic 'Slot Machine Music' and its 2014 sequel 'Slot Machine Music Vol. 2' - you'll be lulled into the same false sense of security that entrances casino regulars. It's almost like ambient music, packed out with tiny sonic details that some well-paid sound engineer-cum-neurologist worked for years to figure out. Guided meditation music? New age crypto-psychedelia? It's all here, packaged in neon-lit one-armed-bandits aimed to target the dopamine centers of aging boomers with money to burn. And the best thing about the recordings is that Rew keeps some of the chatter intact, so we can hear him tangling with casino security, or haggling with his slot machine neighbors over change. We can hear the cheers and claps as paltry sums are won while vast fortunes are lost. The best moment for us comes when Rew wanders outside Grand Victoria Casino in Elgin, Illinois at the dead of night, the crickets singing as the machines echo from behind grand double doors. A freight train rushes past and blots out any other sound, distorting the recording.

It's a good reminder that although you might be able to hide from reality inside the casino, the Midwest will inevitably confront you with its rusted truth.

items._cn_summary: Adrian Rew以一台Olympus LS-11录音机深入美国中西部多家赌场，历时四个月捕捉老虎机的声学景观。不同于简单叠加机械噪音，他揭示了赌场设计师将所有机器调至C大调以实现和声统一的设计逻辑——这种声音不是混乱，而是经过精密计算的操控工具。专辑融合场内筹码碰撞声、弹球机嗡嗡声与外部环境音轨，呈现赌场体验的荒凉本质。Rew将商业空间的声学设计转化为批判性聆听素材，创造出近乎环境音乐的催眠效果。两卷合集被定位为环境录音领域的cult经典，从独立小厂Egot Records到Hanson厂牌发行，展现了声音艺术在消费空间中的独特切入点。

items.body:
Shakali practises signature forms of overeasy exotica on a second jag with NNF, after a gem for Good Morning Tapes, rummaging thru the ambient undergrowth between Spencer Clark fantasias, Japanese environmental and modal spiritual jazz.

"Finnish multi-instrumentalist Simo Hakalisto makes mosaic music of strings, bowls, bells, reeds, wind, water, and obscure electronics, threaded in subtle currents of color and texture. The title of his latest, Toinen Luonto (Finnish for “second nature”), alludes equally to Shakali’s earthen, tactile soundworld and Hakalisto’s deepening comfort with his craft.

The album’s eight songs feel coaxed as much as composed, a web of resonances set in motion and allowed to simmer, build, or billow. Vibrations and silences unspool and intertwine, alternately pointillist and diffuse, attuned to some hidden harmony of the spheres.

In addition to his own repertoire of rare instruments (including a 36-string kantele, built by Hakalisto’s grand-uncle), several notable collaborators contributed to Toinen Luonto: saxophonist Julian Overall; Hakalisto’s partner in the duo Lunar Horns, Timo Juntunen, playing udu and percussion; American experimentalist Roy Werner; and Belgian ambient flute samplist Les Halles."
items._genre: ambient / experimental / world fusion / spiritual jazz
items._cn_summary: 芬兰多乐器演奏家Simo Hakalisto以Shakali名义发行的第二张专辑，以丰富而罕见的乐器配置——包括其叔祖父手工制作的36弦康特勒琴——编织出一张由弦乐、钵、钟、簧片、风、水以及冷僻电子声响交织而成的音响网络。八首曲目更像被诱发而非被创作，振动与静默交替延展，时而点彩时而弥散，营造出一种潜藏的天体和谐氛围。专辑标题在芬兰语中意为"第二天性"，既暗示了Shakalix泥土般可触可感的声景世界，也指代创作者在自身技艺中愈发沉浸的状态。多位合作者包括萨克斯手Julian Overall、实验音乐人Roy Werner及比利时长笛采样者Les Halles等，各自带来不同质感的音色层叠，使整张作品在环境音乐、东方精神爵士与先锋器乐探索之间游走自如。
