items.body:
Over the course of the last decade, the group أحمد [Ahmed] has carved out a distinctive approach to the jazz canon through their tireless exploration of the music of Ahmed Abdul-Malik. Mining Abdul-Malik’s compositions and his incorporation of non-Western microtonality into the jazz vocabulary, pianist Pat Thomas, alto saxophone player Seymour Wright, bassist Joel Grip, and drummer Antonin Gerbal have done more than reinterpretation. They have used the music as a foundation for both immersion and subversion of the way that the standard jazz quartet functions within post-bop structures. For last year’s Sama'a (Audition), they went into the studio for an expansive refraction of Abdul-Malik’s Jazz Sahara. During that same session, the four took a slight detour to record Play Monk, a dive into deconstructions of six pieces by Thelonious Monk, all but one of which he recorded in the late 1950s when Abdul-Malik was part of his group. أحمد [Ahmed] has incorporated Monk tunes into their live sets but this is the first time they have focused on his tunes on a recording.

While Thomas, Wright, Grip, and Gerbal have not altered their strategies in the switch of source material, there is one significant shift in the way one listens to this music. A quick search returns no other versions of Abdul-Malik’s pieces other than those recorded by the composer or أحمد [Ahmed] whereas Monk’s “Epistrophy” or “’Round Midnight” have hundreds. Even a less well-known piece like “Oska T” has dozens. Because the pieces covered are so well known, their teasing apart and restructuring of the underlying thematic kernels are more readily evident. Over two CDs, the quartet digs in, with improvisations that range between 20 and 30 minutes with the exception of a seven-minute extrapolation of “Epistrophy.” These extended explorations allow the group to excavate the forms with a focused patience, zeroing in on and elucidating microscopic details, extricating them into the fundamental elements of penetrating improvisations.

The first phrases of the opening “Bye-ya / Epistrophy” provide a glimpse of what is to come. Bass and piano circle around the theme and Gerbal’s lithe drumming circles up to drive momentum. Wright’s stabbing alto picks apart the melody and the four launch off on a circuitous inquiry, dismantling Monk’s tune into its constituent fragments and then reassembling them with constructivist abstraction. Each of the four seize on elements of the underlying piece, playing them off of each other with unwavering resolve, an approach the group continues to advance in their sweeping live sets. There is an insistent intensity as Wright’s notes pick and prod at Thomas’ skewed clusters, Grip’s free walking lines, and Gerbal’s churning free rhythms. Shards of “Epistrophy” are introduced into the mix by Grip and Thomas, slowly accruing with multifaceted erudition.

The group continues to subvert expectations with “Friday the Thirteenth” as Thomas insistently repeats the first phrase of the tune against Grip’s growling arco inversions. Wright’s keypad pops and Gerbal’s open percussion build momentum and Wright unleashes spattered honks that open into a collective four-part splintering of the theme, picking it apart and recasting it with angular exactitude, building density and intensity over the course of the sweeping 26-minute improvisation. “’Round Midnight” gets a relatively straightforward introduction with Wright intoning the theme over sinuous bass and cymbal splashes. Thomas’ spare chords enter as the quartet dynamically transposes the constituent parts of the piece with imperturbable resolution resolving with the riveting cycling hushed snare abrasions that brings the piece to a close.

A seven-minute scorching, stuttering run through “Epistrophy” serves as an interlude to an abstracted, cascading reading of “Evidence” which takes Monk’s stop-start theme and explodes it with relentless, spiraled piano phrases and the hurtling momentum of bass and drums driving Wright’s coruscating alto which prods and jabs with spiky dexterity. The 30-minute improvisation is an engulfing exemplification of unflagging invention. Monk’s “Oska T.,” structured around an obsessively cyclical riff, is a fitting conclusion to the release. The quartet slows things down to a free shuffle with bass and alto arcing over the mutable pulse of piano and drums. The four players adroitly weave their lines in and out of the collective undercurrent with indefatigable ingenuity. While others have dedicated themselves to the reinterpretation of the music of Thelonious Monk, أحمد [Ahmed]’s Play Monk is distinctive in its mastery, fully absorbing his music into the collective rigor and artistry of this singular ensemble.

items._cn_summary: 专辑《Play Monk》是伦敦四人组合 أحمد [Ahmed] 对塞隆尼斯·蒙克六首作品的解构之作。乐队此前一直致力于挖掘艾哈迈德·阿卜杜勒-马利克鲜为人知的作品，此次则将目光转向蒙克——这位曾与阿卜杜勒-马利克同台的钢琴家。专辑以两碟容量呈现，每首即兴长度通常达20至30分钟，乐队将蒙克旋律拆解为碎片后以构建主义式的抽象方式重组。钢琴家Pat Thomas的偏位音簇与Seymour Wright的尖锐中音萨克斯相互碰撞，贝斯手Joel Grip的自由行走线条和鼓手Antonin Gerbal的翻腾节奏交织推进。与阿卜杜勒-马利克冷门作品不同，蒙克曲目拥有大量录音版本，使得乐队的拆解策略更加透明可辨。从开篇《Bye-ya / Epistrophy》中萨克斯对旋律的剥蚀，到片段主题在乐队互动中的缓慢累积，专辑展现出一种聚焦而耐心的挖掘姿态，将蒙克内核剥离为穿透性即兴的基本元素。

items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dorothy Moskowitz与意大利前卫作曲家Paladino及诗人Ferrari合作的成果，收录十一首歌曲，以钢琴为核心，辅以弦乐、木管与合成器铺陈，呈现出非线性、非调性的音乐结构，挑战西方和声运动的传统听觉习惯。Moskowitz的演唱方式如同方法派演员般沉稳，旋律随意识流动展开，不遵循常规功能和声，而是让每个词获得独立分量。歌词具有鲜明的政治与哲学诉求，从六十年代抗议歌曲传统出发，触及威权主义、新法西斯主义等当代议题，同时包含对死亡与人类在宇宙中位置的沉思。整体呈现出实验性与社会关怀并重的特质，是一位经历过六十年代反主流文化、如今仍持续发声的艺术家的成熟之作。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 乐队以废物利用自制的奇特乐器——tassofons、kitchenofon、klarbass 等——为载体，将克雷兹梅尔、昆比亚、桑巴、非洲节拍、中东旋律等多种世界音乐风格融于一炉。尽管材质是垃圾杂物，这些手工乐器音高准确、音色饱满，在现代录音技术下展现出惊人的丰富层次。乐队根据曲目风格灵活选择对应乐器：单簧管领衔的犹太小调配以巴松与急促打击乐，竹笛铺陈拉美风情，木琴与铃铛构筑非洲律动。每首作品均留有即兴空间，演奏者展现出扎实的技术功底与爵士化的乐句构造能力。专辑延续了首作《Hirsute Farfelus》的杂糅路线，传达出音乐人总能突破物质限制创造声响的乐观态度，是实验精神与世界音乐传统结合的典范。

items.body: Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka I n the High Middle Ages, Hildegard of Bingen said that �The truly holy person welcomes all that is earthly.� William Blake declared in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790) that �Exuberance is beauty.� In 1855, Walt Whitman published the poem �Song Of Myself, 51� in Leaves of Grass , which contains the famous line �I am large, I contain multitudes.� I�m just skimming the surface of mystical experience, of those struck by wonder and an all-encompassing insight into how people fit into the �grand scheme of things.� At some point on this trajectory, the boundary between the religious and the secular breaks down and simply being human becomes the ultimate wow. Which brings us to Polish artist Maria Ka�s latest album Di Mashin . Ka found that her family had Jewish roots, a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. As on 2023�s Der Hemshekh , she unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical, and she presents us with a whole Yiddish cosmos. While not sharing the same type of musical style, Ka reminds me of John Zorn�s aesthetic of mixing the grotesque and the sacred into Jewish experimental music. She also reminds me of the woman on the phone sampled on Wally Brill�s Jewish cantorial electronica album The Covenant (2007), who confesses she can�t sleep after hearing someone in a bar talking about the Book of Ezekiel and being haunted by the vision of Jews arriving from a future space-time. She sees that we are all suspended in webs of relationships. She is also deeply aware of how we are subject to larger social forces and structures � which sometimes must be met with radical action -- that are the machinery of life. There is a heavy dose of electro and punkish attitude spinning through her musical universe. Ostensibly, the album is divided between electronic and rock tracks, but there is a consistency to the sound that is united in loopy joy. At its best, Di Mashin is sly and sexy. Opening track �Alef � Tsentauri Disko� finds Ka in the city, musing on the seaside, wriggling like a snake at night, and watching Gdańsk wake up. �I often Dream about Cosmos, about the Land above the Earth / overhead / Alef Centauri Jewish disco!� she sings, set to a thumping urban electro grind. (See video below) Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �Vos iz dos?� is a standout, more in the �rock� vein, with Ka howling a debate over the Yiddish language itself. Perhaps it is based in a critique that she received, as she starts with What is this? Maria, what is this? I constantly hear it, it has not finished You speak no Yiddish!/ It�s so easy! Your language is incorrect, mistaken is your speech and dialect! � Given that Ka is producing new modern songs in Yiddish, there is something disarming in acknowledging the tension over who might claim ownership of language itself. Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �SuperNove� might remind listeners of Jacob wrestling with God, if that battle was done to an �80s new wave beat. Ka has visions of the past, the Old World and old demons, and she fights a ghost that rises to block her way: � I fought him with Strength, punched him with my both hands�I triumphed over him! I myself � I did triumph over him! � And after that victory, � it�s a great Surprise � the Past melted in the Cosmic Blast! � Ka also seems to be challenging herself, pointing in new directions. �Di Kosmish motorn (Cosmic engines)� brought to mind the former Warsaw Village Band�s blues-influenced singer Maja Kleszcz. Depeche Mode�s (fronted by Dave Gahan, of Jewish ancestry) forays into fusing electronica with blues might be another touchpoint. Hearing the cosmic engines like a modern day Pythagoras, she is awestruck by hearing the cosmic engines in her head. �Dos geverk (The mechanism)� offers some grinding guitars to convey the constant motion of the daily rat race � echoed later on by the title track, �Di Mashin (The Machine),� which peels back the layers of society to reveal the incessant obsession for money. The music of �The Machine� is hyperspeed cabaret, close to madness. The system demands more money � but she indicates that she is a spanner in the works, working to bring it down: � I watch the machine�s death / Full and steadily red is my hand in the end. � Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka Feminist politics come to the fore on �Ikh bin a froy (I am a woman),� and Ka reminds me a bit of the divine Ms. H of Bingen chanting over a motoric beat. She refuses to be hemmed in by structures, signaling that the Forest is her home, the stars her friends; �I wake up every day / and new scroll create.� Album closer �Di milkhome� (War)� is more future blues, transposing war, empty shipyards, and advice from her mother that all miseries will end and freedom will navigate the turmoil �like huge ships at Sea.� Di Mashin is possessed by such a singular offbeat vision and personal mythology that I wonder where Maria Ka will take her Yiddishfuturism next�Perhaps beyond our solar system, grooving on an interstellar plane with her band wriggling like snakes. Find the artist online. Further listening: Maria Ka - Der Hemshekh Warsaw Village Band & Bassałyki - Sploty WoWaKin - Kraj za miastem

items._cn_summary: 波兰艺术家Maria Ka在发现自身犹太血统后，以意第绪语创作了一系列融合电子、朋克与世界音乐元素的原创作品。《Di Mashin》专辑分为电子与摇滚两大脉络，但整体保持着循环往复的欢愉一致性。从开篇轨道' Alef – Tsentauri Disko'的城市电子律动，到'Vos iz dos?'中以摇滚骨架探讨意第绪语本身的存续意义，Ka将神圣与怪诞并置，构建出一个围绕意第绪语言与现代女性主义的独特音乐宇宙。评论将其与John Zorn的犹太实验美学相提并论，强调专辑在神秘主义体验与激进行动之间建立的张力。东欧独立厂牌发行，携带小众文化视角与跨界融合特质。

items.body: sMiLes by Jowee Omicil B orn in Montreal, Haitian-Canadian musician-composer Jowee Omicil plays a fabulous variety of saxophones, clarinets, trumpets, flutes, piano, and keyboards. He came of age in the choral milieu of his father�s Montreal congregation, studied saxophone and music education at Berklee, and gleaned much from engagement with figures including Wyclef Jean, Tony Allen, Ibrahim Maalouf, Roy Hargrove, Kenny Garrett, Pharoah Sanders, Branford Marsalis, and Marcus Miller among others. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released sMiLes one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast. The album opens with a striking reinterpretation of singer and Civil Rights activist Abbey Lincoln�s �Throw It Away,� whose message Omicil invokes in his voiceover, an expression of kinship in creative philosophical outlook. (For good measure, Omicil revisits the title on a distinctive �Throw it Away - FuLL oF LoVe Remix.�) Lincoln�s own 2007 rendition on Abbey Sings (Verve) offers critical context, itself worth a comparative audition for the original melody and the contemplative character of her lyrics. Throw it away, throw it away Give your love, live your life, each and every day And keep your hand wide open, let the sun shine through, Because you can never lose a thing, if it belongs to you. In less accomplished hands, the quirky sampling, effects, instrumentation, and wide-ranging, scruffy, sonic bricolage of sMiLes could make for one muddy m�lange. But no danger lies here in Jowee�s paradoxical, provocative, sound-shifting extended groove. Omicil's voice and sax blend almost imperceptibly in �SOeuR FeLiX AKA BeeHive.� In �Trip to GHanA,� polyrhythm meets wah-tone high-life guitar, cackly sax, and wordless vocalise. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes by Jowee Omicil Feat. Mawuena Kodjovi Other titles transport the listener to Haiti, Morocco, Cape Verde, Jupiter, and Mali. �LeTTre Du MALi PouR JonaTHan� is a meditative, revelatory piano solo nearly ten minutes in length. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes may invoke the free-blowing spirit of Miles (as on the sound-effected �MiLes ConvoY�), but there is no anxiety of influence here. Far from a rote genuflection to musical antecedents, the prevailing voice throughout is purely Omicil�s. As he counsels, �trust the note.� "Seek for the sound that is within you and the [instrument] will drive you to your destination� the singularity of sound is what I have always been searching for, the sound that comes from the heart, the sound that maybe, perhaps, is only heard in nature, this is what we are looking for when we are talking about sound� deep down, heartfelt uniqueness, always connected with the spirits�" - Jowee Omicil In accord with his music education formation, Omicil also leads music workshops through his BasH! AkademY, �a close-knit setting embracing spontaneity, authenticity, and shared growth,� which in 2025 included �a nomadic music experience traveling the world� to Mindelo, Cabo Verde. In 2026 Omicil will perform in New York, Canada, Martinique, France, Germany, Austria, Poland, Romania, the UK, and an African tour in the planning stage.

items._cn_summary: 海地裔加拿大音乐人Jowee Omicil的专辑以每月一首的形式于2025年发行，融合萨克斯、钢琴、人声与电子采样及效果处理。开篇重新诠释民权活动家Abbey Lincoln的《Throw It Away》，以画外音引入哲学对话。专辑标题暗示对Miles Davis自由吹奏精神的继承，但Omicil的声音完全属于自己：人声与萨克斯在《SOeuR FeLiX AKA BeeHive》中几乎不可分辨地融合，《Trip to GHanA》将多节奏与高life吉他、嘶哑的萨克斯和无词声乐交织。曲目跨越海地、摩洛哥、佛得角、马里等地，《LeTTre Du MALi PouR JonaTHan》是一段近十分钟的沉思钢琴独奏。整体呈现出一种悖论式的、挑衅性的、不断变形的绵长律动，声音虽繁杂却层次清晰，体现了深厚的音乐教育背景与跨文化探索。

items.body: The Visit by cris derksen The Visit isn�t an album built on compromises. The fourth release from Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father�s side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions, where it�s the opening, full-throated improvisation of �White Gladis 1� (with singer Jennifer Kreisberg) or the encompassing haunting mood that grows up around �Lyre Birds.� She�s primarily a cellist, one who works across genres; one of the great joys here is it�s impossible to attach any kind of handle to the music. Just as you think you have it nailed down, the next track is something different, as with the the cello and programming of �aabaakwad� which becomes the wordless singing of �New Heya.� The Visit by cris derksen There�s a raw, unfettered beauty to the album, music made with passion and no restraints. There are a couple of songs here, but nothing that conforms to expectations, altering gears and direction, as when the strings and brass that arrive from nowhere to take over �Buffalo Girls.� The Visit by cris derksen But the emotional centrepiece here is �Lyre Birds,� with Derksen�s cello weaving sparely around the shards of spoken words, leading into the fluttering piano arpeggios of �Nice And Clean.� This is an album of surprises, leading down strange lanes and around brilliant corners that offer startling new views. As both composer and musician, Cris Derksen is more than a singular talent; she�s a person with a vision for her music, and she keeps true to it here. The Visit is not an easy listen, but it is eminently satisfying. Find the artist online. Further listening: Liz Hanks - Land Abel Selaocoe - Where Is Home (Hae Ke Kae) The Henrys - Shrug An audio interview with Cris Derksen from The Canadian Music Centre: Prairie Region hosted by Janna Sailor

items._cn_summary: Cris Derksen是来自加拿大北TallCree保留地的细胞器演奏家，母亲有门诺派血统，专辑《The Visit》是她第四张作品，展现出不向任何既定框架妥协的姿态。评论指出音乐拒绝被归类，从与歌手Jennifer Kreisberg合作的开场即兴，到弦乐与铜管突然介入的《Buffalo Girls》，再到《Lyre Birds》中大提琴稀疏地围绕碎裂口语展开，钢琴琶音随后接续，结构持续出人意料。大提琴与电子编程的结合（如《aabaakwad》）与无歌词人声段落（《New Heya》）形成对比。整张专辑被描述为不轻易入耳却极具满足感，作曲家与演奏者双重身份使她保持明确的个人音乐愿景。原生文化与古典训练的交叉视角赋予作品独特的肌理，融合路径与评论中提及的Liz Hanks、Abel Selaocoe等独立厂牌艺术家方向相近。

items.body: Sicilian trio Nuhara have produced one of the best albums of the year in their debut, Rama. They speak to Patrick Clarke about how the discovery that a member's grandfather had been recorded by Alan Lomax led to a deep dive into the island's traditional worksongs, from which they've drawn a record of ferocious power and remarkable sonic scope Photo by Pietro Motisi Photo by Ivan-Di-Vita In 2016, the ethnomusicologist, anthropologist and folklorist Anna Lomax Wood was in Palermo for a conference. While there, she and a friend decided to take a trip to some of the Sicilian villages that her father, Alan Lomax, had visited in the 1950s to take field recordings of local folk singing. The Association Of Cultural Equity,... The post Root and Branch: An Interview with Nuhara appeared first on The Quietus.

items._cn_summary: 西西里岛三人组合 Nuhara 的首张专辑 Rama 以田野录音为根基，将祖父辈被 Alan Lomax 收录的传统劳动号子作为素材进行深度挖掘与重构。专辑在保持民间音乐原始力量的同时，展现出宽阔的声响维度——从无伴奏的人声吟唱到层次丰富的器乐编排，呈现出粗粝的爆发力与仪式感。制作源自 2016 年 Anna Lomax Wood 重访西西里村庄的契机，将尘封的民俗档案转化为当代音乐语汇。乐队将地中海岛国的音乐传统置于现代创作框架之中，既是对地方文化遗产的致敬，也是带有实验意识的当代再诠释。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — The brainchild of classically trained guitarist Jan Zehrfeld, PANZERBALLETT which is a German termreferring to a military tank ballet emerged in Munich in 2005 with its energetic and innovativebrand of jazz metal that is as equally regarded for its emotional connecting humor and funk-fueledsong structures as it is for unleashing a blitzkrieg of technical workouts. This band is legendaryin the live circuit and to the modern day has released eight well-regarded albums which all beganwith this self-titled one from 2006, the year after the band's inception. While the rather limitedworld of jazz metal usually results in a metal band such as Atheist or Cynic coming from the metalworld and incorporating jazz chords and styles into its mix, PANZERBALLETT has been much moiregrounded on the jazz side of the equation with a virtuosic saxophone being delivered by Alexandervon Hagke along with its Messhugah inspired djent-metal approach. Despite being an exclusively instrumental band that was inspired by not only the intricate jazzdisplays of The Weather Report, Tribal Tech and Herbie Hancock but also the avant-prog workouts ofacts such as Mats Morgan and the wily math metal antics of Meshuggah and similarly minded metal.While the band would eventually incorporate prominent technically infused covers of pop acts such asABBA and others like Frank Zappa and even theme songs from TV shows such as The Simpsons, on thiseponymous debut PANZERBALLETT sticks to its own original compositions that feature less of thecreative whimsy that would highlight them amongst the world of progressive jazz fusion metal. Thisalbum is more of a no nonsense declaration that a new band is in town and this ain't your parents'jazz fusion any longer which in 2006 was still somewhat of a novelty in the world of metal (andfrankly still is!)Noticeably less metallic than its future releases, album #1 focuses more on a staccato driven jazzmetal effect that offers intricately complex compositions exuding jazz flavors and melodic workoutswhile adding the heft of guitar grunge to offer the contrast. While the guitar soloing is in actionhere, it's not to the level that Zerfeld would unleash on future releases. The opening "Zerfunk"pretty much sets the stage with a funky bass groove that finds labyrinthine jazz explorations lacedwith guitar chord prominence and occasional soloing prowess however in the end the album soundsfairly uniform and lacks that wild explorative energy that the band would become famous for both inthe studio and in a live setting. This album features nine well constructed tracks but lacks thecreative mojo that would soon take root beginning with the band's second release which would debutthe whacky jazz metal interpretations of totally diverse cover songs only in instrumental form.Overall not a bad debut as PANZERBALLETT definitely delivers a unique take on the world of jazzmetal that focuses first and foremost on the jazz aspects with a prominent saxophone presence andkeeping the metallic furor at bay. While the metal would become a stronger playing card on futurerelease and the two styles would become more integrated, this self-titled debut is by no means awasted effort as it generates a wild and exhilarating ride through metal-tinged jazz-funk-fusionwith blistering technical workouts decorated with intimate softer jazz oriented passages, a traitwhich would only diversify on future releases. A great beginning if not the band's primo offering.This album is bogged down by the tracks being too similar and not enough creative mojo had yet beenmustered up to make a completely compelling album as one would experience on the electrifying albumssuch as "Hart Genossen von Abba bis Zappa." Still though this album really rocks the jazz unlike anyother.3.5 rounded down
items._genre: jazz metal / math metal / progressive fusion / instrumental
items._cn_summary: 这张2006年的同名首作由德国吉他手Jan Zehrfeld领衔，以纯器乐编制将爵士融合与金属结合。与一般从金属出发嫁接爵士元素的乐队不同，Panzerballett以萨克斯为核心展开即兴探索，底色偏向爵士，再叠加重型吉他失真与节奏切分。评论将乐队置于Weather Report、Tribal Tech的精致爵士传统与Meshuggah式数学金属的交汇处，强调其迷宫般的复杂结构与功能性贝斯线条。首作风格相对克制，金属感弱于后续作品，少了日后翻唱ABBA、辛普森一家主题曲的怪诞趣味。九首曲目构造扎实但整体听感略显均匀，被视为乐队确立方向的开端之作。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — Continuing as one of Sweden's most adventurous prog bands that emerged in the fertile musical fieldsof the 1970s, SAMLA MAMMAS MANNA followed up its already eclectic roster of three crazy complex yetaccessibly zany and playful albums with its fourth curveball release which served as a collaborativeeffort with American composer Gregory Allan Fitzpatrick. Although born in California, USA,Fitzpatrick arrived in Finland in 1966 before falling for neighboring Sweden where he moved to in1967 and then commenced to collaborate with bands such as The Quints which became Atlantic Ocean aswell as world fusion acts like Handgjort. For this collaboration he made his debut as chief composer leaving the Rockers In Opposition SAMLAMAMMAS MANNA as the backing band. The musical style is very much reminiscent of the SAMLA's seamlessflow of quirky Zappa-esque whimsy accompanied by fret-scorching avant-prog angularity. Thecumbersome title GREGORY ALLAN FITZPATRICK'S SNORUNGARNAS SYMFONI served as the SAMLA's fourth albumand was released in 1976. In addition to the SAMLA's handling the usual prog duties that coveredkeyboards, guitar, bass and drums, the album featured two guests that added touches of saxophone andtrumpet. FITZPATRICK served exclusively as the composer, arranger and conductor and played noinstruments.The album is broken up into four moments with the introductory "Forsta Satsen" (1st Movement)providing the lengthiest time run. While sounding a bit different than what SAMLAS fans would cometo expect, the way the music flow is generated is familiar territory for anyone entranced by themagic of "M�ltid" or "Klossa Knapitalet" however FITZPATRICK keeps the band on a leash and only letsthem go bat[&*!#] crazy when he commands them to do so therefore the album feels a lot more restrainedand retains an unmistakable serious approach and likewise eschews the over prog excesses of itspredecessor. As with the SAMLA's own solo works, this album encapsulates a lot of the Swedish folkhistory in the melodic touches as well as polka-like marches and traditional festival type anthems.Overall it's a very interesting next development for the SAMLAS who took their own sound to itslogical conclusion with the previous release. This allowed the band to exist in a more orchestratedtype of scenario which they pulled off quite well with nothing sounding forced or dumbed down in theleast bit. It's a successful collaboration that allows the strengths of both parties to be expressedwithout anything sounding watered down. The fun festive jocularity of the SAMLAS is very much intactwhile the compositional style offers a completely different take on the SAMLA's unique avant-gardeapproach to their feisty Rock In Opposition. While not as enthralling as the band's first threealbums, this is still very much a fascinating a excellent slice of folk-fueled avant-prog only withjazz and symphonic touches.
items._cn_summary: 这是瑞典前卫摇滚乐队Samla Mammas Manna与美籍作曲家Gregory Allan Fitzpatrick的合作专辑。Fitzpatrick担任主创、编曲和指挥，不演奏任何乐器，而乐队作为执行乐团，在键盘、吉他、贝斯和鼓的常规编制之外加入萨克管和小号客座。专辑分为四个乐章，开篇乐章篇幅最长，整体风格延续乐队标志性的怪诞气质与坦帕式戏谑，但因作曲家主导，乐队被约束在更克制、严肃的框架内。作品融入瑞典民间旋律元素、波卡式进行曲与传统节庆旋律，营造出管弦乐化的编配效果。Fitzpatrick的作曲风格为乐队原有的前卫抵抗摇滚带来全新视角，同时保留了其节庆式的欢乐基调，形成爵士与交响元素交融的民谣驱动型前卫作品。

items.body:
Debut EP from Seaoul psych-pop outfit LEENALCHI.

"Today we bring you LEENALCHI.

As Brian Eno told us last week, “Leenalchi has changed the way I think about music, dancing and Korea. I have never heard anything quite like this.”

There’s so much to say to you about this amazing band—but what will get you to listen?

Is it that they play addictive psych pop? Or that they sound like animals talking to each other over tripped out bass lines?

They have a new single out today called HERE COMES THAT CROW, which, like all of Leenalchi’s songs, is a chopped and screwed version of a pansori tale (a traditional form of storytelling from the 17th century). Based on a story about the warlord Cao Cao, the song is an allegory about life’s precariousness.

The band wrote a poem to explain:

Doyung doyung goes the small boat floating down the river. Whether the chased or the chaser, no one can stop—just beneath the boards lies the underworld!

도용도용은 작은 배가 물위를 떠가는 모양을 그린 말이다. 조조도 조자룡도 쫓기는 자도 쫓는 자도 멈출수는 없다. 판자때기 아래가 저승인데 어느 누가 멈춰 설 수 있겠는가!"
items._genre: psychedelic pop / pansori / experimental / Korean traditional
items._cn_summary: 韩国首尔乐队 LEENALCHI 发行首张 EP，将十七世纪传统说唱艺术板索里（pansori）与迷幻流行、迷幻贝斯线相融合。主打单曲以三国时代曹操故事为底，隐喻生命的无常与脆弱：追逐者与被逐者无人能停，船板之下即是彼岸。整张作品将传统叙事节奏打碎重组，以慢速扭曲（chopped and screwed）手法处理人声，形成动物般的对话质感。Brian Eno 评价该乐队改变了他对音乐、舞蹈与韩国的认知。作品在传统与现代之间搭建桥梁，文本层面延续板索里的诗词结构，音乐层面则偏向迷幻电子实验，对追求世界音乐与前卫融合的听众具有较强吸引力。

items.body:
Recorded in 1991, 'Rise' sweeps up all known recorded material from A.R. Kane's Rudy Tambala and Cranes vocalist Alison Shaw, aka inrain, compiling a classic 7” for Rough Trade with additional, previously unreleased tracks. It’ll no doubt provide many with a first introduction to a prescient project by two scene legends, delving into shoegaze, dub, electro and trip-hop refractions of the highest order. It's the most essential Music From Memory release in a hot minute, crucial listening for all A.R Kane obsessives (that should be all of you) or anyone into Seefeel, Locust, Zurich.

For someone for whom Cranes' ‘Tomorrow's Tears’ and A.R Kane’s ‘Lolita’ are two absolute foundational texts, this reissue is basically something like a holy grail. Back in 1991, inrain appeared on Rough Trade's Singles Club series with a brief but brilliant 7" that sounded as if it'd been beamed in from another planet. A.R. Kane had already broken the mold, but these three tracks juxtaposed Shaw's dreamy vocals with dubby, spacious electronics and shimmering guitars in a way that wouldn't really rise to prominence until years later. Music From Memory do the heavy lifting here, remastering that original 7" from the original DAT tapes and adding the extra track 'Biology' and an alternate version of 'Sleep' to bump up the package. 

It's those original tracks that have us by the throat - we really can't believe they've been so slept on over the years. '...And Julie Rose' sounds like it should have been picked up for a Duophonic release a decade later, while 'Sleep' completely pre-empts Seefeel's 'More Like Space EP' that wouldn't appear for another couple of years. 

Prophetic, brilliant stuff.
items._genre: shoegaze / dream pop / dub / electronic / trip-hop
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了1991年A.R. Kane成员Rudy Tambala与Cranes主唱Alison Shaw合作项目inrain的全部录音，以7寸单曲为核心并补充未发行曲目。音乐将Shaw空灵的嗓音与dub质感电子节拍、闪烁的吉他层叠结合，呈现出一种漂浮于太空般的声响质感。评论指出其创作远超时代——'Sleep'一曲实际上预见了数年后Seefeel的出现，'And Julie Rose'则呼应了Duophonic厂牌后来的美学取向。Music From Memory厂牌从原始DAT磁带完成母带处理，使这些被长期忽视的声音重见天日。A.R. Kane解构流行结构的实验遗产与Cranes冷冽梦幻的特质在此交汇，形成融合shoegaze、dub与电子的独特文本。

items.body:
Returning to Hands in the Dark for the third time, French artist Sylvain Bombled slides into kosmische territory on 'Finis Terrae', guided by the inclement weather on Ushant.

There's an impressive amount of territory covered on 'Finis Terrae'. The album was recorded last winter, when Bombled was hold up on Ushant, an island on the western end of the English channel. Struck by the natural beauty of his surroundings, even while the weather chopped and changed around him, Bombled wrote these five pieces to reflect his lived reality, translating the movement into music. On opener 'Herminia', it's with 'Zuckerzeit'-like drum and synth sequences that Bombled leads into dizzy trance territory in the final act, but the clouds shift on 'Plight' and the producer slows things down, splicing field recordings into his sloshing synths and ferric, BoC-inspired beats. 

There's light in the distance on the hopeful 'She Builds Myths' and on the title track, Bombled pulls out all the stops, fabricating an EDM-inspired slow electro anthem that'll surely speak to anyone who's ever wondered what a collaboration between Johnny Jewel, Mogwai and Ulrich Schnauss might sound like.
items._cn_summary: 法国艺术家Sylvain Bombled在Ushant岛冬季驻留期间创作了这张专辑，五首作品以kosmische为底色，融合田野录音与合成器序列。开篇'Herminia'以类似Cluster《Zuckerzeit》的鼓机与合成器序列切入，将听觉引向恍惚的恍惚状态；'Plight'则转向慢速，引入田野录音与受BoC启发的磁带质感的节拍；'She Builds Myths'以明亮的音色带来希望感；同名曲试图构建一首EDM灵感的慢速电子颂歌，融合Johnny Jewel式的暗潮质感、Mogwai的后摇情绪与Ulrich Schnauss的梦幻合成器层次。整体以自然环境为素材，将天气变化与情绪流动转化为电子声响的流动，在迷幻电子与氛围之间游走。

items.body:
London/Helsinki label Cold Blow map the subliminal links of early ‘90s electro, techno and its backroom, downbeat offshoots thru a plethora of tunes recorded ’92-’99 by the likes of Stasis, 2000 And One, CiM, all displaying how they translated Detroit techno intricacies and new age ambient soul for UK & EU bodies in motion, or those eaten by sofas.

“Across eight carefully selected slices of starry-eyed machine soul, Cold Blow presents an exquisite tour through backroom techno and downtempo electro. With a focus on thematic flow and an immersive listening experience, the London-based label explores works from leading lights of the 1990s and previously unreleased cuts that celebrate the human heart that can be discovered in synthetic sound practices.

The development of techno in the 1990s saw the music evolve in different directions across the world. From the expressive blueprint laid out by the Detroit pioneers, a wide range of tempos and energies emerged. Techno's evocative synthesis and intricate drum machine programming was especially potent for deeper explorations away from the dancefloor.

Documents Of Different Reality casts back to when technology was steering quantum leaps in communication and creativity and the future was shot through with naive optimism. It was also a time when the media and industry hadn't caught up with the music to box it into distinct categories. As such, there's a sense of creative freedom that informs the older tracks on the album, from 2000 And One and Sandy Huner's (originally as Pure) sparkling example of early Dutch techno to London-based LA Synthesis' detailed take on braindance and the majestic night sky vision of cult legend Stasis.

There's also space for rare, late 90s machine funk from Icelandic outlier Thor alongside Connective Zone's charmingly fractured bleep dream and a more contemporary offering from Barcelona-based duo Permutation. Meanwhile Mind Control and CiM both capture the spirit of stylistic fusion with twitchier rhythms that take influence from hardcore and jungle as much as techno.

With an atmospheric through-line of melancholic pads and harmonious leads, this small but perfectly formed collection naturally follows on from previous, equally thought-out compilations on Cold Blow, and adds a distinct perspective on the history and continuing legacy of pioneering early ambient techno.”
items._cn_summary: Cold Blow厂牌策划的这张合辑聚焦1990年代初至末期的电子音乐场景，收录了Stasis、2000 And One、CiM等艺人在1992至1999年间创作的作品，追溯那个科技跃进与未来主义乐观情绪交织的年代。合辑呈现出底特律技术派对欧洲乐手的深远影响，从荷兰早期的技术舞曲到冰岛艺人Thor的稀有机器放克，涵盖braindance、downtempo electro与ambient techno等多个分支。整体氛围以忧郁的pad铺垫与和声化旋律为主导，编排注重主题连贯性与沉浸式聆听体验。Hardcore与jungle的节奏特征也被纳入，与传统techno形成风格融合。合辑延续了厂牌一贯的策展思路，为早期ambient techno的历史脉络与延续提供了一份兼具深度与可听性的回顾。

items.body:
The Sultans of Sludge slang a definitive label debut for Sub Pop, bringing their singular sound to roost on a legendary label local to their origins in the US north west, whose rugged landscapes fed directly into the LP’s formidably primal concentration of dualistic energies

Hailing some 30 years since Sunn O)))’s formation, their eponymous 10th studio album reckons with forces of nature - time and space, dark and light - for 80 minutes of air-shuddering pressure limning epic, craggy vistas from a thick haar of distortion. Subtly enlivened with field recordings made in forests near Bear Creek Studios, Woodinville, Washington, where O’Malley says they would “go hiking and be out in the woods, spend time outdoors”, the resulting six-part sequence sees the duo drill down to fundamentals with an absorbing sense of purpose and telepathically-attuned intuition. A notable dearth of other contributors also means it’s one of their truest statements as a duo; just Stephen O’Malley & Greg Anderson howling into the wilds on all instrumentation, from trusted axes to keys and electro-acoustic sorcery. 

At this point, not to labour the arboreal metaphors, but it may take a certified guide to see the wood for the trees in Sunn O))) lands, such is the uniquely coherent sprawl of their sound at 30 years up to the hilt in atonal rock doom. Our hair’s not long enough to lay claim as spirit guides, but after 23 years of bearing witness to them live, and ingesting most of their LPs, we can say this side is wholly emblematic of their radical steez. Between the two 18 minute totems of a ‘XXANN’ laced with location recording of running water at tender points, and a ‘Mindrolling’ monstered with claw-handed riffs, they take it to typically stare-down levels of intensity with the sustained threat of ‘Does Anyone Hear Like Venom?’, and billowing sheets of subharmonic distortion harnessed in ‘Everett Moses’. Closer ‘Glory Black’ is, however, a sort of sore thumb with a relatively conventional riff progression and rising banks of silvery wheeze that collapse into keys and field recordings, hearkening most closely to the duo’s precedents and NW peers in the Sub Pop roster, Earth, or even another touchstone, Black Sabbath, at their most strung out. 

Heavy as your life.
items._genre: drone doom / drone metal / experimental ambient / field recording
items._cn_summary: Sunn O))) 的第十张录音室专辑以乐队同名形式发行，是他们在 Sub Pop 厂牌的首作，时长约 80 分钟，共六个章节。整张专辑延续了乐队标志性的极端泥浆金属风格，但更加强调二人组合的纯粹性——Stephen O'Malley 与 Greg Anderson 亲自操持所有乐器，从吉他到键盘再到原声电子实验。专辑在华盛顿州 Bear Creek 工作室附近的森林中进行户外徒步时收录了大量田野录音，包括流水声与自然环境音，这些素材被穿插于极端失真与次低音音墙之间。曲目如 'XXANN' 与 'Mindrolling' 各长约 18 分钟，构成对峙的双柱；'Everett Moses' 运用次谐波失真营造压迫感；终曲 'Glory Black' 则以相对传统的 riff 推进收尾，暗流涌动。整张作品聚焦于时间与空间、黑暗与光明等自然力量的辩证，低频与静态张力贯穿始终。

items.body:
Lush, loosey-goosey psych-house trips by Jeremy Castillo & Pascual Martinez’ duo, ¿Donedos, ruffly jammed with hardware on a mazy swaggering flex somewhere between DJ Milo’s Nature Boy and Beautiful Swimmers​...

"¿DONDEDOS is young dude/unc duo hailing from the Mission. Pascual Martinez (young dude) and BPT head honcho Jeremy Castillo (unc) have spent the last few years in the stu, cooking up this deep fried, groovin' 4 tracker. Fans of 2011-16 LIES and Future Times releases, “Biology" era Young Marco, Juju and Jordash, and the Wah Wah Wino crew are in for a treat.

In an era where literally every aspect of dance music is overly programmed and manicured, ¿DONDEDOS take a massively refreshing approach marked by true experimentation. All drums were recorded on the Roland R8, and the melodies were live played with a loose, jammy feel not felt on many electronic 12" releases in 2026. They're a jam band baby!!!!! 

The fun starts with "Drifting Nowhere," a fried oddball deep house record with one of the year's most infectious basslines. Be ready for it to be on a loop in your brain long after the track has stopped playing.

2nd track "Dies Varos" was described by BPT fam Izaak from Loveshadow as sounding like "part of the Mediterranean touching Mexico." Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh. (that was a deep relaxed sigh, not a scream for once!!!)

"Music for Patios" sounded pretty good on a walk and not on a patio so, just FYI, only a suggestion not a requirement. 

Ender Noche Caminando features Diego Herrera (AKA Suzanne Kraft) on sax. In Jeremy's own words, this track features "oddball dancehall drums on the R8 with 80s synth pop dub melodic sensibilities." "
items._genre: psych-house / lo-fi electronic / live jam / dub
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由来自旧金山Mission区的双人组合¿DONDEDOS制作，所有鼓声均通过Roland R8硬件录制，旋律部分强调现场即兴的松散质感，在当下过度编程化的舞曲场景中呈现出罕见的实验态度。四首曲目风格各异：开篇曲以慵懒的迷幻house律动配以年度最洗脑的贝斯线；第二曲融合地中海与墨西哥式的地中海-拉丁跨界意象；第三曲名字虽叫"庭院音乐"，实际更适合散步聆听；终曲邀请Suzanne Kraft演奏萨克斯，将八十年代合成器流行与dub回响叠加于怪趣的dancehall鼓点之上。整体制作采用全硬件即兴方式完成，这种脱离DAM的演奏方式在当代电子乐中极为少见。

items.body:
More gold from Japan’s endlessly curious Em Records, this time shining a light on southern Californian post-minimalist composer Jeff Bruner, highlighted by Visible Cloaks’ Spencer Doran and bringing together stunning works spanning 1978 - 2020 for mbira, calypso dub and fretless gut-string banjo - huge tip FFO Richard Crandell, Terry Riley, Roland P. Young, Takoma, General Strike, Daniel Lentz.

"I first came across Jeff's mysterious "Reggae Foes" 45 in the mid-2000s at the legendary Logos book/record store in Santa Cruz, California (RIP) - the kind of generic sleeve and label that gives you nothing more than a font and some scant shards of text to go by (luckily this text was "A Flying Saucer Came Down and Burnt My Baby's Neck"). What I heard upon bringing it home felt like some kind of alternate-timeline post punk calypso, unknowingly adjacent to the deconstructions occurring at the Black Ark or in David Cunningham's early productions. When I finally talked to Jeff many years later, I was even more surprised to learn that he was also entrenched in southern California's post-minimalist composer scene in the 1970s alongside many of my compositional heroes, work which this compilation presents for the first time. Couldn't think of a better place for it to be transmitted from than EM!" (Spencer Doran/Visible Cloaks)

Four Corners is a compilation that showcases the various facets of American West Coast minimalist composer Jeff Bruner, with pieces from the 1970s to the 2020s displaying a cohesive set of aesthetic concerns. Bruner has a kinship with the composers Harold Budd and Daniel Lentz, the latter being a mentor to Bruner, and one can hear a relationship with the music of other minimal/post-minimal composers such as John Adams and Terry Riley. 1979's "Magic Mbira", a key piece in this collection, particularly highlights a Riley-esque element, and with its skillful use of tape delays reminiscent of Lenz's cascading echo system. Bruner and his mbira piece also have musical affinities with Roland P. Young and his classic Isophonic Boogie Woogie, in their shared melodic and structural concerns, as well as a desire to perform their compositions in a wider range of performance spaces, away from traditional recital halls. Another side of Bruner is revealed in the funhouse-mirror "Reggae Foes", a deconstructionist post-punk calypso-reggae tune and skewed Black Ark filtered through Cunningham/Toop's General Strike. The remaining two pieces are melancholy beauties of solo instrumentation: "Cold Rain and Snow" is a fretless gut-string banjo re-imagining of an American folk song; "Remembrance in a Pale Room" is a lovely piano piece dedicated to Lentz. Bruner has built upon a tradition, altering and adding to it with his individual vision, giving us this collection of intriguing and beautiful music. Available on CD/Vinyl/Digital, with E/J liner notes by Jeff Bruner, rare photos & the score for "Magic Mbira"."
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑梳理了南加州作曲家Jeff Bruner横跨1978至2020年的创作轨迹，呈现其在后简约主义谱系中的独特位置。核心曲目1979年的《Magic Mbira》使用非洲拇指琴，结合磁带延迟手法，呼应Terry Riley的循环结构与Daniel Lentz的级联回声系统。另类时间线的后朋克卡里索普如《Reggae Foes》，以解构手法过滤Black Ark式的雷鬼制作，与General Strike的扭曲美学形成对照。晚期作品转向内省：《Cold Rain and Snow》以无品肠弦班卓琴重新演绎美国民歌，《Remembrance in a Pale Room》则是献给导师Lentz的钢琴小品。Bruner继承并改写了Harold Budd、Lentz以来的西海岸简约传统，其作品同时面向传统音乐厅之外的多元演出空间。Em Records的日版发行赋予这张跨年代合辑契合的传播语境。

items.body:
Superb late night jazz-jungle fusion by recombinant specialist Antonio Marini’s cult unit, Healing Force Project, coolly nodding to Miles Davis via DJ Shadow, Pat Thomas and 4Hero or Peshay, in a signature, roving but holistic, richly visionary style

His first bow on Berlin’s Evighet label frames Marini deep in a mode of smouldering nocturnal substance that’s consistently snagged lugs since early turns for Acido, Berceuse Heroique and Firecracker identified them as one to keep a watch on in the early 2010s. In its shadow-strafing turns of low down Mo Wax beats, noirish dub touches and rudely loose but disciplined jungle ballistics it all feels like their most collected and thematically thorough work - dare we say even definitive - pursuing classic dragons with a playthru flow that’s a real pleasure to follow.

The eight tracks can’t help but remind us to being a young DJ Shadow fan in the late ‘90s/early ‘00s, and getting hard turned-off his music when reading him outright dismiss jungle/D&B in an interview. Across ‘Unholy Magnetic’, Healing Force Project almost imagines what Shadow could have sounded like if he embraced the ‘nuum, or took cues from Pat Thomas’ ‘New Jazz Jungle: Remembering’ (1997) at the time, as manifest in its eight cuts of deeply smoked out swerve and timeless verve. 

Louche spectres of prime era Mo Wax and ‘On the Corner’ Miles hang out on the slow, dubbed swanger ‘Where’s Doctor Who’, setting up a fleet-hooved suite prone to flash ruder fangs of jungle like Source Direct in spy jazz mode with ‘Cerebral Upload’, and peshay’s debonaire charms in ‘Cathode Rays’, while ‘The Groover’ tests out a sort of unchronic dubstep-jungle sound. But it’s most impressive in the way he tempers those bits with the downstrokes of simmered pressure in ‘The Ways of Golding Space & Flying’ hinting at 4 Hero’s ‘Parallel Universe’, or totally comes into his own on the drill-jungle fusion ‘Playing Tabla and Smoking Weed With Aliens’, thru the 11 mins of recursive dub to ‘Infinite (D[ub]rop.’
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将爵士灵魂与丛林舞曲基因重新编织成八段深夜低光旅程。制作人Antonio Marini以Mo Wax时代的低保真鼓机为骨架，叠加dub的暗黑空间感与jungle的碎裂鼓组节奏，形成介于DJ Shadow的暗色调hip-hop与4Hero、Pat Thomas的nuum美学之间的独特场域。专辑以缓慢dub化的弦乐段落铺陈氛围，随后通过'Source Direct式的间谍爵士'段落释放jungle的锐利动能，最后在11分钟的递归dub构造中收束。整体制作理念强调流动的整体感与主题连贯性，追求跨界融合的完整叙事体验。

French-born, London-based composer and musician Pascal Bideau takes this as his central premise on a new album of intrepid sonic exploration that delights in the sensation of being somewhere you’ve never... more
items.body:
New LP from French-born, London-based composer and musician Pascal Bideau via Tonal Union.

"Cartographers and US multinational technology corporations might think they’ve mapped out most of our big, beautiful blue planet, and yet there’s always more to discover if you know where to look. French-born, London-based composer and musician Pascal Bideau takes this as his central premise on a new album of intrepid sonic exploration that delights in the sensation of being somewhere you’ve never been before. ‘Terra Incognita’ invites us to seven faraway sonic imaginariums fusing global and spiritual jazz with life affirming minimalism into a hypnotic, polyrhythmic odyssey.

This time, the albums’ sound palette is more vibrant, earthy and abundant, drawing inspiration from the radiating optimism and high-energy sources heard in Afrobeat, Highlife and Electronic Afro-pop music, sounding looser, free and primarily interested in raw sensations. Antithetical to the precise ostinatos and gamelan patterns of the acclaimed debut ‘Fleeting Future’ (2022) and ‘Lines’ (2023). Terra Incognita, then, is a hybrid blend of traditional music and modern electronics, a trip into the unknown that ambulates freely, taking pleasure in its repetitions and never staying still. Bideau suggests this unmarked territory could be as much a fantasyland as it is a transportive journey into the inner self."
items._genre: jazz / minimalism / afrobeat / electronic / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是法国出生的伦敦作曲家Pascal Bideau的第三张作品，以"未知的疆域"为概念，将全球爵士与精神爵士与充满生命力的简约主义融合为催眠式的复合节奏旅程。相较于前两张专辑中精准的固定音型与加美兰模式，这张作品的音色更为鲜活、朴实且丰盈，从非洲节拍、高life以及电子非洲流行乐中汲取养分，呈现出更松散、自由且注重原始感官体验的状态。作品在传统音乐与现代电子之间自由游走，重复中蕴藏变化，既是幻想之地的描绘，也是通往内在自我的旅程。厂牌Tonal Union为独立小众厂牌，整体内容质量较高且具备明确的跨界融合特征。

items.body:
A note from J.WLSN.

"In late 2024 my good friend Liam Keenan and I recorded a short session with our friend David Akerman at his studio Lost Sound in Marrickville. We had been working as art and music curators at a major art museum in Sydney, Australia. We both make music separately but had neglected making a record together for too long.

Country/ The County is the first of our combined love of all things longform, expansive, distorted and it is filled with reverberations. Built on subtle guitars, modular synth pads and sample-based loops, the record is us exploring our experience growing up in similar regional and rural settings.

The music represents parts of the country in Western Sydney and further west in regional NSW in Australia where we both grew up across different periods of time. These places are drifting plains, scowling mountains and at times, simply, rolling suburbia. The music is a score of sorts for these meshing places, a way of us decoding these shared geographies, outside of time. You could almost say, it's a music of place, out of time."
items._cn_summary: 专辑由J.WLSN与Liam Keenan于2024年末在悉尼Marrickville的Lost Sound工作室合作录制，融合细颗粒吉他、模块合成器铺底与采样循环，呈现出绵长、扩散且失真的声场。音乐灵感来自两位创作者在西悉尼及新南威尔士州乡村地区的成长记忆，试图以声音还原漂移的平原、阴郁山脉与郊区景观，将地理经验转化为时间之外的听觉文本。整体定位为氛围与实验音乐的跨界之作，强调空间感与回响美学，以"场所之乐"为核心概念探索个人地理与音乐创作的关联。

items.body:
Arvo Pärt has become something of a yardstick by which contemporary sacred music has been measured, and 'Alina' is arguably his most loved and imitated piece of work. 

Für Alina was first performed in Tallinn in 1976, and has become one of Pärt’s most-loved and widely appreciated works - regarded by many as an early, defining example of his signature tintinnabuli style. In the years since its release, Pärt has become the most performed living composer in the world, his approach to religious music seeping deep into our cultural landscape, from the avant garde to the mainstream.

Rendered with nothing more than piano and violin, this definitive ECM version from 1999 features Vladimir Spivakov, Sergej Bezrodny, Dietmar Schwalke and Alexander Malter providing alternate versions, handpicked by Pärt himself from recordings that were originally several hours long. It’s a masterclass in simplicity; an almost painfully beautiful rendering of emotional landscapes that, in the wrong hands, could have (and has, on many occasions, by so many) turned to schmaltz.
items._cn_summary: Arvo Pärt 的《Alina》收录了其标志性的钟鸣式（tintinnabuli）风格代表作《Für Alina》，该曲于1976年在塔林首演，被视为他极简手法与宗教精神融合的早期典范。1999年的ECM版本以钢琴与小提琴为核心，由Spivakov、Bezrodny、Schwalke与Malter演绎多个由Pärt亲自筛选的替代版本，原素材来自数小时的录音。专辑在极简的乐器配置中探索情感空间的纵深，仅凭两条旋律线的交错与共鸣，制造出克制却深沉的聆听体验。Pärt的宗教音乐语言已渗透当代文化，从先锋领域延伸至主流层面，但此版以近乎透明的质感保持了原作的精神内核，避免了感伤化的处理。整张专辑是对极简主义创作逻辑的一次经典呈现。

items.body:
An all-too-brief but seductive teaser for Luca Durán’s debut studio album ‘Killing Mariposas’, benefiting from the atmospheric pressure of Kelman Duran and Gavsborg’s dub poetry.

Hailing a full LP on the horizon, starring other guests Iceboy_Violet, Debit, Rosa Pistola, BÉBE YANA, Kamohelo, kacha & SAM-E, in late summer ’26, the 2 mins of ‘Lejanía’ calls to mind the wist of Sam Kidel’s ‘Disruptive Muzak’ swept out to warmer shores of heat-pitched melody with sublime sense of deferred gratification.
items._genre: experimental electronic / dub poetry / ambient fusion
items._cn_summary: 《Lejanía》是卢卡·杜兰首张录音室专辑《Killing Mariposas》的先行单曲，仅两分钟，却以延展的旋律线条与延迟满足的听感营造出沉浸氛围。制作层面融入凯尔曼·杜兰与加夫斯博格的dub poetry诗性朗诵，使声音层次在文本与电子之间流动，呈现空气压力式的氛围张力。乐评将其与萨姆·基德尔的《Disruptive Muzak》相提并论，指向一种被推向温暖海岸线的失意诗意，在高音域旋律上保留着热带热度的同时不放弃结构的克制。唱片计划于2026年夏末发行完整长篇，参与者还包括Iceboy_Violet、Debit、Rosa Pistola等多位跨领域合作者，意味着这张作品将在电子基底上编织社群化的声音网络。整体听感介于环境音与有调旋律之间，文本与声响的关系被作为核心结构来处理。

items.body:
A note from Oliver and James

"Shaking off the uneasy depths of Lapsed Gasps took a minute (those mix sessions were intense!). Oliver and I knew we’d like the record that followed to let in some light. Not much light, but enough to differently illuminate the darkened corners Push For Night prefers to inhabit. So we shifted the stone slab covering the conceptual entrance to the sarcophagal room that contains the idea of PFN, just a little, and the crepuscular light inside the room changed. The shadows behaved differently, sounded differently. The textures, sizes, shapes, and acoustics of our weird space altered. How can we interpret the shadows’ song and dance differently this time? In these subtle changes in perception there lies a wealth of things to investigate, to peer into, to be afraid of, to be excited by… That said, our writing process doesn’t involve too much premeditated verbal back and forth. We tend to start lobbing sessions at each other and a path inevitably clears.

In this case, and in no small part, the clearing of the path of That Porous Line begins with the contributions of my longtime sonic comrade David Daniell. The two pieces Oliver and I made with David are the earliest in the sessions that would become this record. He brought, for lack of a better word, a beauty - a gentle, organic beauty - that ultimately reoriented PFN toward a sense of the melodic and of spontaneity. We moved away from programming sequences, generative patches, and atomizing every sound source via heavy processing. We lightened the gloom a bit. It might sound naive, but we touched instruments again; we played guitars and basses and keyboards and percussion, fingers on metal wire and wood. We reveled in less-than-perfect real time performance, and documented it as such. There is a certain lightness to that.

Don’t get me wrong, That Porous Line is absolutely a collaged, flickering, chaotic, electro-acoustic record. The project is the project after all. Although our tomb-room isn’t fully hermetic (what is?), I think it is a place PFN will always reside. A total escape outside into harshly lit reality without mystery is fairly unappealing, for us anyway. Inside is personal, guarded from too much light; a dark terrarium of weird ghosts and peculiar shadows ripe for conjuring and harnessing in order to make them kick and howl in a way pleasing to us. Or at least be near enough to them to try and hear what they sing. That’s the motive. We decorate the cave, invite the specters to reveal a message, and try to capture something. Inside, cocooned in the semi-dark of our uncommon space, we bang our heads against the act of interpreting these shifty, chimeric, hidden sonic shadows. How big is it in here? How much further down can we go? Did something move in that corner over there? Can it touch us? Can we catch it? That’s where the fear is. That’s where the fun happens. That’s why we listen. That’s why we play."
items._genre: experimental electronic / electro-acoustic / dark ambient / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是That Porous Line继前作《Lapsed Gasps》之后的转型之作。两位主创Oliver与James在长期合作者David Daniell的吉他与原声乐器加入后，从程序化序列与过度处理转向触摸真实乐器、拥抱不完美的实时演奏，但仍保留了拼贴、闪烁、混沌的电声美学内核。专辑概念围绕一间半明半暗的地下墓室展开，创作者自比为召唤幽灵的洞穴居民，在昏暗与微光之间探寻声音的轮廓、形态与回响。专辑并无意完全逃离阴暗进入刺目现实，而是选择继续驻留于这个幽闭的个人空间，让那些难以捕捉的、变幻无常的暗影发声、踢踏、嚎叫。从沉重的程序化暗潮氛围转向带有一丝有机温度的电声实验，但内核依然深沉、幽闭、神秘。

items.body:
Mutual, leading prism-pushers Batu & Dozzy break fresh ground on duo debut ‘Exhale’, encompassing a spectra of tempos, moods & grooves in pursuit of elusive studio geists between Dozzy’s Rome facility and Batu’s peripatetic CPU.

Seeded in an ad hoc b2b DJ set at Draaimolen Festival, ’23, and cultivated over sessions at Dozzy’s hardware treasure trove in Rome, ‘Exhale’ naturally calibrates the two operators’ distinct visions on eight cuts teeming with detail and clean-hoofed for club use. Dozzy’s quarter century of obsessive, finely variegated techno tekkerz elide Batu’s signature offbeat syncopation and feel for texture within deceptively effortless designs that arguably transcend the sum of their parts. The results surely pin-point a dancefloor ideal of cyborganic sensuality and chromed out chronics that references the now, the future, while exerting mercurial sidespins on tried & tested forms.

In the artists’ own words: "It was interesting to see Omar interacting with my studio methods," explains Dozzy. "I know my machines very well. It was fun to do something out of my routine and use my machines in a different way to turn on Omar's ideas. There were a few things I was very excited to use, especially with someone who's an expert and used these instruments for a very long time," Batu reveals. "We tried lots of different tempos, different rhythmic patterns. I was excited by the direction we were taking, and getting so many ideas of where it could go."

In combination they generate a slew of rudely balanced equations, tentatively toeing glassy waters in the hyaline cavern of ‘Emergence’, locking into a swingeing Afro-acid churn on ’Spiral’, and stepping  to more angular, holographic techno on ‘Drift’, with nods to the nuance of mbalax-via-oingy boingy dubstep in ‘Off Axis’. And it only gets craftier in the 2nd half, diffusing the finest haze of cyberdub FX and palpitating subs on ‘Swarm’, training tendons to the tightest steppas techno on ‘Flicker’ and the title tune’s expansive trek, before seeing it off with a sublime update of early AI electronica in the shine-eyed swoon of ‘Bloom’.
items._cn_summary: Batu与Donato Dozzy的首张合作专辑诞生于2023年Draaimilen音乐节的一场即兴b2b演出，随后在Dozzy位于罗马的工作室中逐步完善。专辑涵盖八首作品，横跨多种节奏、情绪与律动，将Dozzy精微多变的技术处理与Batu标志性的切分律动和质感触感相融合。曲目在玻璃质感的氛围、酸性churn、棱角分明的全息techno以及dubstep节奏元素之间穿梭，后半段进一步探索cyberdub残响、低频脉冲与紧密steppas节奏。整体呈现出有机与机械交织的舞池美学，是两位制作人在脱离各自常规创作路径后的一次跨界碰撞。

items.body: “Ane Addhrai” means “go there” in the Salentino dialect, and that forward pull shapes Trevize‘s new single. Behind the name is Puglia producer and sound engineer Francesco Barletta, who threads folk roots through deep bass and electronic beats. On the track he builds a hypnotic groove from frame drums and ancestral percussion, the sound of a Salento ritual dropped onto a late-night dancefloor. The voice is Alessia Tondo, who first sang pizzica at six in her grandmother’s group, Mera Menhir, and in 2015 joined Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino, the band that has driven Salento’s pizzica revival since the 1970s. Her lyric takes the title literally: “go there” as a command to keep moving, written for music whose destination was never a fixed place. “Ane Addhrai” also titles the album Trevize releases after the summer. Stream and listen to the single HERE The post Daily Discovery: Trevize – Ane Addhrai appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: world fusion / electronic / folk / deep house
items._cn_summary: 来自意大利普利亚地区的制作人Francesco Barletta以Trevize为名，将萨伦托地区的传统民间音乐pizzica与电子节拍、深度贝斯相融合。单曲以框鼓和祖传打击乐器构建催眠律动，将古老的萨伦托仪式声音移植至深夜舞池场景。人声由Alessia Tondo担纲，她自幼在祖母的民间团体中演唱pizzica，后加入推动萨伦托音乐复兴的核心团体Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino。歌词以萨伦托方言中"去那里"的短语为标题，作为持续前行的指令，契合其本身不设固定目的地的音乐气质。该单曲为同名专辑先行曲，专辑将于夏季之后发行，是传统地方音乐与当代电子制作跨界结合的一次实践。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Considering the way Japanese percussionist Stomu Yamash'ta approached any new project, whether his duo with Masahiko Satoh, Come To The Edge, the music for the Red Buddha Theatre, or East Wind (alongside Soft Machine bassist Hugh Hopper and Brian Auger guitarist Gary Boyle). Freedom Is Frightening (a title that could not be more apt) opens with an extended organ passage; it is significant that Yamash'ta handled not only the drums but also the arrangements and composition, as his delicacy and meticulousness lend the work real depth.His wife, Hisako, played violin, while Brian Gascoigne handled synthesizers, keyboards, and vibraphone. Together, this quintet delivers over half an hour of progressive fusi�n, a sound that feels almost religious, were it not for moments bordering on the sacrilegious; when the drums kick in, accompanied by that provocative, distinctive bass, the music ventures into uncharted territory.After a cosmic, magical opening reminiscent of Hiromasa Suzuki's High-Flying, the music enters a psychedelic space-rock spiral where the guitar seems to dance with a chorus; then, as the second track kicks in, things go wild, evoking the Canterbury sound. This is "Rolling Nuns," where the keyboards provide a flashing "red alert" signal; over this, the guitar improvises sustained notes alongside a jazz-rock violin, never losing that sense of urgency, all underpinned by the bass. And just when it seems to be over... it starts all over again, much like the capacity to never cease being amazed. Towards the end, those soprano notes, reminiscent of King Crimson's Islands but here with a Japanese flavor, blend with the percussion so integral to Yamash'ta's natural tradition."Pine on the Horizon" begins with classic fusion tones... yet we soon notice an underlying Eastern texture in the violin, in the way certain notes slide sideways, like tree branches swaying in the wind within one of those meticulously manicured gardens where nothing is left to chance. And indeed, that is precisely the case.An almost psychedelic, yet funky, section, driven by the bass and followed by the keyboard, sweeps us up in a frenetic, infectious rhythm. And then... it's almost as if the Mahavishnu Orchestra were joining forces with Yes, rapid-fire scales... yet driven by a persistent, tenacious bassline and a guitar that's funky and at times distorted, then crisp again, plus an organ with an almost Santana-esque feel. The ending, featuring the bass and organ, really reminded me of Soft Machine, and the Canterbury scene once again. The members of this quintet truly inspired one another."Wind Words" begins tentatively with the violin and vibraphone, along with the novel inclusion of acoustic guitar, creating an intimate atmosphere to close out an otherwise extroverted album.That mystical vibe is infectious; the violin seems to drift away and return, bouncing within the confines of our ears. You can tell when there is real compositional craft at work, and Stomu Yamash'ta knew exactly what he was doing, whether in the music itself or in the naming of the tracks.
items._genre: jazz-rock / fusion / progressive / world fusion / psychedelic
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1973年日本鼓手STOMU YAMASH'TA领衔的五重奏前卫融合专辑，融合爵士摇滚、太空摇滚与东方色彩。他不仅担任打击乐手，更主导了整张作品的编曲与作曲，使作品展现出细腻而层次丰富的气质。小提琴与合成器、颤音琴的搭配营造出近乎宗教感的氛围，键盘段落以红色警报般的急切感贯穿，与吉他即兴形成持续张力。专辑后半段融入日本传统音阶的微妙滑音与东方意境，将凤尾丝竹般的精致与西方摇滚的爆发力并置。在快速段落中，键盘带有Santana式管风琴质感，吉他走funky与失真之间的棱线，结尾的低音线与键盘组合令人联想到Soft Machine的坎特伯雷场景。各成员之间激发出的化学反应是这张作品的核心。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — based on another play on word, Mosaismic is maybe a tad overselling the music on the disc - or anyother Ikarus album, for that matter. This is not to say that the band's music is bad or uneventful,but qualifying it of being "seismic" is too ambitious. Again presented in an all-cardboard mini-lpformat, this gives the object quite a nice appearance that gives you the envy to discover what'sinside, especially so that label-owner Nik Bartsch is behind the desk.As with the preceding Chronosome, their music still hovers a certain type of chamber Zeuhl or post-minimalist avant-jazz, with the main lead instrument being the male/female duo wordless vocals thatare mainly scatting, but in a very different galaxy of Ella and Satchmo. Actually, Anna Hisrchreplaced the departed Stefanie Suhner, but sonically, this doesn't change much, and the playfulnature of the voices remain intact. It wouldn't be that misleading to call Ikarus ' music instrumental, since the voices are totally used as another instrument.Having heard three of their four albums (so far), I can't choose one over the other, so it's up toyou to choose your entry point, as you can hear all of them on the Bandcamp page.
items._cn_summary: IKARUS的《Mosaismic》延续了Zeuhl流派的实验脉络，以室内乐编制与后极简主义手法构建独特的声场。男女双人无歌词人声被完全当作乐器使用，以类似拟声唱法的形式与乐器交织，形成一种介于声音艺术与自由爵士之间的质地。评论者认为专辑名中的"seismic"（地震般）一词过于夸张，音乐本身虽不至于平淡乏味，却也未达到石破天惊的程度。Anna Hirsch接替离队的Stefanie Suhner后，声音色彩几乎无变化，乐队的顽皮气质得以延续。作为厂牌主理人Nik Barttsch监制的作品，实体以迷你黑胶形式呈现，外观精致。评论者坦言已听过三张专辑却难以分出高下，建议听众通过Bandcamp自行选择切入点。

items.body: Blokkontroll Odin Na Odin Ratflak Kyiv-based one-man act Blokkontroll has been on a tear for the last year and a half, self-releasing a slew of digital EPs which immediately established the project’s read on stripped-down to the studs and wholly manic EBM. Even for those of us constantly searching out new records of exactly this style, it was difficult to keep track of the torrent of 160 BPM missives washing over us. Hell, even if you ordered the selection of tracks from the first three EPs pressed on vinyl by the always sharp Oráculo label for Blokkontroll’s first physical release, one or two more EPs had probably dropped by the time the vinyl got to your door. First full LP Odin Na Odin offers a sustained blast of those same sounds Blokkontroll’s been hammering for the past eighteen months. The core mix of sub-genres, component sounds, and moods Blokkontroll has been working with was laid out on day one. Rapid-fire pogoing kicks which blur the line between EBM and synthpunk, classic stabbing basslines, and anxiously shrieked vocals. That’s a formula that’s still very much in play on Odin Na Odin, with very little apart from slightly cleaner recordings and the addition of a few more leads and pads to flesh out the rhythmic programming distinguishing pensive opener “Opoznanie” from the project’s first release. The BPMs vary a bit and there’s some reach between a moodier cut like “Yad” which recalls classic dark electro and tracks like “Algoritm” which lean into punkier rhythms, but Blokkontroll’s commitment to a no-frills approach can also lead to a fair amount of repetition, especially once the uniform bass sound’s kicked around your head for a few tracks. By the time penultimate track “Sfera” rolls around its tonal similarity to “Gorizont” kept faking me out into expecting to hear the icy chimes from the latter, no matter how many times I spun the record. That closing track “einanzopO” is, quite literally, “Oponzanie” played backward could be read as a knowing nod to the uniformity of the release. It’s up to the listener to determine whether this extent of repetition is a feature or a bug, but one way or another there’s no denying the potency of Blokkontroll’s unremitting aggression even stretched out to a lengthy by their standards 37 minutes. The sound and style are blunt, direct, and packed full of the live-wire energy the style demands. If this is your first point of contact with the project, you’re getting a healthy slab of it; if you’ve already sampled Blokkontroll, you already know the score. Buy it. Odin Na Odin by Blokkontroll The post Blokkontroll, “Odin Na Odin” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 乌克兰基辅单人项目Blokkontroll的首张全长专辑延续了过去十八个月密集发行的数字EP脉络，以160 BPM的高强度节奏为核心。制作上采用极简手法，融合EBM与合成朋克的快速弹跳底鼓、经典尖锐贝斯线与焦躁刺耳的人声，辅以暗色电子的氛围切片。整体在纯粹黑暗电子的沉重段落与更偏朋克律动的曲目之间游走，但统一的贝斯音色和有限的变化导致重复感较为明显，末曲甚至以倒放开篇曲形成自我指涉。录音比早期作品稍显干净，补充了更多领奏与垫底音色来丰满节奏编排。该项目以不加修饰、直接猛烈的现场感著称，这张专辑在长度上有所延展，对熟悉其早期作品的听众而言并不提供太多新内容，但对首次接触的听众是一次集中的风格呈现。

items.body: Ayria is back with a new EP—one that could easily be described as a mini-album. “Vicious World” serves as a teaser for the upcoming full-length release, which Jennifer Parkin has already described as hard. The EP features five tracks, along with a remix of the title song by Seb Komor, who also handled the production. It is clear that a great deal has happened in Jennifer Parkin’s life, experiences she has channeled into both her music and lyrics. The result is a highly varied release. The hard-hitting title track is driven by a solid EBM bassline and elevated by Parkin’s charismatic vocals, while the Komor Kommando remix takes the aggression to an even higher level. In contrast, the remaining tracks are softer in tone and draw more heavily on the Electro-Pop elements that have become a hallmark of Ayria’s sound. These songs are expertly crafted, with occasional EBM touches adding depth and texture. At the same time, a sense of sensuality emerges throughout the EP, conveyed not only through the vocals but also through the rhythms and sonic landscapes. Parkin’s vocal delivery occasionally brings the ‘Queen of Pop’ to mind, making the inclusion of a Madonna cover feel entirely fitting. It may be a bold choice, but “Burning Up” proves to be a delightful rendition that genuinely lifts the spirits. Ayria plays to her strengths throughout ‘Vicious World’. Over the years, the Canadian artist has gained considerable experience and brought a new level of maturity to her songwriting. Combined with Seb Komor’s talents as a producer and arranger, the result is an EP that not only whets the appetite for the forthcoming album but also stands firmly on its own merits. (Rating:8). Listen to “Vicious World”: Vicious World by Ayria About Ayria Ayria is the Canadian futurepop and synthpop project of Jennifer Parkin, formed in Toronto in early 2003 after she left the EBM band Epsilon Minus. Parkin writes, sings, and produces the project, and has toured North America and Europe as well as Japan. Her albums include “Debris” (Alfa Matrix, 2003), “Flicker” (2005), “Hearts for Bullets” (2008), “Plastic Makes Perfect” (2013), “Paper Dolls” (2016), and “This Is My Battle Cry” (Artoffact Records, 2022). Released on Artoffact Records in 2026, the five-track “Vicious World” was produced by Sebastian Komor and sets up a forthcoming full-length.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP收录五首曲目及一首Seb Komor操刀的重混音版本，作为即将发行的全长专辑的预热。制作人Komor同时负责编曲与制作，标题曲以坚实的EBM贝斯线为骨架，Parkin的演唱充满力量感与个人魅力；同名重混音则进一步强化了攻击性。剩余曲目转向更柔和的电波流行方向，延续了艺术家标志性的合成器流行语汇，间或点缀的EBM元素为整体增添了层次与纵深感。整张作品散发出的感官气息贯穿于演唱、节奏与音景之中，Parkin的声线偶尔令人联想到流行乐坛的标志性人物，使得其中翻唱Madonna的作品显得恰如其分。作为一位经验丰富的加拿大创作人，Parkin在词曲创作上展现出愈发成熟的把控力，与制作人的合作使这张EP在铺垫新专辑的同时也具备了独立存在的完整价值。

items.body:
Perhaps it is from experiences like collaborating with increasingly popular techno act Shaun Moses within the live duo MO/SS or a natural progression, but Sanil Sudan is definitely dialling up the second word on dub techno, the genre he has dedicated his moniker Tyrell Dub Corp to, on 'MK618'.

The new EP by the Delhi-based artist revs up the tempo for the first 2 tracks. Still carrying the expanse of dub and synth chords bouncing around unobtrusively, the opener 'Inner Garden' is one of the more percussive outings under the TDC banner. The rigid drum groove contrasts against the limber harmonic layers, and if there is a hook beyond the repeating bassline, it's in the interplay of analog tom sounds.

Even the succeeding title track gives the drums a more prominent role, as their mercurial echoes provide the only thing tactile in the engulfing yet elusive pumping atmosphere. Only on the final 'Drift' does the pace slow down and the textures get more easily traceable. They step out from the expanse as individual characters evolving noticeably to allow the hypnotic constantness of a bassline looping beyond the rhythmic framework and a mangled vocal sample repeating like a chant. With that, 'Drift' sets itself apart from the more cloud-like nature of the rest of the EP.

Listen to 'MK618' below and follow Tyrell Dub Corp for more information.

MK618 by Tyrell Dub Corp
items._cn_summary: Tyrell Dub Corp 的《MK618》在标准 dub techno 蓝图中注入了更强的节奏张力与实验意图。前两轨加速并突出打击乐层，模拟底鼓与铜管般的合成声部在宽广的空间中交织，模拟 tom 音色与刚性 groove 的对峙形成核心张力。终曲《Drift》放慢步伐，让 bassline 脱离节奏框架循环往复，破碎的人声采样如咒语般重复，令作品从云雾般的氛围中浮现可辨识的线条与人物感。来自新德里艺术家的视角为这一欧洲主导的流派带来边缘地带的文化语境，使其更具跨地域探索价值。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)
