items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items.excerpt: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music.
items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku暌违多年推出的第四张专辑，将北欧传统旋律与巴尔干民间节奏巧妙交织。专辑以保加利亚民间舞曲节奏为灵感创作曲目，融汇马其顿情歌元素，并穿插几首节奏明快的波尔卡，与开篇阴沉低回的短曲形成对比。Niku展现出敏锐的旋律直觉，对夏末光影变幻的捕捉尤为细腻。最动人的部分是末曲——为母亲七十岁生日所作的挽歌，质朴而崇高，加入人声后达到超越性的情感高点。整张作品体现了对故土音乐的深沉热爱与跨国界文化交融的探索，独立发行，源于欧洲非主流音乐地区，是一张真诚而内敛的世界音乐跨界之作。

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body:
Produced by Neek and Jabu's Amos Childs (aka O$VMV$M), Manonmars' third album is syrupy suite of smoke-hazed recollections and free associated reflections set to decelerated, semi-rhythmic bumps, sluggish samples and cloudy drones. Sturdy biz FFO Ka, MIKE, King Vision Ultra or Coby Sey.

Manonmars' 2018 debut is one of those albums we still go back to periodically. It's that rare meeting of minds: a space for O$VMV$M to flex their production muscle and a scratchpad for London-based MC, painter and photographer Jack Martyn Richardson to sketch out his vision of England. And his experiences and impressions on 'Entertainment System' still feel chewable. "Goddess on my arm and both our phones got no service," he quips on 'Goddess'. "Acid is lysergic, psychedelic rock is Turkish." His rhymes aren't throwaway, they map out an underground that's very recognisable, shadowed by O$VMV$M's tuff, effective soundscapes - beats that reference trip-hop, ambient music, exotica and '70s movie soundtracks as much as they do US rap. On opener 'Flam3throw3r', Mars raps in double-time over shrill horns that blot out any trace of a beat; Neek and Childs sound as if they're relishing the negative space, adding chic sword swipes to a track that's got little else to do with the Wu Tang Clan. And even when a lumbering beat kicks in on 'Decathlon', flipping from downtempo to no-tempo in the final act, it sounds as if it's just there to assert O$VMV$M's commitment to slowness - Mars doesn't even seem to notice, rhyming casually but never losing his internal flow.

On 'Nasyua', his slurred expressions duck and weave around industrial whirrs and animalistic groans. "There was a time when I had flaws now I've adapted," he slurs. "I hit the zoot like Steve Zissou in 'The Life Aquatic' / then I dashed it, Christian Bale in a facemask on some Bat shit." Bristol mainstays Franco Franco and Dali de Saint Paul turn up to assist on 'Volcanic Shield', one of the album's most conventional bangers, led by O$VMV$M's skittering Surf Gang-like beats and morse code blips, and cold light's Birthmark lends his voice to 'Infinite', going bar for bar with Mars over Neek and Childs' soupy slackened funk. These moments are when 'Entertainment System' really shines, blaring out like an old tape on a busted in-car audio system. 'Firewater' takes the same approach, leaving Mars to do his best as snares are reformed into splashes alongside sultry stabs and sax from Brum-based sound artist Lorenzo Prati. "My bitch white, she can scuba dive and ice climb," he spits. "Put the drink down, I wasn't in my right mind." It's music that laughs through the tears - what could be more British than that?

items._cn_summary: ManonMars第三张专辑由制作人O$VMV$M（Neek与Jabu的Amos Childs）操刀，呈现出烟雾弥漫的减速氛围。制作上采样trip-hop、ambient、exotica与七十年代电影配乐元素，节奏常在downtempo与no-tempo之间摆动，大量留白与负空间构成阴郁音景。MC Jack Martyn Richardson的歌词绘制英国地下图景，押韵松散却内部流畅，配乐中工业嗡鸣、剑击声、saxophone、摩斯密码采样交织。Bristol与Birmingham客串艺人点缀部分曲目，整体声响如老旧车载磁带般嘶哑破碎。专辑在抽象嘻哈与实验电子之间游走，具备一定的实验制作意识，但整体仍以说唱为骨架，未深入触及自由爵士或学院派即兴领域，与用户偏好的实验爵士、前卫电子融合方向存在一定距离。

items.body:
Bristol’s leading bassbin drivers indulge their passion for a spectrum of speedy UKG to US ghettotech style & pattern at 140-150BPM as BAGS INC.

"Bristol's Sam Binga & Addison Groove have been friends and collaborators since their 2013 'BS3' EP, released on Modeselektor's '50 Weapons' imprint. This project, the third full-length on Binga’s Pineapple Records, is born from an intense 72-hour session at the legendary Devon Analogue Studios, where the pair were able to explore their mutual love of uptempo machine funk - whether that be Detroit Jit, Chicago Boxjams or Turbo Electro.

Three days of intense creativity across classic drum machines, vintage analogue synths and rare hardware effects resulted in a collection of raw but powerful audio building blocks - and over the past two years, the pair have been gradually shaping them into what is now a complete project - the BAGS INC album. Across 12 tracks, Binga & Addison explore that exciting space between 140 and 150 bpm - but while it's fast, it's not 'hard'; as you'd expect from the creators, it's still got that wiggle, and the all-important cheekiness for which they're known."
items._genre: UK bass / ghettotech / juke / footwork / machine funk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是布里斯托两位低音制作人Sam Binga与Addison Groove在Devon Analogue Studios经过72小时密集创作的结果。两人自2013年合作EP以来持续探索140至150BPM速度区间的音乐可能性，素材涵盖底特律Jit、芝加哥Boxjams与Turbo Electro等美式快节奏机器放克风格。12首作品依托经典鼓机、老式模拟合成器与稀有硬件效果器构建，以两年的时间逐步雕琢成型。整张专辑保持着高速节奏的同时并未走向硬派路线，而是延续了创作者标志性的律动摆荡感与俏皮气质，将英式UKG节奏框架与美式ghettotech传统进行了有机结合。

items.body:
Gilberto Gil’s debut album Louvação originally released in 1967 on Philips Records.

"Arriving on the eve of Tropicalismo, the record places Gil’s guitar at the center of rich arrangements by Carlos Monteiro de Souza, Dori Caymmi, and Leonardo Bruno. Blending samba, bossa nova, carnival traditions, and Northeastern Brazilian rhythms, the album explores social, political, and religious themes. The title track “Louvação,” co-written with Torquato Neto, calls for collective awareness, while “A Rua” carries a bittersweet nostalgic tone. Gil’s deep connection to Bahia flows through “Beira-Mar” (with Caetano Veloso), and his poetic imagination shines in “Lunik 9,” reflecting on the space race. “Ensaio Geral” captures the political energy of carnival, while “Rancho da Rosa Encarnada” (with Torquato Neto and Geraldo Vandré) evokes traditional festivities. Highlights include the rhythmically inventive “Roda,” the celebratory “Viramundo” (with Capinan), and the nostalgic “Água de Meninos.” The romantic “Maria (Me Perdoe, Maria)” offers a moment of intimacy, while “Procissão” closes the album with a powerful reflection on faith and society."

items._cn_summary: 这是吉尔伯托·吉尔1967年发行的首张专辑，诞生于热带主义运动前夕。以吉他为核心，编曲由卡洛斯·蒙特罗、德奥利·凯米和莱昂纳多·布鲁诺共同完成，将桑巴、波萨诺瓦、嘉年华传统与巴西东北部节奏融为一体。曲目涵盖社会、政治与宗教主题，与托尔夸托·内图合作的标题曲呼吁集体意识，《A Rua》带有怀旧色彩。与卡耶塔诺·维洛索合作的《Beira-Mar》展现巴伊亚地方风情，《Lunik 9》以太空竞赛为隐喻展开诗化想象。《Ensaio Geral》捕捉嘉年华的政治能量，《Procissão》则以信仰与社会为收束。作为热带主义前奏之作，它为吉尔后续的实验转向奠定了根基。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录七首低保真福音冥想之作，在Shuggie Otis与Otis G. Johnson之间的精神气质中寻找平衡点。Lynn Marshall的假声录音充满飘忽与脆弱感，原始的录音质感赋予作品一种粗糙的真实。制作人Norman Marcelle以Lowery风味的管风琴音色与原始鼓机程序构建节奏骨架，整体呈现出1980年代家庭录音特有的粗粝感。专辑并非追求精致打磨，而是以lo-fi美学捕捉福音音乐中的恍惚与虔诚。Brooklyn的厂牌Private Mind Garden与芝加哥的Numero Group为其提供了地下发行的语境，适合对复古低保真灵魂乐与实验性福音美学感兴趣的听众。

items.body:
On part 4 of 6 tapes documenting his legendary all-night set at The White Hotel, Tom Boogizm goes innnnnnn on the UKF/ballroom/Jersey club/Detroit techno axis for 90 mins of cantering, bucking, pendulous and slamming pressure.

Unleashing another sliver of his 10 hour set recorded during The White Hotel’s reopening weekend, summer ’21, this one depicts the artist also known as Rat Heart deep in his DJ flow, edging from 130BPM upwards across 90 mins of pure pressure in ceaseless swang and drive, initially simmering on a UKF tip that only gets ruggeder, screwing off into kwaito, electro-house, ballroom and Jersey club buck on the front.

Turn it over for a masterclass in Manchester’s take on a key touchstone, Detroit techno; lacing bustling, polyrhythmic zingers, UR anthems, and tracky tools to febrile effect, keen-as-mustard on the FX and always edging on the next, teasing transition. 

Hopefully parts 5 and 6 land before TWH closes in 6 months. rip!

items._cn_summary: 本张专辑是Tom Boogizm在White Hotel演出十小时DJ set的第四部分录制，呈现90分钟持续高能的混音过程。整体节奏从130BPM起步，逐渐向上攀升，前半段围绕UK funky风格展开，融入kwaito、electro-house、ballroom和Jersey club等俱乐部音乐的跳动律动。后半段翻面则专注于底特律techno的演绎，使用多层次打击节奏、UR系经典曲目和功能性工具曲，频繁运用效果器处理，营造出高密度的紧张感。整张作品记录了DJ在数小时set中保持流动状态的真实过程，段落间的衔接与情绪递进是核心聆听价值，对于热衷地下俱乐部混音与多种城市舞曲交汇的听众而言是一次完整的状态呈现。

items._cn_summary: Devin Townsend 的这张专辑酝酿多年，是一部野心宏大的概念作品，以完整管弦乐编制呈现戏剧化的摇滚歌剧。制作规模庞大，舞台感强烈，乐手在专辑中融入了大量古典管弦乐元素和歌剧式的人声演绎。然而评论者认为专辑在摇滚与古典之间的平衡不够理想，音乐本身偏向歌剧化，古典配器的比重盖过了摇滚成分，使得听感上起伏不一。评论者承认这一工程的庞大规模和作者的创作热情，但表示个人不会反复聆听这张专辑。整体而言，这是一张以制作规模见长、音乐张力不够均衡的概念专辑。

items.body: Review by BBKron — This 2nd album from Albion provides more dynamic symphonic progressive folk, mixing in traditionalIrish and Celtic themes with elements of Symphonic Prog and metal. Beautiful melodies and vocals,great arrangements and instrumental prowess. This album leans even more into the folkier aspectsthan the first album, with more acoustic work and the use of heavier guitar riffs limited to just acouple tracks. Their prominent use of flute and prog folk arrangements invites inevitable comparisonwith Jethro Tull, and although there are similarities Albion has their own unique sound and style.Although this album doesn't quite reach the heights of their fantastic debut, Lakesongs of Elbid(2024), it is a great follow-up and most worthy successor, with great songs and dynamicinstrumentation. A special treat for those that crave a mix of folk and Prog. Best Tracks: Eldest,Down with The Hero, Calan Mai, She is the River, Cherry Hill. Rating: 4 stars
items._genre: progressive folk / symphonic prog / Celtic folk
items._cn_summary: 这是 Albion 乐队的第二张专辑，以凯尔特与爱尔兰传统民谣主题为底色，融合交响前卫摇滚与金属元素。长笛与民谣编排占据主导位置，辅以部分较重的吉他段落，整体编排具有动态变化，器乐演奏展现出扎实功底，旋律与演唱俱佳。评论指出作品与 Jethro Tull 存在明显相似性，但乐队已逐步形成自身的辨识度。与首张专辑相比，本作更偏向民谣化与原声化取向，acoustic 比重明显提升。推荐曲目包括 Eldest、Down with The Hero、Calan Mai 等。整体而言，这是一张在民谣与前卫摇滚交界处探索的作品，对同时喜爱两类风格的听众具有吸引力，但与传统民谣和纯前卫摇滚之间的距离同样存在。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是融合多种早期音乐风格的第五张作品。乐队使用手风琴、班卓琴、曼陀林、萨克斯、单簧管、口琴、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他等多种乐器，重新诠释上世纪二三十年代的老唱片素材，涵盖bal-musette、拉格泰姆、jug band、法语香颂、skiffle等类型。二十七首短曲以法语念唱式人声为主，包含向已故法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的曲目，以及对《烟雾迷眼》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典曲目的改编。评论将其与同样风格杂糅的Dan Hicks & his Hot Licks相提并论，强调其对遗失音乐风格的严谨复活态度。

items._cn_summary: 这是一期RootsWorld Radio的节目推介，主题为'Racing into the Big Muddy'，聚焦河流与沼泽意象的音乐内容。节目收录了二十余位艺术家的作品，横跨美国根源音乐、非洲传统、巴西音乐、北欧民谣、希腊与亚美尼亚器乐融合等多个领域。选曲涵盖Dr John、Steve Earle、Johnny Cash等主流民谣歌手，同时也包括Jake Blount、Klakki、Iduema Quartet等更具实验色彩的世界音乐演奏者。从编排来看，节目试图通过地理与文化多样性构建跨文化听觉体验，以河流与沼泽为线索串联不同地域的传统声响。整体偏向广播节目播放清单而非深度乐评，缺乏对具体音乐技法的讨论与艺术性分析，信息层次较为表浅。世界音乐与跨文化融合的选曲方向与学院派爵士及电子音乐品味存在一定距离，但其中包含的非西方传统元素仍具有探索价值。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述实录。25位参与者年龄从17岁到67岁不等，许多人是临时被吸引加入，讲述他们与暴力直接相关的亲身经历。录制地点选在南城一位94岁祖母家的前廊，背景声完全来自现场环境——包括蚊虫声、机场降落路径下的噪音，以及街头游荡的野狗。专辑没有添加任何配乐，仅保留即兴说唱和原始人声。该项目记录了芝加哥被遗忘角落的居民真实生活状况，所有收益将捐赠给Cure Violence Global组织。这是一份社会声音文献，具有田野录音与纪实性质，但作为音乐评论的核心信息较为有限。

items.body:
A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared, seemingly from nowhere.
From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music
opened a window on something so many didn�t even know existed to show that country music had never been a white preserve. That album was a few years before the Carolina Chocolate Drops burst on the scene, reclaiming the Black heritage in country and string band music, plus a great deal more.
Genuine Negro Jig
, their third release, saw them move up to the prestigious Nonesuch label, a powerful artistic imprimatur, winning them a Grammy for an album very far removed from the mainstream.
items.label: Nonesuch
items._genre: folk / string band / roots music / black country
items._cn_summary: 该专辑聚焦于复兴黑人乡村音乐与弦乐乐队传统，承接了此前合辑对乡村音乐黑人根源的揭示。乐队签约知名独立厂牌Nonesuch后发行此作，将被主流叙事边缘化的非裔美国人音乐文化遗产重新呈现在当代听众面前。专辑涉及班卓琴、提琴等传统弦乐器演奏，以弦乐乐队编制为基础展开创作。他们获得了格莱美奖项认可，表明这种根植于传统但被遗忘的音乐分支仍具有当代艺术价值。整体而言，这是一张以传统复兴为导向的根音乐作品，在文化视野上具有独特意义。

items._cn_summary: 这是西班牙吉他手 Dani Jané 的第三张专辑，融合了弗拉门戈、加泰罗尼亚民谣、古典音乐、爵士及探戈等多种元素。Jané 毕业于巴塞罗那 Liceu 高等音乐学院，并曾在西班牙、德国、法国、意大利及印度深造，跨文化背景深厚。专辑核心由吉他、长笛、打击乐及人声构成，作品多与他的个人经历相关：柏林求学期间创作的古典组曲、向祖父致敬的朗巴、致敬故乡卡恩菲内斯特雷斯（Can Finestres）的米隆加，以及受 Toti Soler 影响的探戈斯曲。整体呈现出新一代加泰罗尼亚学院派艺术家的视角，将弗拉门戈视为多元影响中的一种，编排精致但实验性和前卫程度有限。

items.body: Review by jcdude — After going on a 4 year bender of prog discovery I thought I had skimmed all there was to skim of the great classic albums. Each time I start to get comfortable with the thought that I have found all there is to find from the classic era another gem twinkles amongst the rocky substrate and catches my eye. The opening track I could never be a soldier caught me entirely by surprise. At first I found the intensity of the lead singer's voice to be a bit overwhelming and forced. However, as the song progressed and the theme and emotion required to convey it became clear, I found the vocalist more relatable when placed in the context of the times. This album has everything a lover of classic and heavy prog could want. I'm still absorbing my first listen but I already know this is going to be an album I come back to again and again for years to come.
items._genre: eclectic prog / heavy prog / classic prog
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1972年的经典前卫摇滚专辑，开篇曲《I Could Never Be A Soldier》以高强度的人声切入，初期可能让听者感到压迫，但随歌曲推进，主唱的情感表达与时代背景逐渐融合，显示出表演的合理性。整张专辑被评价为兼具经典前卫与厚重前卫的元素，适合反复聆听。不过评论本身较为简短，主要传达了初次聆听的惊喜感，对专辑具体的器乐编排、结构创新或跨界融合缺乏深入分析。作为Eclectic Prog类型的作品，它与用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士、电子融合等方向有一定距离，更偏向传统摇滚框架内的前卫探索。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — From what I understand, 32 Mars is still from the recording sessions that gave Masq and Chevrons. And indeed, we're still psychedelic-inducing flying in the troposphere, though not via a Hammond, but a Farsifa organ. This "album" is only 23 minutes long (I wouldn't have complained if it was 32 instead ;-)))))Clearly the album's centerpiece is off-centered since it opens the festivities: the lear-12-mins 32 Mars is a trip right through the controls of the heart of the sun. The rest of the short album is of the same ilk, though all three short tracks offer badly recorded vocals and returning themes. Clearly this release rehashed ideas, because those three tracks are reworks (alternate versions, if you wish) of the title tracks of their previous releases.Suffering from the same amateurish shortcomings as their previous releases, I'd never really fallen for this album, hence only my 2026 review.

items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的迷幻太空摇滚专辑延续了乐队前作的录音素材，时长仅23分钟。标题曲32 Mars长达12分钟，构成本作核心，以Farsifa风琴替代Hammond，营造出穿越对流层的迷幻氛围。其余三首短曲均为前作主打曲的重新混录版本，主题重复且人声录音质量欠佳。整体呈现出业余制作的特点，缺乏新意，主要是对先前素材的再利用，未能带来新鲜的听觉冲击。作为迷幻与太空摇滚领域的早期作品，其音乐理念具有一定的时代探索性，但在创新性和完成度上存在明显短板。

items.body:
Numero unearths another lost emo gem here, scraping together short-lived Delaware band Eldritch Anisette's complete recordings: a single 7" and a few additional DAT recordings that have never before seen the light of day.

Saddled with a mouthful of a name that spliced H.P. Lovecraft with French Sambuca for some reason, Eldritch Anisette only lasted a year but they did something a little different. The band sprung up from Delaware's tiny punk scene, that was gathered around Railhed drummer Nick Rotundo's Clay Creek Recording Studio. Calling themselves The Enoch Collective, the group of teens and twentysomethings shares tunes and organized cheap shows, eventually forming a sequence of different outfits. Eldritch Anisette was fronted by Clevinger's Courtney Miller and rounded out by local screamo outfit Network 34's Marc Krupanski and Tim Nichols and guitarist Allen Hitchens. And it's their fusion of influences that set them apart; Miller was driven by her interest in The Sundays and Tori Amos, while the rest of the band were circling the local punk fringe.

They played around a dozen shows, spending $100 on a session at Clay Creek and recording six tracks, three of which made it to their only release. And although the band splintered in 1997 just after the 7" appeared, their tracks are oddly resonant - edgier and weirder than most of the emo we've heard from that same period. Miller is clearly the secret weapon and it's her voice - and her charisma - that gives these songs, even the long-buried additional sessions, their bite.
items._cn_summary: Numero厂牌重新发掘了特拉华州短命乐队Eldritch Anisette的全部录音，将一张7寸单曲与几段从未面世的DAT录音合辑出版。乐队源于当地由Clay Creek录音室串联起的Enoch Collective场景，成员来自周边朋克圈子。前主唱Courtney Miller受The Sundays与Tori Amos影响，其余成员则浸染于本地硬核朋克氛围，这种碰撞使作品比同期多数emo更为尖锐与怪僻。Miller的嗓音被视为核心亮点，为这些简短粗粝的录制赋予了辨识度。专辑记录了一支仅存在一年、演出约十余场的小乐队在1990年代中期留下的声响碎片，对研究地下emo历史的听众具有一定档案价值。

items.body:
Brooklyn's Frances Chang foreshadows her third album with an EP of brittle and baroque bedroom pop. RIYL Wendy Eisenberg, Julia Holter or Cate Le Bon.

With 'been thinking bout confession' on the horizon, Chang teases a few of the key tracks, including the charming piano led 'I can feel the waves', that's maybe the most obvious line in to the whole record. Chang wrote the album on an old baby grand in her Sunset Park apartment, and that's the first sound we hear, before it's broken up by clattering drum machine samples, oddball strings and Chang's soft, effective vocals. Her songs are deceptively simple, sounding like insider's outsider music - packed out with earworms but disrupted by unusual production choices and intricate orchestrations.
items._cn_summary: 布鲁克林创作人Frances Chang以这首EP为即将发行的第三张专辑预热，作品定位为精致脆弱的卧室流行，带有巴洛克式的装饰感。她在Sunset Park公寓的旧三角钢琴上完成了整张专辑的创作，开篇的钢琴音色随即被杂乱的鼓机采样、怪趣的弦乐编排和柔软的人声打断。歌曲表面听来平易近人，藏有朗朗上口的旋律线条，但制作上的反常选择与复杂的管弦乐编排不断打破预期，形成一种局外人式的独立质感。整体风格更接近独立流行的抒情表达，与实验、前卫或电子等方向关联较弱。

items.body:
Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep, by seasoned music writer Lauren Martin.

"At the cusp of a new millennium, British electronic music was rapidly changing. Jungle and garage had broken into the mainstream, but were running out of creative gas – what fresh movement would next captivate the underground? On the outer edges of London, a small group of bass lovers had the answer. Through a new strain of subloaded beats that stripped jungle, rave, techno and garage for parts, this scene returned to the dub roots, prizing the fundamentals of soundsystem culture: bass, space and togetherness. They called it dubstep.

In Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep, Lauren Martin charts the origins of one of the 21st century’s most innovative music genres in an oral history format. Through the testimonies of its architects and an immersive array of photography, flyers and unseen scene history, Aftershock chronicles the rise of artists like Skream, Mala, Coki, Loefah, Horsepower Productions and Rusko, as well as labels and parties such as Hyperdub, Tempa, DMZ, FWD>> and Skull Disco.

Together, this movement shook the British underground, exploded onto the internet and, within a decade, had rocked global music at unprecedented scale. Through first-hand storytelling, Aftershock is a testament to how the imagination and persistence of a few can transform culture."

items._cn_summary: 这是一本关于dubstep音乐的口述历史书籍，并非音乐专辑的乐评。内容介绍了Lauren Martin撰写的《Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep》，追溯了21世纪初英国伦敦地下场景中dubstep的诞生与发展，涵盖Skream、Mala、Coki、Loefah等核心艺术家，以及Hyperdub、DMZ、FWD>>等标志性厂牌与派对。书籍采用口述史形式，辅以照片、传单等珍贵史料，讲述bass音乐如何从伦敦地下蔓延至全球网络文化。然而从用户偏好来看，dubstep作为bass music的一种较为商业化的分支，虽然与电子音乐有交集，但偏离实验前卫、自由即兴、暗潮等核心兴趣领域，融合度和创新性有限。Velocity Press虽为独立小众出版社，但此书内容偏向音乐史文献而非声音艺术实验。

items.body:
Oxfam launches label/campaign No More Radio Silence with a collaborative release featuring artists from Palestine, DRC and South Sudan.

"Artist Espoir Dekin features on our upcoming music track ‘(No More) Radio Silence’, bringing together artists connected to DRC, Palestine and Sudan, blending Afro/Arab hip-hop, industrial electronic music and spoken word into a powerful act of solidarity. Espoir uses his music to tell a story that millions of people living through conflict still face. At eight years old, he fled conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), travelling through Angola, Turkey and Greece before eventually settling in the UK."
items._genre: afro/arab hip-hop / industrial electronic / spoken word
items._cn_summary: 该专辑由乐施会发起的'No More Radio Silence'厂牌及倡议推出，汇聚来自刚果民主共和国、巴勒斯坦和南苏丹的艺术家，以协作形式完成一首融合非洲与阿拉伯嘻哈、工业电子音乐及口述诗的跨界作品。参与艺术家Espoir Dekin八岁时因刚果冲突逃离，辗转安哥拉、土耳其、希腊，最终定居英国，作品以个人流散经历承载冲突地区的集体叙事。该项目将音乐作为团结与发声的媒介，在风格层面触及工业电子与嘻哈的交汇地带，并融入口述传统，具有一定的跨界意识与社会语境。然而，原始内容更接近新闻稿性质，对音乐本体——编曲结构、声音设计、制作水准——缺乏实质性描述，信息量极为有限，无法对其艺术质量作出深入判断。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于专辑《Feathered Creatures》的乐评片段，介绍其作为吉他与西塔琴融合的合奏作品。文中提到九首曲目、总时长约四十分钟，由GroundUP Music发行，被描述为'充满奇思妙想且具有感染力'。文章正文极度简短，约为新闻摘要或转载性质，缺乏具体的音乐分析、演奏细节、创新性讨论或艺术价值评估等实质性乐评内容。从风格描述来看，融合了印度西塔琴与爵士吉他元素，属于世界融合爵士范畴，与用户偏好的实验前卫、自由即兴、电子实验等方向有一定距离。该专辑的厂牌GroundUP Music由Snarky Puppy成员创建，属于相对小众的独立厂牌，但文章本身信息量严重不足，无法进行深入的审美或创新性判断。

items.body: Review by BBKron — Interesting album from Muse, and a bold step forward relative to their other recent releases.Strange mix of styles and tracks, but with some real standouts. Although the album has somewhat of aspace-age theme with the title reference and some more spacey synths and such, there are also plentyof gothic stylings with cathedral organ, choirs, and dark theatrical flair, their compelling dramapop, as well as some pure pop and dance tracks. But the two standout tracks are straight-up rockers,Cryogen and The Sickness in You, with heavy guitar and killer riffs and groove. It's a bit all overthe pace stylistically, with some real ups and downs, but overall, surprisingly good and a promisingreturn from the band. Best Tracks: Cryogen, The Sickness in You, Hush, Unravelling. Rating: 3.5stars
items._genre: progressive rock / pop rock / alternative rock / space rock
items._cn_summary: Muse 的这张专辑在风格上呈现出杂糅的特征：太空主题的合成器音色与哥特式的管风琴、合唱团交织，融合了戏剧化的流行曲式以及纯流行和舞曲作品。其中两首突出曲目回归了硬摇滚路线，以厚重吉他和强劲律动为核心。尽管整体方向显得摇摆不定，时有亮点亦有低谷，但作为乐队近期创作中较为大胆的一次尝试，仍展现出回归质朴摇滚根基的潜力。专辑被评价为风格跨度大、起伏明显，却出人意料地具有可听性。

items.body: Review by BBKron — 2nd album from this exciting young Prog band from Tacoma, Washington featuring, an enticing mix ofsymphonic prog, melodic rock, metal elements, and sophisticated vocal arrangements, as well asdashes of classical, jazz, pop, and soft rock. Beautiful melodies and vocals punctuated with drivingrock and metal make a heady blend. However, in some places, the metal elements seem to be workingagainst or even undermining the vocal melodies, and a lighter touch would be preferred, such as onParadise and Tidal Lock. But the full potential of the band is realized on the fantastic epic-lengthtitle track (24 min.), where the band eases back on the metal aspects and lets their great vocals,melodies, songwriting, and instrumental prowess shine, showcasing numerous different styles to greatsuccess. Shows great promise, and with this album, the band is just on the brink of greatness. BestTracks: Hollow Drift, The Shadow, Voice of a Stranger. Rating: 4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / symphonic prog / melodic rock / soft rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自华盛顿塔科马的一支年轻前卫金属乐队，是其第二张全长作品。乐评描述其融合了交响前卫、旋律摇滚、金属元素以及古典、爵士、流行和软摇滚等多种风格，旋律与人声编排精致。乐队在多数曲目中倾向于较重的金属质感，部分评论者认为这反而干扰了人声旋律的表现力，建议在某些段落采用更轻盈的处理。专辑的同名长篇作品（24分钟）被认为是最能展现乐队潜力的时刻，金属成分退居次要，让人声、旋律和器乐实力充分发挥，展示了多种风格的综合能力。整体而言，乐评认为这支乐队已展现出良好前景，但仍处于突破的临界点。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Every House We Built by Exploring Birdsong is a very creative blend of progressive rock & metal, with neo prog and pop that results in some very unique sounds and compositions. The trio do not have any guitars, other than bass, and the melodies are created with nice synth and piano textures. The most interesting aspect of the band's production comes from the rhythm section, with the distorted bass and loud drums very much eclipsing and improving upon the heavy aspect, more so than most djent bands could dream of. Lynsey Ward's beautiful vocals shine forth with great multi layered harmonies and some great creative melodies and lyrics, giving a rather Fleetwood Mac meets Kate Bush vibe to the project's overall sound. While there is alot of genre interplay throughout, it's a fantastic debut album with alot of future potential. The real stand out track to me is Spy In The House Of Love, with fantastic crossover appeal. If Taylor Swift released it, it would be a massive hit. I'd give this a mid 8 out of 10.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / art pop / neo prog
items._cn_summary: EXPLORING BIRDSONG的首张专辑《Every House We Built》以三人编制挑战了前卫摇滚的常规配置——没有吉他，仅依靠贝斯、合成器与钢琴构建旋律。失真贝斯与响亮鼓点构成节奏核心，重量感甚至超越许多djent乐队。Lynsey Ward的人声层次丰富，带有Fleetwood Mac与Kate Bush式的抒情气质，和声与歌词创作是专辑亮点。多类型融合贯穿始终，但在创新性上偏向对既有元素的优雅重组，而非真正的声音实验。专辑在小众圈内获得好评，曲目《Spy In The House Of Love》被认为具有出圈潜力。整体而言，这是一张制作精良、旋律悦耳的前卫跨界作品，但在实验深度和冒险精神上较为克制，更接近精致流行框架内的前卫点缀，而非真正意义上的实验性表达。

items.body: Wie die letzten Jahre aussahen? Isaiah Rashad antwortet mit einem Albumtitel: It’s Been Awful thematisiert, wo der Rapper zuletzt war – am Boden, in den Tiefen seiner eigenen Gefühlswelt, kopflos in einem leeren Raum, wie es bereits das Frontcover suggeriert. Und sonst so? Ach, immer derselbe Mist. So heißt nicht zufällig einer der Höhepunkte der Platte: »Same Sh!t«. Dort zählt Rashad Substanzen, Geld und Routinen auf; der Refrain bringt es auf die Formel »It’s the same shit«. Auf dem Album klingt das tatsächlich genauso, wie es sich liest: wie die erschöpfte Bestandsaufnahme eines Mannes, bei dem sich dringend etwas ändern muss. Nicht falsch verstehen: It’s Been Awful klingt gut. Doch Rashad sucht hörbar nach Auswegen aus den Sackgassen, in denen er sich festgefahren hat. Von Anfang an gehörte er zu den selbstreflektiertesten und emotional offensten Künstlern im Kader von Top Dawg Entertainment. Auch auf It’s Been Awful kreisen seine Texte um mentale Probleme – und um den Wunsch, ihnen zu entkommen. Mit Drogenmissbrauch und suizidalen Tendenzen hatte Rashad bereits in jungen Jahren zu kämpfen. Doch obwohl er diese Probleme auf It’s Been Awful erneut anerkennen muss, verliert er die positiven Seiten des Lebens nicht aus dem Blick. In einem Skit wird er aufgefordert, drei Dinge zu nennen, für die er dankbar ist. Seine Antwort: die Freiheit, das tun zu können, was er möchte. Also eine schwebende, sphärische Jazz-Rap-Platte mit viel Tiefe und Charakter.
items._cn_summary: 这是Isaiah Rashad在经历个人低谷后推出的回归专辑。整张作品以自省为核心，围绕药物滥用、心理困境与求生欲望展开。专辑开篇即暗示创作者身处情感深渊，歌词反复清点金钱、物质与日常循环，构成一种疲惫的自我审视。Rashad并未沉溺于绝望，而是在中段穿插感恩skit，以对自由的珍视作为救赎支点。制作层面采用漂浮的球形爵士嘻哈风格，层次丰富，氛围感强烈，与词作中追求出路的主题相互呼应。专辑既是对创伤的承认，也是对改变的渴望，整体呈现出一位成熟创作者在困境中寻找出口的过程。

items.body: Two of dark electronic music’s most commanding forces are joining together for a fall run across North America. Buzz Kull and Kontravoid will bring their body-lit blend of darkwave, EBM, electro, and synth-pop to clubs and festivals beginning September 10 in Austin, with dates stretching through Texas, the South, the East Coast, Canada, the Midwest, the Pacific Northwest, and California. Five of those shows — in Spokane, Vancouver, Seattle, Portland, and Sacramento — will be shared with Spike Hellis and Normal Bias. The pairing feels inevitable. Both artists have carved out distinct territories in the fogged-out corners of modern dark music: Buzz Kull with a severe, cinematic pulse that turns anxiety into motion, and Kontravoid with a masked, strobe-lit mystique that sharpened into dancefloor discipline. See the full list of dates below. Buzz Kull is the solo project of Sydney-based musician and producer Marc Dwyer. Since 2012, Buzz Kull has been blending elements of darkwave, EBM, and synth-pop into a sound that is dark, dissonant, and danceable. His early work, including his 2017 debut Chroma and 2018’s New Kind of Cross, was defined by stripped-back production and a fascination with minimal synth textures. These records drew from early industrial and post-punk traditions, pairing drum machine-led tracks with cool, monotonous vocals and moody atmospherics. Over time, Dwyer’s sound has grown harder and more precise. His 2022 album Fascination, released through Italian label Avant! Records, marked a turning point: a sleek, focused collection of dark dance tracks that channel the energy of late-’80s body music. In 2026, Buzz Kull returned with Deep Hate, a four-song statement of intent: relentless, cinematic, and charged with nocturnal electricity. The release marks some of Buzz Kull’s most focused and ferocious work to date, a document of emotional clarity and mechanical pulse. Outside of Buzz Kull, Dwyer is a frequent collaborator and remixer, working with artists across the darker ends of electronic music. He has toured extensively throughout Europe, the United States, Latin America, and Asia, sharing stages with contemporaries like Cold Cave, Boy Harsher, Kontravoid, and Spike Hellis. Buzz Kull’s latest release is Deep Hate, out now via Heartworm Press. Watch the latest official video, “Human Force,” below. Kontravoid’s masked mystique has remained intact for over a decade. Ever since the release of his self-titled LP in 2012, Canadian-born, Los Angeles-based Cameron Findlay has perfected a strain of dark pop that teeters between EBM, electro, and goth. His productions, such as 2019’s “Too Deep” and 2021’s “Faceless,” dive into the most derelict corners of foggy, strobe-lit clubs: there is no choice but to dance. Still, beneath the harsh pulse, there is an uncanny softness and a clear songwriting instinct. Kontravoid’s work carries a capacity for heart-wrenching melody, with songs that are both captivating and drenched in melancholy. 2018’s “Undone,” released on Berlin’s Fleisch Records, has remained a fan favorite since its arrival. Onstage, Kontravoid demands the audience’s attention with a powerful performance that balances harsh beats with signature bassline-driven rhythmic patterns. He has toured with Boy Harsher, ADULT., Drab Majesty, and Hide, and has remixed artists including Schwefelgelb and Kris Baha. Truly a man of the shadows, Kontravoid remains an unparalleled fixture in the dark electronic arena. Kontravoid’s latest release is the 2026 single “Mortal,” out via Artoffact Records. Watch the video “For What It Is” below. Buzz Kull and Kontravoid 2026 Tour Dates Thu, Sept 10 — Austin, TX @ Levitation / Elysium Fri, Sept 11 — Houston, TX @ Barbarella Sat, Sept 12 — New Orleans, LA @ Santos Sun, Sept 13 — Atlanta, GA @ The Earl Tue, Sept 15 — Tampa, FL @ The Orpheum Wed, Sept 16 — Orlando, FL @ Will’s Pub Fri, Sept 18 — Baltimore, MD @ Metro Gallery Sat, Sept 19 — Philadelphia, PA @ Nikki Lopez Sun, Sept 20 — Brooklyn, NY — tickets onsale in late July Tue, Sept 22 — Montreal, QC @ Foufounes Électriques Thu, Sept 24 — Toronto, ON @ Cafeteria Fri, Sept 25 — Pittsburgh, PA @ Funhouse at Mr. Smalls Sat, Sept 26 — Milwaukee, WI @ Anodyne Coffee Roasting Co. items.body:
Since everyone else has written something about the centennials of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, why not join the parade? It is a good opportunity to look at the timeline of bassists the legendary trumpeter and saxophonist used. Born just under four months apart, the pair worked together under the elder Davis’ name periodically between Fall 1955 and Spring 1957 before a more steady affiliation in 1958-1960.

It is in that latter period that this analysis will begin, as it gives a convenient bit of serendipity: the fact that two of the their most famed albums were made in that period, Davis’ Kind Blue (March 2nd and April 22nd, 1959 for Columbia) and Coltrane’s Giant Steps (May 4th–5th and December 2nd, 1959). And the analysis will end with Coltrane’s death in 1967, which came during the tenure of Davis’ “second great quintet” and before his groups swelled and electrified during his fusion period.

As such, we begin with the same man, the bassist on both those albums: Paul Chambers. He had taken up the bass a decade earlier in his adopted home of Detroit (where he was a student at the seminal Cass Technical High School ... more on that later). He arrived in New York in 1954 at 19. By the time of Kind of Blue and Giant Steps, he had been on over 100 sessions from dozens of leaders, with multiple dates under Davis (with whom he had started working in late 1955) and Coltrane (who had used him for several albums in 1957-58 as well as both fellow sideman for many others and Chambers also hiring Coltrane for his own sessions). In addition to the five albums he led, Chambers played on sessions for Benny Golson, Curtis Fuller, J.J. Johnson, Lee Morgan, Red Garland, Sonny Clark, and Sonny Rollins.

The collaboration between Davis and Chambers was remarkably fruitful before and after Kind of Blue and solidified a part of Davis’ music that had previously seen widely differing players like Tommy Potter, Oscar Pettiford, Al McKibbon, and Percy Heath. The rest of 1959 saw multiple engagements around the country and closed with recordings that would be part of another monumental record, Sketches of Spain, that paired Davis’ group with the Gil Evans Orchestra. 1960 continued that momentum with more Sketches of Spain recording and almost non-stop touring, including two stretches in Europe, from Spring onward. 1961 and 1962 had more of the same activity, the documents being Someday My Prince Will Come and Quiet Nights. Then, quite suddenly, Chambers left Davis’ group in early February 1963.

It should be stated that Chambers did not restrict his activities solely to Davis, recording over four dozen albums during the period with, among many others, Jackie McLean, Wynton Kelly, Benny Golson, Hank Mobley, and Curtis Fuller. And after leaving Davis, he worked steadily with an array of leaders through the end of 1968, sadly passing away from tuberculosis caused and/or aggravated by drug abuse at only 33.

Stepping right into the Davis group was another Cass Technical High School alumnus: Ron Carter. Nearly 26, Carter was already prophesying his prolific career, participating in over three dozen albums since 1960, with the likes of Charli Persip, Yusef Lateef, Eric Dolphy, Don Ellis, Coleman Hawkins, Cecil Payne, Jaki Byard, Wes Montgomery, Bobby Timmons, Tadd Dameron, Dizzy Reece, Ken McIntyre, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson and others, plus waxing his leader debut, Where?, for Prestige subsidiary New Jazz in 1961.

It was Carter’s arrival that heralded Davis’ soon-to-be seminal band, though it took until Fall 1964 for its personnel to solidify. With Carter, Davis recorded Seven Steps To Heaven and played the Antibes festival in 1963. What is interesting though is while the “second great quintet” is thought of as a monolith, the bass chair had some upheaval/fluidity, depending on how you look at it. Gary Peacock – already a veteran and likely the only person to work for both Bud Shank and Albert Ayler – took the chair for nearly six weeks in the spring of 1964, Carter returning thereafter through the end of the year. 1965 began auspiciously with the January recording of E.S.P. but then things derailed with a convalescing Davis unable to play. And when he could, in November and December, Carter, a hot commodity, was absent, spelled by Peacock once more, then Reggie Workman, who had come up around the same time as Carter and had already come and gone in the groups of Coltrane. In 1966, Carter would return to the group but only partially, participating in East Coast performances, shows elsewhere having either Richard Davis, Carter’s only real equal in terms of fecundity, or in the Peacock mold of eclecticism, Eddie Gomez, returning permanently in October, just before the album Miles Smiles. 1967 was similar: Carter was on board when not busy elsewhere, Gomez on call, then Albert Stinson for one show (a little over two years before his passing – see Bass Tragedies column in Issue 94) and then another veteran, Buster Williams, for a tour (and playing on one track of the 1981-released compilation album Directions). Carter would fill a fixed point for all of 1967, including the albums Sorcerer and Nefertiti and would continue with Davis through the middle of 1968.

Like Chambers or perhaps even more so, Carter was also on the greater jazz scene during his tenure with Davis. He recorded on sessions led by his fellow Davis bandmates but also by everyone from Bobby Timmons, Charles Lloyd, Donald Byrd and Bobby Hutcherson to Jimmy Smith, Shirley Scott, Eddie Harris, and Stanley Turrentine, to name only a handful. He has, of course, gone on to be likely the most recorded bassist in jazz history.

Paul Chambers’ time under Coltrane was shorter and more intermittent. After Giant Steps he was part of, along with the rest of Davis’ period band, November 1959 recordings that would partly comprise Coltrane Jazz and be brought back 18 months later as one of three individual bassists taking part in the Africa/Brass recordings (though his contribution was only heard on the 1995 complete sessions version).

Also in 1959 was a Birdland engagement for Coltrane where either Ahmed Abdul-Malik or George Tucker, both established and close in age to Coltrane, were on bass.

In 1960 Coltrane hired the slightly younger Steve Davis in what seems to be his first professional engagement. Davis stayed in the band through the end of the year for all its live dates and played on music recorded in October and released piecemeal on My Favorite Things, Coltrane Jazz, Coltrane Plays the Blues, and Coltrane’s Sound. Though Davis lived until 1987, his credits after Coltrane were slight: the Mangione Brothers, Dave Burns, McCoy Tyner, Kenny Dorham, James Moody, Freddie McCoy, and Eddie Jefferson, all made in the ‘60s. One deviation in the year came via Coltrane’s shared date with Don Cherry, The Avant-Garde, where bass was handled by either Charlie Haden or Percy Heath.

1961 was a year in flux, bassist-wise, for Coltrane. He introduced a concept to which he would return later in the decade by using two bassists for an engagement at Chicago’s Sutherland Lounge in March: Raphael Don Garrett and Workman, the former, about six years younger, working with Roland Kirk, Paul Serrano, and Eddie Harris, the latter 11 years younger, sideman for Gigi Gryce, Donald Byrd, Duke Jordan, Richard Williams, and Dave Pike.

Workman would be part of the aforementioned Africa/Brass, as would, separately, another bassist, Art Davis, already with credits under Max Roach, Lee Morgan, Booker Little, Hal Mooney, Ernestine Anderson, Dizzy Gillespie, Leo Wright, Clifford Jordan/Sonny Red, Abbey Lincoln, and Booker Little. But in May they were together for Ole Coltrane and nearly a month at the Village Vanguard in August. Workman would become the fixed bassist for Coltrane through the end of the year for concerts, including a European tour, and a small portion of the Ballads album from the end of the year. An exception was Workman either alternating or alongside Jimmy Garrison for a November stint at the Village Vanguard.

If not for a family health crisis forcing Workman to leave the group at the end of 1961 and return to his native Philadelphia, he likely would have stayed with the band and jazz history been quite different. It should be said that Workman hardly is a footnote, becoming one of the most revered players of his generation. But it was Garrison who became the anchor. Born between Garrett and Workman, prior to joining Coltrane he had worked with Philly Joe Jones, Curtis Fuller, Kenny Dorham, Jackie McLean, JR Montrose, Walter Bishop, Jr., Ornette Coleman, Bill Barron, and Ted Curson.

Unlike Carter and Davis, once Garrison was on board, he stayed there. That was mostly to do with Coltrane’s packed schedule of touring and albums and that, unlike Davis, he was healthy and non-combustible. From 1962-1964, Garrison was omnipresent, including the bulk of Ballads, Duke Ellington & John Coltrane (where he split duties with Ellington’s period bassist Aaron Bell), 2018 discovery Both Directions At Once, John Coltrane And Johnny Hartman, Impressions, Crescent, another new millennium unearthed gem in Blue World, and closing out the year with Coltrane’s magnum opus A Love Supreme (which added Art Davis for a second day of recording, released as a second disc to the album’s deluxe edition in 2002).

In 1965 Garrison was still the main man but occasionally Davis would be alongside him: partially on The John Coltrane Quartet Plays in February and fully for June’s Ascension. Otherwise, Garrison was the sole bassist for performances and most of the other albums: Transition, Sun Ship, and Meditations. The exceptions without Davis were overdubs of Haden for the posthumously released Infinity and Garrett returning to play both bass and clarinet for Live In Seattle (as well as the 2021 archival release A Love Supreme: Live In Seattle), Om, and part of Kulu Se Mama.

1966 was even more Garrison-centric, with the only documented work including a second bassist shows in November and December with Lionel “Sonny” Johnson, the brother of Dewey Johnson, who had played on Ascension. The last year of Coltrane’s life, Garrison was there as well, with one notable absence: the Coltrane/Rashied Ali duet Interstellar Space.

Unlike Chambers or Carter, Garrison was kept so busy during his time with Coltrane that his outside discography at the time is meager, though it does include his sole leader date, Illumination! with the Elvin Jones/Jimmy Garrison Sextet. Otherwise it was sessions with Lorez Alexandria, Coltrane bandmate McCoy Tyner, Sonny Rollins, Bill Dixon, and Robert F. Pozar.

After Coltrane’s death, Garrison kept working but his documentation slowed, his two Blue Note dates with the Jones trio rounded out by Joe Farrell being the most enduring. There were also dates with Rolf and Joachim Kuhn, Clifford Thornton and Nathan Davis, and regular work with Alice Coltrane and Archie Shepp. His final recording came in early 1975 with Beaver Harris and Dave Burrell’s 360 Degree Music Experience. Garrison died of lung cancer in 1976 at 42.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Tchaikovsky’s Concert Fantasy remains a concert-hall rarity. Its unusual structure stems from the composer’s reputed dislike of blending piano and orchestral sonorities: to avoid that clash, Tchaikovsky kept the forces largely separate, devoting most of the first movement to a massive, unaccompanied solo cadenza. Beyond a shared key of G major, the piece evokes the character of his Second Piano Concerto, with an unfailing optimism expressed through bravado and a pronounced balletic grace. Wanderer Fantasy Amazon Presto Apple The flute section of the Sinfonieorchester St. Gallen, under Modestas Pitrėnas, projects that elegance with a rounded, mellow tone. What drives the Quasi Rondo is the dynamic interplay between instruments: the brass adds a martial edge while the strings bridge lyricism, gaiety, and virtuosity. Pianist Lukas Geniušas commands the movement’s expansive cadenza with fearless assurance. He avoids empty showmanship; his fortes project real power, and every flourish serves a musical purpose. He is equally at home in the quieter writing, shading finely graded piano dynamics and finding a delicate, bell-like touch where the music calls for it. The second movement, Contrastes, lives up to its name, moving through an eclectic array of musical personalities. It opens with an intimate, passionate duo for piano and cello, and it is the sharp juxtaposition of its episodes that lends the reading its volatility. Liszt was only eleven when Schubert composed the original solo version of the Wanderer Fantasy, yet he returned to the work across his life, arranging it several times, most notably here for piano and orchestra (S. 366). Rather than reinvent the piece, Liszt scores it to bring out its thematic transformations, and the result sounds entirely natural in an ensemble setting. In the Allegro con fuoco (track 3), the strings open up an expansive dimension absent from the solo original. Geniušas plays with evident restraint here, a marked shift from the thunderous dynamics he unleashed in the Tchaikovsky. The choice mostly convinces, though a few climaxes could take more weight. Lukas Geniušas (© Jean-Baptiste Millot) In the Adagio, Liszt leaves the material largely untouched until the halfway mark, giving the solo piano room to carry the movement’s gravitas. Geniušas delivers introspective chords that, however gently played, register with real weight, and the cello’s entry in the major-key section is a striking touch that eases the full ensemble back in. The Presto sets piano and woodwinds together to amplify the score’s sprightly humor, both sides alert to each other’s articulation and dynamics. The strings add buoyant touches before turning into an unapologetic, driving force as the music intensifies. Liszt’s transcription works because he knows when to leave the music alone: the large fugue that opens the final Allegro is impressive enough on solo piano and needs little intervention. Geniušas’s account may lack the thrilling urgency of Alexandre Kantorow’s recording of the solo version, but it holds the same authoritative character that made his Tchaikovsky so compelling. With the soloist’s presence firmly set, the ensemble’s entry a minute later enhances Schubert’s textures rather than robbing the piano of prominence, and it lands the extra punch the closing pages need. Lyala Kandaurova’s liner notes add welcome historical and musical context, and the engineering gives piano and orchestra equal standing. This is a rewarding release, and one worth returning to. 1975年、神奈川県横須賀市生まれ。早稲田大学第一文学部卒業後、2000年よりベルリン在住。著書に『明子のピアノ』（岩波ブックレット）、監修を務めた『おとうさんのポス... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る ベルリン・ドイツ交響楽団は、アマチュア音楽家が誰でも参加できるフラッシュモブ形式の演奏会「シンフォニック・モブ」を毎年開催している。6月20日、ポツダム広場のソニーセンターで行われた今年の公演に、次期首席指揮者の山田和樹が登場した。 この「シンフォニック・モブ」は、いまでは他の場所でも行われているが、2014年のベルリン・ドイツ響が発祥。今回はオーケストラと合唱を合わせて総勢800人ほどが参加したという。この5月、東京芸術劇場で水野修孝の超大曲《交響的変容》を指揮して反響を呼んだ山田に、ベルリン市民を巻き込んでの野外公演を初めて指揮する意気込みを聞いた。 「いまの時代、こうして人が実際に集まってなにかをやるということ自体に意義を感じています。セキュリティや規制でとかく人が集まりにくい世の中ですが、それを超えて、ポジティヴなエネルギーを生み出せるのは音楽の特別なところだと思います。人が集まる力が戦争など悪いほうへではなく、よいほうへ向かう……。大作曲家たちもきっとそういう思いで名曲を書いてきたはずです」 15時半の開演に合わせて行くと、山田とオーケストラ、合唱がモーツァルト「レクイエム」から「怒りの日」、ビゼー「《アルルの女》組曲」の〈ファランドール〉などを演奏していた。フラッシュモブをもじった「シンフォニック・モブ」だが、ただ突然集まるイヴェントではなく、事前に楽譜を配布し、応募したアマチュア奏者・合唱がプロと一緒に演奏を作り上げる仕組みである。Tシャツ姿で指揮する山田とアマチュア音楽家の共演を聴きながら、ポジティヴなエネルギーが伝わってきた。 危機一髪！ペトレンコ指揮ベルリン・フィルのヴァルトビューネ公演 ヴァルトビューネの舞台から。キリル・ペトレンコ（右）とヨナス・カウフマン（中央） ©Bettina Stoess 6月は野外公演が盛んになる季節である。その代表格であるベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団のヴァルトビューネ公演は、気候変動時代の野外コンサートの難しさを感じさせる一夜となった。 開催日の6月27日の週末は、最高気温38〜40度というベルリンでは超異例となる酷暑の予報が出ていた。そのため、主催者側は持ち込める水の量を増やし、現地でも飲み水を無料で補充できるようにするなど、聴衆に配慮をした。しかし、それでも筆者が会場入りした18時半の時点で38度。森の谷に座る観客が、持参した扇子や紙を一斉にあおる光景はかつて見たことがない。 そんななかでも、ベルリン・フィルは長袖の黒服で臨み、キリル・ペトレンコの指揮も、ヨナス・カウフマンの歌唱も、じつに研ぎ澄まされたもの。ようやく少し気温も下がってきて、後半への期待が高まろうとしていた。 しかし、レスピーギ《ローマの噴水》が終わった直後、楽団インテンダントのアンドレア・ツィーチュマンがマイクを持って現れた。「天候悪化の予報が出ており、20分の休憩時間を5分に短縮させてもらいたい」という内容だった。嫌な予感は現実のものとなる。プログラム最後のレスピーギ《ローマの松》の第1曲が終わった静かな箇所で、雷が光ったのだ。このころから退出する人の姿が目立ち始める。雷がそう遠くない場所で光る度に、もしここで激しい雷雨に襲われた場合、逃げ場のない2万人の聴衆はどうなるのだろうと想像をして、いささか怖くなった。 こんな状況でも、ペトレンコとベルリン・フィルの集中力は途切れることがない。〈ジャニコロの丘〉のクラリネット・ソロのたっぷりとした歌、そして〈アッピア街道の松〉でのたたみかけるような演奏は圧巻だ。最高潮に盛り上がり、カウフマンがアンコールで《カタリ・カタリ》を歌った直後、マイクを持って聴衆に呼びかけた。 「雷雨が近づいています。安全上の理由から、残念ながらこれ以上公演を続けられません。《ベルリンの風》は、どうか帰る支度をしながらお聴きください！」 ひょっとしたら恒例の《ベルリンの風》を演奏しないのではという不安をもった直後だっただけに、安堵が混じり合った喝采が起きる。そして終演後、筆者がバスに乗り込んだわずか数分後に、大雨が降り始めたのだった。20分の休憩時間を5分に短縮した主催者の判断は正しかった。と同時に、一昔前は想像もしなかった酷暑の野外コンサートの難しさに、ドイツでさえ直面しつつあるのを肌で感じた。

items.body:
Green Gartside and co’s addictively sugary turning point album crops up for a masterclass in blue-eyed soul styles.

Upon its release in 1985, ‘Cupid & Psyche 85’ marked a radical leap for the once squat dwelling communists from new wave dreamers to chart-worthy pop pucker. Prior to this record they had markedly political and philosophical leanings set to a mix of almost folksy whims, disco and reggae lite, as found on a handful of Rough Trade releases, but with ‘Cupid & Psyche 85’ they mounted a sly assault on the charts, drawing on Green Gartside’s love of Aretha Franklin’s aching soul for a far more polished sound that would parallel the likes of Prefab Sprout’s entry to the US billboard charts.

In many ways its not hard to draw lines between Gartside and the Sprout’s Paddy McAloon; both are reclusive genius types who saw the other side of the pop machine and disliked it, and both made some of the ‘80s greatest power moves, as Scritti Politti did with the likes of ‘Absolute,’ which now uncannily reminds us of trotting around Co-Op during early lockdown (it was on their in-store radio A-list), and the natty funk of ‘Wood Beez,’ their seminal prayer for Aretha Franklin, which is coincidentally co-produced by Arif Mardin.
items._cn_summary: 这张1985年发行的专辑是Scritti Politti从早期新民谣、迪斯科与雷鬼风格向精致流行转型的里程碑。制作人Arif Mardin参与制作，将Green Gartside对Aretha Franklin灵魂乐的热爱融入到打磨光滑的合成器流行框架中。《Absolute》与《Wood Beez》等曲目展示了natty funk的律动质感，与同时期的Prefab Sprout在美国的商业路径相似。虽然乐评提到了从政治性独立厂牌到榜单流行的转变过程，但对于追求实验、前卫、爵士、电子或暗潮等音乐的听众而言，这张专辑本质上是主流蓝眼灵魂与合成器流行的产物，制作精良但缺乏实验性突破，与用户口味匹配度较低。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自捷克布拉格乐队的续作专辑，以六十余分钟的概念专辑形式展开，由多组短曲组成套曲结构。音乐将前卫摇滚元素与经典摇滚、强力流行乐融合，形成复杂但易入耳的旋律性前卫声响。评论将其与尼尔·莫尔斯、Styx、Kansas以及更前卫的Toto相提并论，强调其旋律性与可听性的平衡。整张专辑呈现出工整的曲式编排和清晰的器乐架构，听感上接近七十年代美式前卫摇滚传统的延续而非突破。亮点曲目包括《A Fool's Errand》《Mind Speaker Suite》《Constant Silver Lining套曲》以及《The Syncretist》。评论给出三星半评价，认为作品有效且愉悦，但并未展现前卫音乐应有的实验锋芒，更偏向传统旋律性前卫摇滚范畴。

items.body: Review by BBKron — This first full-length album, following two fantastic EPs, The Thing With Feathers (2019) andDancing in the Face of Danger (2023), shows the full potential of this wonderful UK Prog triofronted by the dynamic keyboards and great vocals of Lynsey Ward, and ably supported by Jonny Knight(bass) and Matt Harrison (drums). Bringing a modern pop sound into their Prog landscapes, they blendmultiple genres from dreamy pop to heavy prog to create their unique sound and style. Often movingfrom plaintive piano phrases to an immersive wall of soaring vocals, keyboards, bass and thunderingdrums, while maintaining a strong melodic sense amidst rhythmic intensity, they deliver bold anddynamic tracks, quite proggy, yet still fit somewhat within the pop world. items._cn_summary: 英国三人乐团Exploring Birdsong的首张全长专辑，在前卫摇滚框架中注入现代流行元素。键盘手兼主唱Lynsey Ward负责主要的旋律与声乐构建，节奏组以贝斯与鼓为基础支撑。作品在钢琴独白段落与厚重声墙之间频繁切换，融合梦幻流行与重型前卫两端，保留了流行歌曲的旋律感与可听性，同时具备一定的前卫复杂性。从结构上看，曲目多以多段落交替为核心，抒情主题与力度对比形成张力，但整体仍偏向流行化的呈现方式，与深度实验性音乐存在一定距离，适合喜欢跨界作品的乐迷。

items.body: Review by BBKron — 4th solo album from founding member, vocalist, multi-instrumentalist, and primary songwriter for the Pineapple Thief, Bruce Soord. It is dark, moody, and atmospheric. Yes, somewhat melancholic, but with shimmering arrangements and instrumentation, and Soord's wonderful vocals. It is like all the quieter, gentler, brooding parts of Pineapple Thief maintained throughout the whole album, but without the heavier outbursts and more rockin' elements, which in some cases really seems missing here, and is what keeps this album from reaching the heights of the Pineapple Thief albums. Still, very good, with some great guitar, instrumental sections, and melodic moments throughout. The slow, sustained atmosphere is cool, but sounds a bit too much the same from song to song. But, if you are in the right mood for this, it is very effective and beautiful. Best Tracks: Day of Wrath, Ghosts in the Park, Our Predicament, Kept Me Thinking. Rating: 3.5 stars
items._cn_summary: 这是Pineapple Thief主创Bruce Soord的第四张个人专辑，整体风格阴暗、忧郁且氛围感强烈。专辑延续了乐队作品中较为安静、内省的部分，但去掉了更重型的摇滚段落，以闪亮的编曲和精致的器乐演奏为主打，吉他段落尤为出彩。Soord的人声在专辑中占据重要位置，成为情感表达的核心载体。慢速且持续的氛围贯穿全作，但也被指出在各曲之间略显雷同，缺乏足够的变化与起伏。最佳曲目包括《Day of Wrath》《Ghosts in the Park》《Our Predicament》《Kept Me Thinking》，在合适的心境下聆听能展现其感染力。作为跨界前卫摇滚作品，氛围营造扎实但缺少实验性突破。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the early prog revival bands that swept Sweden during the 1990s, the Malm� based A.C.T.started out as the rather quirky Fairyland before adopting its acronym inspired moniker that doesn'tseem to refer to anything. A band known for its eclectic melodic prog meets pop workouts and stilloperates in the modern era, A.C.T. unleashed its debut release TODAY'S REPORT at the cusp of a newmillennium in 1999 and featured aspects of symphonic prog, jazz, metal and power pop. The album wassort of a new beginning for the band with several new members joining at the cusp of releasing thefirst album.TODAY'S REPORT features ten tracks including the multi-suite closer "Personalities" which entanglesseven distinct movements. The band liberated its full sound on this debut with a crafty mix of superprogified instrumental moves including heavy guitar riffing and symphonic accoutrements along withcrafty angular time signature workouts that alternated with rather instantly catchy if not a tadcheesy at times, melodic pop constructs. Generally the band navigates these turbulent fields quitewell by manufacturing labyrinthine journeys throughout fairly demanding musical terrain. This teamof five adopts the crafty symphonic moves of Yes and the saccharine pop moves of Supertramp only setto a more metallic power pop excess.The opening "Abandoned World" pulls out all the A.C.T. tricks and trinkets and ushers the band intothe prog revival scene with a bang which contributed to Sweden and Scandinavia's dominance of modernprog ever since. While the tracks tend to be stuffed with proggy outbursts that will satisfy themost hardened prog stalwart, the tunes themselves are actually quite accessible inspired more by theworld of neo-prog and crossover prog acts rather than the more eclectic nerdy compositions of themost demanding bands on the market. In general this is a good thing for those seeking the moremelodic side of prog that happens to incorporate a lot of the prog moves that essentially define thegenre. Unfortunately this comes off as a bit cheesy at times as if Styx was trying to emulate KingCrimson without sacrificing the radio friendly arena rock.Overall it's not a bad debut with even lead vocalist Herman Saming delivering beautiful vocalcontributions as well as a tight-knit band that somehow skirts the territory between catchy angst-driven 90s alternative rock and 70s progressive sophistication. This is a very tough high wire actto tackle indeed and i don't think these guys quite nailed it at this point as the pop aspects soundsomething like the quirky new wave of Sparks only performing with a Swancore type of act like ThankYou Scientist! It's a pleasant enough listen for sure but the two diametrically opposing forceshaven't seemed to sufficiently gel at this early stage. For those much more into this style ofmusic, it may ring a bit more triumphant to your ears but for mine it just seems a bit forced on theprog side of things to ratchet up the band's credentials without incorporating the song structuresto support the weight of it all.3.5 rounded down
items._genre: eclectic prog / melodic rock / pop rock
items._cn_summary: A.C.T.乐队1999年发行的首张专辑将交响前卫摇滚与流行摇滚相融合，借鉴Yes的交响编制与Supertramp的甜美旋律，整体偏向新前卫和跨界流行路线。评论指出乐队在复杂编曲与朗朗上口的流行元素之间寻求平衡，但这两者尚未充分融合，作品有时显得做作且过于商业化。主唱Herman Saming的声线表现突出，乐队技术扎实，但'前卫'与'流行'的对立力量在首张专辑中未能形成统一。对于追求实验性、先锋性或非主流融合的听众而言，这张专辑的亲和力与新派前卫定位距离较远。

items.body: Review by BBKron — This exciting Heavy Prog band from Salt lake City, Utah, made a big splash with their previousalbum, A Cell to Call Home (2023), which was absolutely fantastic. What was so great about this bandand that album in particular was the great (and delicate) balance and mix between the heavy (metal)elements, classic melodic rock, and lighter more acoustic melodies and vocals. Just a fantasticblend that was unlike any other band. With this ambitious new album, they have again createdsomething special, but they have also disrupted that wonderful blend by moving in a much heavierdirection. The album is still very good, but the heavy elements dominate now, even including theaddition of some extreme growling vocals. To be sure, there are still some beautiful melodic momentsand great vocals, but these are fleeting, much less prominent, and are overpowered by the onslaughtof heavy guitar throughout most tracks. That great balance has been lost and their sound now fitsmore closely with what other prog metal bands are doing, albeit some very good prog metal. Thus,although still quite good, this album was a disappointment for me, as I was really looking forwardto some similar magic to what they created on the last album. To me, none of the songs here are asgood as anything from the last album, although there are many fine moments. Best Tracks: Past LifeParable, Patience, Gravity I. Rating: 3.5 stars
items._genre: heavy prog / progressive metal / melodic rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自犹他州盐湖城的重前卫乐队，是其2023年专辑《A Cell to Call Home》之后的续作。上一张作品在重金属元素、经典旋律摇滚与轻柔原声段落之间取得了精妙平衡，而新作明显偏向更厚重的吉他音墙，甚至加入了极端咆哮人声，导致原有那种独特的多元融合被打破，旋律段落变得稀少且转瞬即逝。整体仍属精良的前卫金属制作，器乐编排扎实，旋律段落依然偶有闪现，但乐队已从独树一帜的风格滑向与同类前卫金属乐队趋同的方向。对于偏爱旋律与轻盈质感交替的听众而言，这是一次令人惋惜的转向；而对于纯粹的前卫金属爱好者，制作水准依然在标准线之上。

items.body: Review by BBKron — 8th album from this US Heavy Prog band that has really developed from their early days of psych-rockand stoner metal into a premier heavy Prog band. Their previous album, Innate Passage (2022) was oneof the best of the year, and they just keep going from there. A great Prog sound that is atmosphericand complex, but also quite heavy at times (without indulging metal cliches) while also maintaininga spirited rockin' groove, kind of like a heavier, harder-rocking Pink Floyd. Their constantlymoving rhythm section with interweaving keyboard lines keeps the tempo brisk and energetic,providing the perfect foundation for the guitar riffs laid on top, which is also surprisingly brightand uplifting. Great collaborative instrumental work that meshes together well throughout, effectivevocals, and quite melodic and atmospheric despite the heaviness. It all works extremely well onmultiple levels. All the tracks are great (6 songs, each 6-11 min), but the album really takes offfrom the title track on offering an exhilarating album experience. Best Tracks: Through Zero,Strata, Sight Unseen, Blighted Age. Rating: 4.5 stars

items._cn_summary: 这是美国重前卫摇滚乐队ELDER的第八张录音室专辑。乐队从早期的迷幻摇滚与石人金属风格，发展为成熟的重前卫摇滚乐队。专辑以大气而复杂的声场为基底，在保持厚重音墙的同时维持明快的律动，键盘线条与不断推进的节奏组交织，为吉他 riff 提供支点。整体被描述为一种更重、更有力气的Pink Floyd式的声音。器乐协作紧密，人声有效，虽然沉重但旋律与氛围兼具。六首曲目时长均在六至十一分钟之间，自标题曲起进入核心体验。评论者给予4.5星评价。专辑整体偏向传统重摇滚与前卫摇滚的重叠范畴，在实验性、跨类型融合方面较为有限，与用户偏好的实验前卫、自由爵士、电子及暗潮方向距离较大。

items.body: Review by BBKron — The current version of Yes (Steve Howe, Geoff Downes, Billy Sherwood, and Jay Schellen) returns withtheir 2nd album with this lineup (follow-up to 2023's Mirror to the Sky) and 24th album overall, anddelivers a solid album that both honors the past but also tries to move in some new directions. Insome ways this is sort of like Yes-lite, or DAD-Yes, as the songs have a more gentle sound andstyle, less rock, more acoustic and more orchestration, but the songs are generally good, just witha somewhat different mood and feel. Steve Howe's guitar, and especially acoustic guitar work shinesthroughout, as well as various vocals and harmonies, and rich arrangements. Along with the tracksthat try to recapture that Yes sound, there are some departures, such as the more classical andorchestrated Ariadne, the funkier rocker All Hands on Deck, and the fun, poppy Jambustin'. No, thisis not Yes from their classic period, but how could it be? That was 50 years ago. This is a finealbum that shows where the band is today, and it is quite good. Best Tracks: Countermovement, AllHands on Deck, Ariadne, Jambustin', Watching the River Roll. Ratng: 3.5 stars

items._cn_summary: 这是Yes乐队当前阵容的第二张录音室专辑，乐评指出专辑整体偏向柔和、内敛的路线，减少了摇滚力度，增加了原声吉他和管弦乐编配。Steve Howe的吉他演奏尤其是原声部分贯穿始终，配合人声和声与丰富的编曲层次。单曲方面既有尝试回归传统Yes风格的曲目，也有偏向古典管弦化的实验（如Ariadne）、放克摇滚（All Hands on Deck）以及流行化的Jambustin'。乐评承认这张专辑并非乐队经典时期的作品，更多展现了乐队当下的状态。整体来看，专辑是温和的渐进摇滚延续，风格偏主流，与极端实验、前卫爵士或电子领域距离较远。

items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自加拿大乐队的专辑，将经典摇滚、前卫摇滚、放克、布鲁斯、强力流行甚至华丽摇滚等多种元素融合在一起。从乐评描述来看，乐队的创作方式更偏向于将多种主流摇滚类型的历史风格进行杂糅式拼接，参考对象涵盖了披头士、小脸乐队、皇后、坏指头、10cc、冲击合唱团、黑乌鸦等经典摇滚乐队。专辑主打趣味性和熟悉感，强调'既熟悉又独特'的听感。整体定位偏向主流摇滚谱系中的风格混搭，而非实验性或前卫性的探索，制作思路相对传统，注重旋律与编曲的可听性。
